docs.title: Halal-Queue Design System
docs.text:
Version 2.0 · August 2026

A unified design language for the Halal-Queue platform — a halal food and shopping marketplace. Three platform variants share the same brand DNA but are adapted for their respective contexts: Mobile (iOS), Web (merchant portal & storefront), and iPad (split-view customer app).

docs.title: Logo & Identity
docs.text:
• Brand name: Halal-Queue
  • Mark: Shopping bag icon with a gold "Q" monogram and leaf motif
  • Wordmark: Calligraphic script — "Halal" in green, "Queue" in gold
  • Logo file: src/imports/logo-6.jpeg
  • Logo usage: Always on white or very dark backgrounds. Minimum size: 28px height. Never stretch or recolor.

docs.title: List Rows
docs.text:
Structure: [icon 40–42px] [title + subtitle] [right element] [chevron]

docs.title: Skeleton / Loading
docs.text:
All skeleton elements use:

  • Background: --neutral-100 (#F0F2F0)
  • Radius: same as content element
  • Animation: pulse keyframe — opacity 0.5 → 1 → 0.5, 1.5s infinite (implement with CSS or Tailwind animate-pulse)
  • Never use a spinner as the primary loading state for content — use skeleton instead

  • Header: padding: 20px 24px / DM Serif Display 20px title / border-bottom: 1px --neutral-50

docs.title: Mobile (iOS · 390pt)
docs.text:
Structure:

[Status bar — 44px]
[App bar — variable]
[Content — scrollable]
[Bottom tab bar — 80px + safe area]

App bar variants:

  1. Green hero bar — location + notification icon (home screen)
  2. Search bar — back icon + search input + filter button (browse screen)
  3. White detail bar — back button + centered title + action icon (detail screen)

Touch targets: Minimum 44×44pt for all interactive elements.

Scroll behavior: overscroll-behavior: contain on inner scroll areas. No visible scrollbars.

Safe areas: Respect env(safe-area-inset-*) for notch, home indicator, and Dynamic Island.

Status bar: Transparent, content appears above. Text color white on green backgrounds, dark on white.

Home indicator: 120px wide, 5px height, --neutral-300, centered at bottom.

docs.title: iPad (iPadOS · 834pt)
docs.text:
Structure:

[Status bar — 24px]
[Persistent sidebar — 220px] + [Content area — fluid]
  [Top bar — 64px]
  [Content — scrollable]

Layout approach: Sidebar + master-detail within content area. No bottom tab bar.

Split View (master-detail):

  • List pane: 240px fixed within content area
  • Detail pane: fills remaining width
  • List items: 56–60pt min height, selected state with --green-50 bg

Touch targets: 44pt minimum; prefer 48–52pt for primary actions.

Pointer support: Hover states on all interactive elements (cursor: pointer). Tooltips on icon-only buttons.

Sidebar collapse: At narrow multitasking widths (< 400pt), sidebar collapses to icon-only (64pt) or a slide-in overlay.

Grid: 2-column default, 3-column for product grids, 4-column for stat cards. 20px screen padding. 12–16px gap.

docs.title: Web (Desktop · 1280px)
docs.text:
Structure:

[Sidebar — 220px] + [Main area — fluid, max 1280px]
  [Global top bar — 56px]
  [Page header — breadcrumb + title + actions]
  [Section tabs or filters]
  [Content — data tables, grids, forms, charts]

Breakpoints: | Breakpoint | Behavior | |------------|----------| | < 768px | Single column, sidebar becomes overlay drawer | | 768–1024px | Sidebar collapses to icons (64px), 2-col content | | 1024–1280px | Full sidebar, 2–3 col content | | ≥ 1280px | Max-width container centered, full layout |

Hover states: All interactive elements show hover via background tint or color shift. Transition: 0.18s ease.

Focus states: box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(27,92,42,0.3) — visible keyboard focus ring.

Cursor: cursor: pointer on all clickable elements, cursor: not-allowed on disabled.

Scrollbars: Hide by default (scrollbar-width: none), show on hover for data tables.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Requirement Standard How met Text contrast — body 4.5:1 AA --neutral-900 on white = 18:1 ✓ Text contrast — large 3:1 AA --green-900 on white = 7.3:1 ✓ Text contrast — UI 3:1 AA --gold-500 on white = 2.9:1 ⚠ — use only for decorative labels, not critical info Touch targets 44×44pt All mobile/iPad targets enforced at 44pt minimum Focus visible WCAG 2.1 2.4.7 Green ring applied to all focusable elements Color alone WCAG 1.4.1 Status always includes icon or text alongside color Motion WCAG 2.3.3 All transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion

Note on Gold: --gold-500 (#C8A44A) on white is 2.9:1 — below AA for body text. Use gold only for decorative elements (ratings, badges, accents), never for body copy or critical information. Pair with a supporting icon or dark text when conveying meaning.

docs.title: Codebase Architecture & Implementation
docs.text: Halal-Queue is a monorepo consisting of 3 distinct applications, each using technology tailored for its platform. The design tokens below are implemented differently depending on the application's framework.

docs.title: 1. Customer App (Mobile) & Vendor App (iPad)
docs.text:
• Path: apps/customer-app/ and apps/vendor-app/
  • Framework: React Native (Expo)
  • Implementation Rules:
  • Colors are defined in a shared design token theme object (e.g. colors.green900 = '#1B5C2A') or NativeWind Tailwind theme.
  • Shadows use React Native shadow style properties / elevation on Android or NativeWind utility classes.
  • Fonts are loaded using expo-font / @expo-google-fonts.
  • Layouts use Flexbox with React Native View, Text, and virtualized list components.

docs.title: 2. Admin Web (Desktop/Web)
docs.text:
• Path: apps/admin-web/
  • Framework: React (Vite)
  • Responsive Approach: CSS Grid + Flexbox, Tailwind CSS
  • Typography Integration:
  • Fonts can be loaded via @fontsource packages or @import in CSS.
  • Dark Mode Strategy:
  • Applied via data-theme="dark" attribute on <html>.
  • Driven by CSS custom properties. No hardcoded color swaps needed.

docs.title: CSS Custom Properties (Admin Web Only)
docs.text:
Add to :root in src/index.css after Tailwind import:

  /* Brand Green */
  --green-950: #134020;
  --green-900: #1b5c2a;
  --green-700: #246b32;
  --green-600: #2e8040;
  --green-500: #3a9e50;
  --green-200: #c2dfc8;
  --green-100: #e8f4ea;
  --green-50: #f4faf5;
  --green-25: #f8fdf9;

  /* Brand Gold */
  --gold-900: #7a5f1a;
  --gold-700: #a8862c;
  --gold-500: #c8a44a;
  --gold-400: #e2c06a;
  --gold-300: #edd89a;
  --gold-100: #f9f2e1;
  --gold-50: #fefbf3;

  /* Neutrals */
  --neutral-950: #0d120d;

docs.title: Do

• Use --green-900 as the primary action color on all platforms

Halal-Queue Design System · v2.0 · Generated August 2026

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) document significant architectural decisions made during the design and evolution of the Halal-Queue platform.

Each ADR captures:

  • Context
  • Decision
  • Consequences
  • Alternatives considered
  • Status

ADRs provide historical traceability and help future contributors understand why architectural choices were made.

docs.title: ADR Index
docs.text: ADR Title Status ADR-001 Modular Monolith Architecture Accepted ADR-002 NestJS Backend Accepted ADR-003 Flutter Mobile Applications Superseded ADR-004 PostgreSQL Database Accepted ADR-005 Redis & BullMQ Accepted ADR-006 JWT Authentication Accepted ADR-007 S3-Compatible Object Storage Accepted ADR-008 OpenAPI-First API Design Accepted ADR-009 Clean Architecture Accepted ADR-010 Monorepo Structure Accepted ADR-011 React Native Expo Mobile Applications Accepted ADR-012 React & Vite for Admin Web Portal Accepted

docs.title: ADR Lifecycle
docs.text:
Each ADR progresses through one of the following statuses:

  • Proposed
  • Accepted
  • Superseded
  • Deprecated

Accepted ADRs represent the current architecture of the platform.

docs.title: Template
docs.text:
New ADRs should follow the template located in:

docs/templates/adr.md

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform requires rapid development while maintaining clear business boundaries and allowing future growth.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Version 1 shall use a Modular Monolith architecture.

Business capabilities are organized into independent modules:

  • Authentication
  • Vendor Management
  • Catalog
  • Ordering
  • Pickup
  • Notifications
  • Administration

Modules communicate through application services rather than directly accessing each other's persistence layer.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive

  • Simpler deployment
  • Lower operational overhead
  • Easier debugging
  • Shared transactions
  • Clear module boundaries

Negative

  • Single deployment unit
  • Shared runtime
  • Scaling is application-wide

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Traditional layered monolith
  • Microservices
  • Serverless architecture

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The backend requires a framework that supports modularity, dependency injection, validation, testing, and long-term maintainability.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use NestJS as the backend framework.

Key technologies include:

  • TypeScript
  • Express/Fastify
  • Dependency Injection
  • Validation Pipes
  • Guards
  • Interceptors
  • Swagger Integration

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive

  • Strong architecture
  • Excellent testing support
  • OpenAPI integration
  • Modular design

Negative

  • Additional abstraction compared to Express
  • Learning curve for new developers

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Express.js
  • Fastify
  • Spring Boot
  • ASP.NET Core

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-003 Flutter Mobile Applications
docs.text: [!NOTE] Superseded by ADR-011: React Native Expo Mobile Applications. Mobile development has transitioned from Flutter to React Native with Expo.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform requires native-quality mobile applications for customers and vendors while minimizing development effort.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Develop separate Flutter applications for:

  • Customer
  • Vendor

Shared functionality will be extracted into reusable packages.

docs.title: Shared Packages
docs.text:
• shared_api
  • shared_models
  • shared_ui
  • shared_utils

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive

  • High code reuse
  • Native performance
  • Single language
  • Material 3 support

Negative

  • Separate application deployments
  • Shared package version management

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• React Native
  • Native Android & iOS
  • Flutter Web

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Halal-Queue platform requires a reliable transactional database capable of supporting complex business relationships, ACID transactions, and future scalability.

The database must support:

  • User management
  • Vendor management
  • Product catalog
  • Order processing
  • Notifications
  • Reporting

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
PostgreSQL is selected as the primary relational database.

Database schema changes are managed using Flyway migrations.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
PostgreSQL provides:

  • ACID compliance
  • Excellent relational modeling
  • Strong indexing capabilities
  • JSON support
  • Mature ecosystem
  • Excellent performance
  • Open-source licensing

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Excellent data integrity
  • Strong transactional guarantees
  • Mature tooling
  • Extensive community support
  • Easy backup and recovery

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Vertical scaling has limits
  • Requires migration management
  • Operational administration required

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• MySQL
  • MariaDB
  • MongoDB
  • Microsoft SQL Server

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Some business operations should execute asynchronously rather than blocking user requests.

Examples include:

  • Push notifications
  • Email delivery
  • OTP delivery
  • Image processing
  • Report generation

The platform also requires distributed caching.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Redis will be used as the in-memory datastore.

BullMQ will be used for background job processing.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
Redis

  • Cache
  • Session storage (future)
  • Rate limiting
  • Queue backend

BullMQ

  • Job scheduling
  • Background workers
  • Retry policies
  • Delayed jobs

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
Benefits include:

  • Faster response times
  • Improved scalability
  • Reliable retries
  • Queue monitoring
  • Reduced API latency

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Better user experience
  • Improved throughput
  • Reliable background processing
  • Horizontal worker scaling

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Additional infrastructure
  • Queue monitoring required
  • Job failure handling

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• RabbitMQ
  • Apache Kafka
  • Amazon SQS
  • Database-backed queues

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The platform requires secure authentication for:

  • Customers
  • Vendors
  • Administrators

The authentication mechanism must support stateless APIs and mobile applications.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Authentication uses:

  • Phone number
  • Password
  • JWT Access Token
  • Refresh Token

Authorization is implemented using Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

Passwords are hashed using Argon2id.

docs.title: Token Strategy
docs.text:
Access Token

  • Short-lived
  • Sent with every authenticated request

Refresh Token

  • Long-lived
  • Used to obtain new access tokens
  • Can be revoked

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
JWT provides:

  • Stateless authentication
  • Excellent mobile support
  • Horizontal scalability
  • Standardized implementation
  • Broad ecosystem support

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Stateless backend
  • Easy API integration
  • Scalable authentication
  • Standard Bearer authentication

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Token revocation complexity
  • Secure refresh token storage required
  • Token expiration management

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Session cookies
  • OAuth 2.0 only
  • API Keys
  • Basic Authentication

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• HTTPS only
  • Short-lived access tokens
  • Refresh token rotation
  • Secure password hashing
  • Audit authentication events

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Halal-Queue platform stores user-uploaded assets such as:

  • Product images
  • Vendor logos
  • Vendor cover images
  • Customer profile photos

The storage solution must be scalable, secure, highly available, and independent of the application server.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The platform shall use an S3-compatible object storage service.

Supported implementations include:

  • AWS S3
  • MinIO

The application stores only object metadata and URLs in PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
S3-compatible storage provides:

  • Virtually unlimited scalability
  • High durability
  • Secure object access
  • CDN integration
  • Lifecycle management
  • Vendor independence through the S3 API

MinIO enables local development using the same API.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Small application servers
  • Independent storage scaling
  • Easier backups
  • Cloud portability
  • Efficient large file handling

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Additional infrastructure
  • Network latency
  • Object lifecycle management

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Local filesystem
  • PostgreSQL BLOB storage
  • Azure Blob Storage
  • Google Cloud Storage

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Generate unique object keys using UUIDs.
  • Validate MIME types before upload.
  • Store object metadata in PostgreSQL.
  • Never expose storage credentials to clients.
  • Use signed URLs when direct access is required.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The platform exposes REST APIs consumed by:

  • Customer Mobile App
  • Vendor Mobile App
  • Admin Web Portal

A single, authoritative API contract is required to coordinate frontend and backend development.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The project adopts an OpenAPI-First development approach.

All REST APIs shall be designed, reviewed, and approved before implementation.

The OpenAPI specification serves as the authoritative API contract.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
OpenAPI-First provides:

  • Clear API contracts
  • Parallel frontend and backend development
  • Automatic documentation
  • SDK generation
  • Easier testing
  • Reduced integration issues

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Consistent API design
  • Early design reviews
  • Better developer experience
  • Improved documentation quality

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Additional upfront design effort
  • Specification maintenance required

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Code-First API development
  • Documentation after implementation

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
The OpenAPI specification shall include:

  • Paths
  • Schemas
  • Parameters
  • Responses
  • Examples
  • Security Schemes

Changes to the API contract require review before implementation.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The platform is expected to evolve significantly over time while remaining maintainable and testable.

Business logic should remain independent of frameworks and infrastructure.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The backend adopts Clean Architecture principles.

Application modules are organized into distinct layers:

  • Domain
  • Application
  • Infrastructure
  • Presentation

Dependencies point inward toward the domain.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
Clean Architecture provides:

  • High maintainability
  • Independent business logic
  • Improved testability
  • Framework independence
  • Clear separation of concerns

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Easier unit testing
  • Better module isolation
  • Lower coupling
  • Flexible infrastructure replacement

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Additional abstraction
  • More project structure
  • Slight learning curve

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Traditional layered architecture
  • Feature-based architecture
  • Hexagonal architecture

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Business rules shall never depend on:

  • NestJS
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis
  • BullMQ
  • External services

Infrastructure depends on the domain—not the other way around.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Halal-Queue platform consists of multiple applications and shared libraries, including:

  • Customer Mobile App
  • Vendor Mobile App
  • Admin Web Portal
  • Backend API
  • Shared packages
  • Documentation
  • OpenAPI specification

Managing these projects in separate repositories would increase maintenance overhead and complicate dependency management.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The project shall use a monorepo structure.

Applications are organized under apps/, reusable libraries under packages/, and shared documentation under dedicated directories.

Example:

apps/
  backend/
  admin-web/
  customer-mobile/
  vendor-mobile/

packages/
  shared_api/
  shared_models/
  shared_ui/
  shared_utils/

docs/

openapi/

database/

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
A monorepo provides:

  • Centralized version control
  • Easier dependency management
  • Shared tooling
  • Consistent coding standards
  • Simplified CI/CD pipelines

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Easier cross-project changes
  • Improved code sharing
  • Unified documentation
  • Simplified onboarding

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Larger repository
  • More complex CI configuration
  • Requires workspace tooling

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Multiple repositories
  • Git submodules
  • Git subtree

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
The repository uses:

  • npm Workspaces
  • Shared ESLint configuration
  • Shared TypeScript configuration
  • Shared Prettier configuration
  • Shared GitHub Actions workflows

Applications remain independently deployable despite residing in a single repository.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Halal-Queue platform requires native-quality mobile applications for:

  • Customer Mobile App (Android & iOS)
  • Vendor Mobile/Tablet App (iOS/iPad & Android)

Previously, ADR-003 specified Flutter for mobile development. However, to maximize ecosystem cohesion across the platform (where the Admin Portal and full-stack utilities utilize React and TypeScript), align language and skillsets across teams, leverage extensive React libraries and developer tooling, and utilize Expo Application Services (EAS) for streamlined builds, cloud credentials, and over-the-air (OTA) updates, a unified React-based mobile architecture is preferred.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use React Native with Expo (managed workflow with config plugins when required) for developing both:

  1. Customer Mobile Application
  2. Vendor Mobile / iPad Application

Key technical standards include:

  • TypeScript across all application code.
  • Expo Router / React Navigation for declarative, deep-linkable routing.
  • TanStack Query / SWR & Axios/Fetch for REST communication with the NestJS backend.
  • Shared domain models and utilities via monorepo workspace packages (packages/).
  • Native styling and UI primitives using React Native Paper / Tamagui / NativeWind (Tailwind).

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Unified Language & Ecosystem: Full TypeScript stack across Backend (NestJS), Admin Web (React + Vite), and Mobile (React Native Expo).
  • Code Sharing: High reuse of types, validation schemas (Zod), API client code, and formatting utilities between web and mobile apps.
  • Expo Tooling & EAS: Rapid local testing via Expo Go / dev clients, simplified cloud builds for iOS and Android, and OTA update capability.
  • Extensive UI/Component Ecosystem: Access to the vast React community packages and developer tooling.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Native bridges and TurboModules require specific Expo configuration plugins for complex hardware integrations.
  • Performance optimization requires mindful React state management and list virtualization compared to Flutter's compile-to-canvas rendering model.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Flutter (ADR-003): High performance and custom canvas rendering, but introduces Dart as a separate language and siloed tooling from the TypeScript web/backend stack.
  • Native Android & iOS (Swift / Kotlin): Maximizes platform-specific capabilities but doubles engineering overhead and eliminates cross-platform code sharing.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted (Supersedes ADR-003)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Admin Web Portal provides back-office administration, vendor onboarding approval, store catalog oversight, dispute moderation, and operational monitoring for platform operators.

Initial drafts explored Next.js for web portals. However: 1. The Admin Portal is an authenticated Single Page Application (SPA) with zero requirement for public Search Engine Optimization (SEO) or Server-Side Rendering (SSR). 2. SSR in Next.js introduces extra server hosting infrastructure, cold starts, and complex deployment runtime boundaries compared to static assets. 3. Vite provides superior local developer experience with instantaneous Hot Module Replacement (HMR) and optimized Rollup-based production builds.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Develop the Admin Web Portal as a Single Page Application (SPA) using React bundled with Vite.

Key technical standards include:

  • TypeScript with strict mode.
  • Vite for build tooling, local dev server, and asset bundling.
  • Client-Side Routing via React Router / TanStack Router.
  • State & Data Fetching via TanStack Query (React Query) or SWR communicating with the NestJS REST API.
  • Component System: Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI / Radix UI primitives.
  • Hosting: Static distribution via CDN (Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront + S3, or Nginx).

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Simplicity & Performance: Lightning-fast local dev startup and HMR via native ES modules.
  • Deployment Efficiency: Compiles to pure static assets (dist/), deployable anywhere with zero Node.js server overhead and near-zero hosting cost.
  • Reduced Complexity: Eliminates SSR-related hydration mismatches, server actions lifecycle quirks, and node runtime vulnerabilities for internal admin operations.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Initial load includes the JS bundle (mitigated by route-based code splitting with React.lazy).
  • No native SSR capabilities if public storefront capabilities were to be merged into this portal (which are intentionally separated in architecture).

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Next.js: Excellent for public SEO-facing marketing or e-commerce storefronts, but unnecessary complexity and hosting burden for an internal back-office admin portal.
  • Remix: Strong routing and form handling, but requires dedicated server runtimes.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

Business rules defined here must not be inferred, duplicated, or reimplemented differently elsewhere in the repository.

Use this directory to understand:

docs.title: Using Business Documentation
docs.text:
Before implementing or modifying business behavior:

  1. Identify the affected business domain.
  2. Read the relevant document(s).
  3. Inspect the existing implementation.
  4. Follow the documented rules.
  5. Update the relevant documentation when business behavior changes.

docs.title: Source of Truth

Business documentation is authoritative for business behavior.

If business documentation conflicts with implementation:

Do not guess.

Stop and request clarification.

If a requested behavior is not documented and requires a business decision:

Stop and ask before implementing it.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the vision, mission, and strategic direction of Halal-Queue. It serves as the highest-level business document for the project and guides all product, architectural, and engineering decisions.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: To become the leading pickup-first ordering platform for local grocery and fresh food businesses by providing customers with a fast, reliable, and organized ordering experience while enabling vendors to efficiently manage order preparation and pickup operations.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Halal-Queue's mission is to eliminate unnecessary waiting time at local grocery stores by allowing customers to place orders in advance, customize products to their needs, receive real-time order updates, and collect their orders through a secure and convenient pickup process.

At the same time, the platform provides vendors with simple but powerful tools to manage inventory availability, organize incoming orders, reduce operational errors, and improve customer satisfaction.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Many local grocery stores and fresh food vendors still rely on traditional walk-in ordering. During busy periods, this creates several operational challenges:

docs.title: Customer Challenges
docs.text:
• Long waiting times.
  • Crowded stores during peak hours.
  • Uncertainty about product availability.
  • Difficulty placing customized orders.
  • Poor visibility into order preparation status.

docs.title: Vendor Challenges
docs.text:
• Manual order management.
  • High risk of preparation mistakes.
  • Difficulty handling multiple simultaneous orders.
  • Limited communication with customers.
  • No structured pickup verification process.

These problems reduce customer satisfaction and create unnecessary operational inefficiencies.

docs.title: Solution Statement
docs.text:
Halal-Queue provides a digital pickup ordering platform where customers can:

  • Discover nearby vendors.
  • Browse vendor product catalogs.
  • Customize products through predefined options.
  • Place pickup orders in advance.
  • Receive real-time order status updates.
  • Collect completed orders using a secure QR code or pickup code.

Vendors receive a dedicated application that enables them to:

  • Manage product availability.
  • Receive and process incoming orders.
  • Request customer approval for order modifications when necessary.
  • Organize order preparation.
  • Verify customer pickup securely.
  • Manage business hours and temporary closures.

Administrators manage the overall platform, including vendor onboarding, product catalog administration, operational oversight, and system configuration.

docs.title: For Customers
docs.text:
• Save time by ordering before arriving.
  • Avoid long queues.
  • Know the status of every order.
  • Customize products before purchase.
  • Experience a secure and efficient pickup process.

docs.title: For Vendors
docs.text:
• Structured order management.
  • Reduced preparation errors.
  • Better workflow during busy periods.
  • Improved communication with customers.
  • Increased operational efficiency.
  • Better customer experience.

docs.title: For Platform Operators
docs.text:
• Centralized administration.
  • Standardized product catalog.
  • Vendor management tools.
  • Operational reporting.
  • Scalable platform architecture.
  • Foundation for future business expansion.

docs.title: Primary Market
docs.text:
• Halal meat shops.
  • Fish markets.
  • Poultry vendors.
  • Fresh produce stores.
  • Local grocery shops.

docs.title: Secondary Market
docs.text:
The platform architecture is intentionally designed to support future expansion into additional pickup-based businesses, including:

  • Organic food stores.
  • Specialty food retailers.
  • Small supermarkets.
  • Bakery shops.
  • Frozen food retailers.

docs.title: Product Principles
docs.text: Every product decision should align with the following principles:

docs.title: Pickup First
docs.text: The platform is optimized for customer pickup rather than delivery.

docs.title: Simplicity
docs.text: Workflows should be simple for both customers and vendors without sacrificing operational control.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text: Customers and vendors should always have confidence in the current state of an order.

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text: Order progress should remain visible throughout the entire lifecycle.

docs.title: Scalability
docs.text: The platform should support future business growth without requiring major architectural redesign.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Customer information, vendor operations, and order verification must be protected using secure engineering practices.

docs.title: Product Objectives
docs.text:
The initial release (Version 1) aims to achieve the following objectives:

  • Enable customers to place pickup orders digitally.
  • Reduce customer waiting time.
  • Improve vendor order organization.
  • Minimize preparation errors.
  • Standardize pickup verification.
  • Provide administrators with centralized operational control.
  • Establish a scalable platform foundation for future features.

docs.title: Version 1 Scope Summary
docs.text:
Version 1 includes:

  • Customer mobile application.
  • Vendor iPad application (iOS only).
  • Admin web portal.
  • Product catalog management.
  • Product variations.
  • Multiple quantity types.
  • Shopping cart.
  • Pickup ordering.
  • Order modification workflow.
  • Order preparation workflow.
  • QR code and pickup code verification.
  • Push notifications.
  • Business hours.
  • Temporary vendor closures.
  • Automatic daily reset of manually unavailable products.
  • Human-readable order numbers.

docs.title: Future Vision
docs.text:
The platform architecture is intentionally designed to support future capabilities without requiring fundamental redesign.

Potential future capabilities include:

  • Online payment processing.
  • Home delivery.
  • Customer loyalty programs.
  • Promotions and discount campaigns.
  • Product reviews and ratings.
  • Advanced analytics dashboards.
  • ERP and POS integrations.
  • AI-powered demand forecasting.
  • Vendor performance analytics.

These capabilities are outside the scope of Version 1 but are considered during architectural planning.

docs.title: Success Statement
docs.text: Halal-Queue will be considered successful when it enables customers to consistently place and collect orders with minimal waiting while allowing vendors to manage increasing order volumes through efficient digital workflows.

docs.title: Guiding Principle
docs.text:
Every business and engineering decision should answer the following question:

Does this improve the pickup ordering experience for customers while making vendor operations simpler, faster, and more reliable?

If the answer is no, the feature should be reconsidered.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
Version 1 assumes:

  • Vendors prepare orders manually.
  • Customers collect orders in person.
  • Every order belongs to exactly one vendor.
  • Internet connectivity is available during normal operation.
  • Push notifications are available on supported devices.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
Version 1 is constrained by the following decisions:

  • Pickup-only business model.
  • REST API architecture.
  • PostgreSQL database.
  • React Native (Expo) mobile applications.
  • React + Vite Admin Web Portal.
  • NestJS backend.
  • QR code and pickup code verification.
  • Admin-managed vendor onboarding.
  • Single vendor per order.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Version 1 is considered within scope when:

  • Customers can successfully place pickup orders.
  • Vendors can manage and fulfill orders digitally.
  • Administrators can manage vendors and the product catalog.
  • Orders can be verified using QR codes or pickup codes.
  • Push notifications function correctly.
  • Product availability and business hours are enforced.
  • All approved business rules are implemented.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the strategic goals of Halal-Queue. These goals guide product planning, architecture, engineering decisions, and future roadmap prioritization.

Every major feature should contribute to one or more goals defined in this document.

docs.title: Goal Categories
docs.text:
The goals are divided into four categories:

  • Business Goals
  • Customer Goals
  • Vendor Goals
  • Technical Goals

docs.title: BG-001 — Digitalize Pickup Ordering
docs.text: Replace manual and phone-based ordering with a structured digital ordering platform.

docs.title: BG-002 — Reduce Customer Waiting Time
docs.text: Allow customers to place orders before arriving so vendors can prepare them in advance.

docs.title: BG-003 — Increase Vendor Efficiency
docs.text: Provide vendors with tools to manage orders, product availability, and pickup workflows efficiently.

docs.title: BG-004 — Standardize Order Management
docs.text: Ensure all vendors follow a consistent order lifecycle and pickup verification process.

docs.title: BG-005 — Build a Scalable Platform
docs.text: Design the platform so it can support future capabilities without requiring major architectural redesign.

docs.title: CG-001 — Fast Ordering
docs.text: Customers should be able to place an order with minimal effort.

docs.title: CG-002 — Order Transparency
docs.text: Customers should always know the current status of their order.

docs.title: CG-003 — Convenient Pickup
docs.text: Customers should be able to collect orders quickly using a QR code or pickup code.

docs.title: CG-004 — Reliable Product Information
docs.text: Customers should only see products that vendors currently offer.

docs.title: CG-005 — Simple User Experience
docs.text: The application should remain intuitive regardless of future feature additions.

docs.title: VG-001 — Organized Order Queue
docs.text: Provide vendors with a structured workflow for managing incoming orders.

docs.title: VG-002 — Reduce Preparation Errors
docs.text: Allow vendors to review, modify, and confirm customer orders before preparation.

docs.title: VG-003 — Inventory Flexibility
docs.text: Enable vendors to quickly mark products as temporarily unavailable while automatically restoring availability the following day.

docs.title: VG-004 — Business Availability Control
docs.text: Allow vendors to configure weekly business hours and temporary closures with optional customer-facing notices.

docs.title: VG-005 — Faster Customer Handover
docs.text: Reduce pickup time using secure verification methods.

docs.title: TG-001 — Maintainability
docs.text: Use a modular architecture that supports long-term maintenance and extension.

docs.title: TG-002 — Scalability
docs.text: Support increasing numbers of users, vendors, products, and orders without major architectural changes.

docs.title: TG-003 — Reliability
docs.text: Maintain consistent system behavior and data integrity during normal operation.

docs.title: TG-004 — Security
docs.text: Protect customer, vendor, and administrative data using industry-standard security practices.

docs.title: TG-005 — Performance
docs.text: Provide responsive application performance for common user actions.

docs.title: TG-006 — Observability
docs.text: Enable monitoring, logging, and auditing of critical business operations.

docs.title: TG-007 — API-First Development
docs.text: Define and approve API contracts before implementation to ensure consistency across backend and client applications.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
The following metrics will be used to evaluate the success of Version 1.

ID Metric Target SM-001 Customer can complete an order successfully ≥ 95% SM-002 Vendor can process an order without manual intervention ≥ 95% SM-003 Order status updates delivered successfully ≥ 99% SM-004 Pickup verification succeeds on first attempt ≥ 99% SM-005 Platform availability ≥ 99.5% SM-006 Critical API response time < 500 ms (normal load)

These targets are initial engineering goals and may be refined after production usage.

docs.title: Decision Principles
docs.text:
When evaluating new features or architectural changes, use the following priorities:

  1. Improve customer pickup experience.
  2. Simplify vendor operations.
  3. Preserve data integrity.
  4. Maintain system scalability.
  5. Avoid unnecessary complexity.
  6. Ensure long-term maintainability.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Version 1 does not aim to:

  • Compete with full delivery platforms.
  • Replace vendor ERP or POS systems.
  • Support every retail business type.
  • Optimize for complex enterprise workflows.
  • Introduce AI-driven automation.

  • Display only available vendors.
  • Display vendor products.
  • Display product images.
  • Display prices.
  • Display quantity types.
  • Display available variations.
  • Prevent unavailable products from being added to the cart.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Customer successfully adds products to the cart.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Vendor temporarily closed.
  • Product unavailable.
  • Product archived.
  • Network unavailable.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Allow customers to submit a pickup order.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Customer

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
• Cart contains products.
  • All products belong to one vendor.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Customer reviews the cart and submits the order.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Open cart.
  2. Review products.
  3. Enter an optional order note.
  4. Submit order.
  5. Receive confirmation.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Validate the cart.
  • Create a new order.
  • Generate a human-readable order number.
  • Generate a QR code.
  • Generate a pickup code.
  • Notify the vendor.
  • Display order status.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Order status becomes Pending Vendor Review.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Vendor closed during checkout.
  • Product becomes unavailable.
  • Validation fails.
  • Network interruption.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Allow vendors to process customer orders efficiently.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Vendor

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: • New order received.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Vendor reviews the order and decides whether to accept, modify, or reject it.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Open new order.
  2. Review items.
  3. Review order note.
  4. Accept order OR
  5. Request modification OR
  6. Reject order.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Lock the order during processing.
  • Record the decision.
  • Notify the customer.
  • Record audit history.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Order progresses to the next valid state.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Vendor loses connection.
  • Order already processed.
  • System error.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Allow vendors to resolve stock shortages without cancelling the entire order.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Vendor

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: • Order contains unavailable items.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Vendor marks unavailable items and submits a modification request.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Open order.
  2. Select unavailable items.
  3. Mark unavailable quantity.
  4. Submit modification.
  5. Wait for customer response.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Create an Order Revision.
  • Notify customer.
  • Prevent preparation until customer responds.

docs.title: Customer Decision
docs.text:
Customer may:

  • Accept changes.
  • Reject changes.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Accepted modifications become the new order version.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Customer rejects changes.
  • Customer does not respond.
  • Modification expires.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Ensure only the correct customer receives the order.

docs.title: Primary Actors
docs.text:
Customer

Vendor

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: • Order status is Ready for Pickup.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Customer arrives at the store and presents the pickup credential.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
Customer:

  1. Open order.
  2. Show QR code OR
  3. Provide pickup code.

Vendor:

  1. Scan QR OR
  2. Enter pickup code.
  3. Confirm pickup.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Validate QR code.
  • Validate pickup code.
  • Prevent duplicate pickup.
  • Record pickup timestamp.
  • Complete order.
  • Notify customer.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Order status becomes Completed.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Invalid QR.
  • Invalid pickup code.
  • Order already collected.
  • QR expired (future enhancement).

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Allow vendors to manage inventory availability.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Vendor

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: Vendor logged in.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Vendor updates product availability.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Open products.
  2. Select product.
  3. Mark available OR
  4. Mark unavailable.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Update availability.
  • Record audit log.
  • Hide unavailable products.
  • Automatically restore manually unavailable products at the beginning of the next business day.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Availability is updated.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Product archived.
  • Product deleted.
  • Update conflict.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Allow vendors to define operating schedules.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Vendor

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: Vendor logged in.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Vendor configures business hours or temporary closures.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Open business settings.
  2. Configure weekly schedule.
  3. Add temporary closure.
  4. Enter optional closure reason.
  5. Save.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Validate schedule.
  • Publish availability.
  • Prevent ordering while closed.
  • Display closure message to customers.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Business availability reflects the configured schedule.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Invalid schedule.
  • Overlapping closure periods.

docs.title: Business Goal
docs.text: Maintain platform integrity and operational quality.

docs.title: Primary Actor
docs.text: Administrator

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: Administrator authenticated.

docs.title: Business Journey
docs.text: Administrator manages vendors and platform data.

docs.title: User Journey
docs.text:
1. Login.
  2. Review dashboard.
  3. Approve vendors.
  4. Manage categories.
  5. Manage Global Products.
  6. Review audit logs.
  7. Monitor platform activity.

docs.title: System Journey
docs.text:
The system shall:

  • Record administrative actions.
  • Maintain audit history.
  • Apply role-based permissions.
  • Notify affected users where appropriate.

docs.title: Success Outcome
docs.text: Platform remains operational and properly managed.

docs.title: Exception Journey
docs.text:
• Unauthorized access.
  • Validation errors.
  • Concurrent updates.

docs.title: Journey Relationships
docs.text:
flowchart LR

BrowseProducts --> PlaceOrder

PlaceOrder --> VendorProcess

VendorProcess --> ModifyOrder

VendorProcess --> Pickup

ModifyOrder --> Pickup

Pickup --> Completed

VendorProcess --> Cancelled

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the functional requirements for the Halal-Queue platform.

Each requirement describes a capability that the system shall provide. Detailed business rules are documented separately in the Business Rules section.

docs.title: Requirement Format
docs.text:
Each requirement is assigned a unique identifier.

Example:

  • FR-001
  • FR-002
  • FR-003

Functional requirements use the word shall to indicate mandatory behavior.

docs.title: FR-001
docs.text: The system shall allow users to register using a mobile phone number.

docs.title: FR-002
docs.text: The system shall verify every registration using a One-Time Password (OTP).

docs.title: FR-003
docs.text: The system shall prevent registration using an already registered phone number.

docs.title: FR-004
docs.text: The system shall require users to create a password after successful OTP verification.

docs.title: FR-005
docs.text: The system shall create a customer account after successful registration.

docs.title: FR-006
docs.text: The system shall allow users to log in using their verified phone number and password.

docs.title: FR-007
docs.text: The system shall issue JWT access and refresh tokens after successful authentication.

docs.title: FR-008
docs.text: The system shall invalidate refresh tokens during logout.

docs.title: FR-009
docs.text: The system shall reject invalid authentication attempts.

docs.title: FR-010
docs.text: The system shall allow authenticated users to change their password.

docs.title: FR-011
docs.text: The system shall support password reset through OTP verification.

docs.title: FR-012
docs.text: The system shall allow users to update their profile.

docs.title: FR-013
docs.text:
The system shall support storing:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Profile photo (optional)

docs.title: FR-014
docs.text: The system shall allow administrators to approve vendor accounts.

docs.title: FR-015
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to manage their business profile.

docs.title: FR-016
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to manage multiple branches.

docs.title: FR-017
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to configure operating hours.

docs.title: FR-018
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to temporarily close a branch.

docs.title: FR-019
docs.text: The system shall display vendor availability to customers.

docs.title: FR-020
docs.text: The system shall maintain a global product catalog.

docs.title: FR-021
docs.text: The system shall maintain product categories.

docs.title: FR-022
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to publish product listings from the global catalog.

docs.title: FR-023
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to set prices for their product listings.

docs.title: FR-024
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to mark products as unavailable.

docs.title: FR-025
docs.text: The system shall automatically restore unavailable products to available status during the next scheduled daily reset.

docs.title: FR-026
docs.text: The system shall display only available products to customers for ordering.

docs.title: FR-027
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to add products to the cart.

docs.title: FR-028
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to update product quantities.

docs.title: FR-029
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to remove products from the cart.

docs.title: FR-030
docs.text: The system shall calculate the cart total automatically.

docs.title: FR-031
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to place pickup orders.

docs.title: FR-032
docs.text: The system shall generate a unique order number.

docs.title: FR-033
docs.text: The system shall create one or more order items for every order.

docs.title: FR-034
docs.text: The system shall maintain the order lifecycle.

docs.title: FR-035
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to cancel eligible orders.

docs.title: FR-036
docs.text: The system shall maintain order history.

docs.title: FR-037
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to mark ordered products as unavailable.

docs.title: FR-038
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to propose a reduced quantity for an ordered item.

docs.title: FR-039
docs.text: The system shall require vendors to provide a note when modifying an order item.

docs.title: FR-040
docs.text: The system shall notify customers when an order modification is proposed.

docs.title: FR-041
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to accept a proposed modification.

docs.title: FR-042
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to cancel the affected order item.

docs.title: FR-043
docs.text: The system shall allow customers to cancel the entire order after receiving a modification request.

docs.title: FR-044
docs.text: The system shall generate a unique pickup code for every accepted order.

docs.title: FR-045
docs.text: The system shall allow vendors to verify pickup using the pickup code.

docs.title: FR-046
docs.text: The system shall mark the order as completed after successful pickup verification.

docs.title: FR-047
docs.text: The system shall send OTP notifications.

docs.title: FR-048
docs.text: The system shall send order confirmation notifications.

docs.title: FR-049
docs.text: The system shall notify customers about order status changes.

docs.title: FR-050
docs.text: The system shall notify customers when an order is ready for pickup.

docs.title: FR-051
docs.text: The system shall maintain notification history.

docs.title: FR-052
docs.text: The system shall allow administrators to manage product categories.

docs.title: FR-053
docs.text: The system shall allow administrators to manage the global product catalog.

docs.title: FR-054
docs.text: The system shall approve or reject vendor registrations.

docs.title: FR-055
docs.text: The system shall monitor platform activity through an administrative interface.

docs.title: FR-056
docs.text: The Worker application shall process asynchronous jobs.

docs.title: FR-057
docs.text: The Worker application shall deliver push notifications.

docs.title: FR-058
docs.text: The Worker application shall execute the daily product availability reset.

docs.title: FR-059
docs.text: The Worker application shall retry failed background jobs.

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
Each functional requirement shall be traceable to:

  • Business Rules
  • Use Cases
  • API Endpoints
  • Test Cases

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
This document does not define:

  • User interface design
  • API specifications
  • Database schema
  • Implementation details

These topics are covered by other documentation.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the non-functional requirements for the Halal-Queue platform.

These requirements describe the quality attributes, operational expectations, and constraints that the platform shall satisfy.

docs.title: Requirement Format
docs.text:
Each requirement is assigned a unique identifier.

Example:

  • NFR-001
  • NFR-002

All requirements use the word shall to indicate mandatory behavior.

docs.title: NFR-001
docs.text: The platform shall return at least 95% of API requests within 500 milliseconds under normal operating conditions.

docs.title: NFR-002
docs.text: The platform shall support at least 500 concurrent authenticated users in Version 1.

docs.title: NFR-003
docs.text: The platform shall paginate large result sets.

docs.title: NFR-004
docs.text: Background processing shall not block API requests.

docs.title: NFR-005
docs.text: The production platform shall target 99.5% monthly availability.

docs.title: NFR-006
docs.text: Scheduled maintenance shall be communicated in advance.

docs.title: NFR-007
docs.text: Database transactions shall preserve data consistency.

docs.title: NFR-008
docs.text: The platform shall recover gracefully from temporary external service failures.

docs.title: NFR-009
docs.text: Background jobs shall support automatic retry.

docs.title: NFR-010
docs.text: Backend services shall support horizontal scaling.

docs.title: NFR-011
docs.text: Worker services shall support independent scaling.

docs.title: NFR-012
docs.text: The architecture shall support future migration to microservices without major redesign.

docs.title: NFR-013
docs.text: All network communication shall use HTTPS.

docs.title: NFR-014
docs.text: Passwords shall be hashed using Argon2id.

docs.title: NFR-015
docs.text: The platform shall use JWT access tokens and refresh tokens for authentication.

docs.title: NFR-016
docs.text: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) shall protect all secured resources.

docs.title: NFR-017
docs.text: Sensitive information shall never be written to application logs.

docs.title: NFR-018
docs.text: Only authorized users shall access personal information.

docs.title: NFR-019
docs.text: The platform shall minimize storage of personal information.

docs.title: NFR-020
docs.text: Personal information shall only be processed for legitimate business purposes.

docs.title: NFR-021
docs.text: Customer and Vendor applications shall follow Material Design 3 guidelines.

docs.title: NFR-022
docs.text: The platform shall provide clear validation messages.

docs.title: NFR-023
docs.text: The platform shall provide consistent navigation across all applications.

docs.title: NFR-024
docs.text: Applications shall support scalable text.

docs.title: NFR-025
docs.text: Interactive controls shall be clearly identifiable.

docs.title: NFR-026
docs.text: Important actions shall not depend solely on color.

docs.title: NFR-027
docs.text: The backend shall follow Clean Architecture principles.

docs.title: NFR-028
docs.text: Source code shall follow the project's coding standards.

docs.title: NFR-029
docs.text: Business logic shall be isolated from framework-specific code.

docs.title: NFR-030
docs.text: Shared functionality shall be implemented in reusable packages where appropriate.

docs.title: NFR-031
docs.text: Customer and Vendor applications shall support Android and iOS using React Native with Expo.

docs.title: NFR-032
docs.text: The Admin application shall support modern desktop web browsers.

docs.title: NFR-033
docs.text: REST APIs shall use JSON for request and response payloads.

docs.title: NFR-034
docs.text: All primary business entities shall have unique identifiers.

docs.title: NFR-035
docs.text: Referential integrity shall be enforced by the database.

docs.title: NFR-036
docs.text: Business-critical operations shall execute within database transactions.

docs.title: NFR-037
docs.text: The platform shall log authentication events.

docs.title: NFR-038
docs.text: The platform shall log application errors.

docs.title: NFR-039
docs.text: The platform shall monitor API health.

docs.title: NFR-040
docs.text: The platform shall monitor worker health and background job execution.

docs.title: NFR-041
docs.text: Production databases shall be backed up daily.

docs.title: NFR-042
docs.text: Backup restoration procedures shall be tested periodically.

docs.title: NFR-043
docs.text: Object storage shall support backup and recovery.

docs.title: NFR-044
docs.text: The platform architecture shall support English only.

docs.title: NFR-045
docs.text: Dates, times, and numbers shall be formatted according to the US locale (en-US).

docs.title: NFR-046
docs.text: Environment-specific configuration shall be externalized.

docs.title: NFR-047
docs.text: Secrets shall never be stored in source code.

docs.title: NFR-048
docs.text: Push notifications shall be delivered asynchronously.

docs.title: NFR-049
docs.text: Temporary notification delivery failures shall be retried automatically.

docs.title: NFR-050
docs.text: Uploaded files shall be stored in S3-compatible object storage.

docs.title: NFR-051
docs.text: Uploaded files shall be validated before storage.

docs.title: NFR-052
docs.text: Version 1 shall use a Modular Monolith architecture.

docs.title: NFR-053
docs.text: The backend shall be implemented using NestJS.

docs.title: NFR-054
docs.text: The primary database shall be PostgreSQL.

docs.title: NFR-055
docs.text: Redis shall be used for caching and queue infrastructure.

docs.title: NFR-056
docs.text: BullMQ shall be used for background job processing.

docs.title: NFR-057
docs.text: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) shall be used for push notifications.

docs.title: NFR-058
docs.text: Prisma ORM shall be used for database access.

docs.title: NFR-059
docs.text: The Customer and Vendor mobile applications shall be developed using React Native with Expo.

docs.title: NFR-056
docs.text: The Admin application shall be developed using React and Vite as a Single Page Application (SPA).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Each non-functional requirement shall be verified through one or more of:

  • Code Review
  • Automated Testing
  • Performance Testing
  • Security Testing
  • Integration Testing
  • Manual Validation

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
This document does not define:

  • Business processes
  • User interface layouts
  • Database schema
  • REST API specifications
  • Deployment procedures

These topics are covered in other project documentation.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document describes the interactions between users and the Halal-Queue platform to achieve business goals.

Each use case identifies the primary actor, preconditions, normal flow, alternative flow, and postconditions.

docs.title: Actors
docs.text: Actor Description Customer Places pickup orders. Vendor Manages business, products, and orders. Administrator Manages the platform and vendors. Worker Executes automated background tasks.

docs.title: UC-001 Register Customer
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Preconditions

  • Phone number is not registered.

Main Flow

  1. Customer enters a phone number.
  2. System sends an OTP.
  3. Customer enters the OTP.
  4. System verifies the OTP.
  5. Customer creates a password.
  6. Customer account is created.

Alternative Flow

  • OTP is invalid or expired.
  • Customer requests a new OTP.

Postconditions

  • Customer account exists.
  • Phone number is verified.

docs.title: UC-002 Login
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer, Vendor, Administrator

Preconditions

  • Account exists.
  • Phone number is verified.

Main Flow

  1. User enters phone number.
  2. User enters password.
  3. System validates credentials.
  4. System issues access and refresh tokens.
  5. User is authenticated.

Alternative Flow

  • Invalid credentials.
  • Account disabled.

Postconditions

  • User session is established.

docs.title: UC-003 Manage Profile
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Main Flow

  1. Customer opens profile.
  2. Customer updates personal information.
  3. System validates input.
  4. Profile is saved.

Postconditions

  • Profile information is updated.

docs.title: UC-004 Browse Products
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Main Flow

  1. Customer selects a vendor.
  2. System displays product categories.
  3. Customer browses products.
  4. Only available products are displayed.

docs.title: UC-005 Search Products
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Main Flow

  1. Customer enters a search term.
  2. System searches available products.
  3. Matching products are displayed.

docs.title: UC-006 Manage Cart
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Main Flow

  1. Customer adds products.
  2. Customer updates quantities.
  3. Customer removes products if desired.
  4. System recalculates totals.

docs.title: UC-007 Place Order
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Preconditions

  • Cart contains at least one product.

Main Flow

  1. Customer reviews the cart.
  2. Customer submits the order.
  3. System validates product availability.
  4. Order is created.
  5. Order number is generated.
  6. Customer receives confirmation.

Alternative Flow

  • Product becomes unavailable before order submission.

Postconditions

  • Order is recorded.

docs.title: UC-008 Prepare Order
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Main Flow

  1. Vendor views new orders.
  2. Vendor prepares requested items.
  3. Vendor updates order status.
  4. Customer receives notification.

docs.title: UC-009 Modify Order
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Main Flow

  1. Vendor identifies an unavailable product or insufficient quantity.
  2. Vendor marks the product unavailable or proposes a reduced quantity.
  3. Vendor enters a note explaining the change.
  4. Customer is notified.

Alternative Flow

  • Vendor completes the order without modifications.

docs.title: UC-010 Respond to Order Modification
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer

Main Flow

  1. Customer reviews the proposed changes.
  2. Customer accepts the changes, cancels the affected item, or cancels the entire order.
  3. System updates the order.

Postconditions

  • Order reflects the customer's decision.

docs.title: UC-011 Verify Pickup
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Preconditions

  • Order status is Ready for Pickup.

Main Flow

  1. Customer provides the pickup code.
  2. Vendor enters or scans the pickup code.
  3. System validates the code.
  4. Order is marked as completed.

Alternative Flow

  • Pickup code is invalid.

docs.title: UC-012 Manage Business Profile
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Main Flow

  1. Vendor updates business information.
  2. Vendor saves changes.
  3. System validates and stores the information.

docs.title: UC-013 Manage Branches
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Main Flow

  1. Vendor creates or edits branches.
  2. Vendor configures operating hours.
  3. Vendor saves changes.

docs.title: UC-014 Manage Product Listings
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Vendor

Main Flow

  1. Vendor selects products from the global catalog.
  2. Vendor sets prices.
  3. Vendor marks products available or unavailable.
  4. Product listings are updated.

docs.title: UC-015 Manage Categories
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Administrator

Main Flow

  1. Administrator creates, edits, or removes categories.
  2. System updates the catalog.

docs.title: UC-016 Manage Global Products
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Administrator

Main Flow

  1. Administrator creates or updates global products.
  2. Product catalog is updated.

docs.title: UC-017 Approve Vendor
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Administrator

Main Flow

  1. Administrator reviews a vendor application.
  2. Administrator approves or rejects the application.
  3. Vendor is notified.

docs.title: UC-018 Receive Notifications
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Customer, Vendor

Main Flow

  1. A business event occurs.
  2. Worker queues a notification.
  3. Notification is delivered.
  4. User views the notification.

docs.title: UC-019 Daily Product Availability Reset
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Worker

Main Flow

  1. Scheduled task executes daily.
  2. Previously unavailable products are restored to available status.
  3. Vendors can manually mark products unavailable again if necessary.

docs.title: UC-020 Retry Failed Background Job
docs.text:
Primary Actor

Worker

Main Flow

  1. A background job fails.
  2. Worker retries according to retry policy.
  3. Job succeeds or is marked permanently failed after maximum retries.

docs.text:
Each use case shall trace to:

  • Functional Requirements

  • API Endpoints
  • Test Cases

This document does not define:

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the official terminology used throughout the Halal-Queue platform.

All project documentation, APIs, database design, source code, and user interfaces should use these definitions consistently.

docs.title: Account
docs.text: A registered identity that can authenticate to the platform.

docs.title: Administrator
docs.text: A platform user responsible for managing the overall system, including vendors, categories, and the global product catalog.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Application Programming Interface used for communication between client applications and the backend.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The process of verifying a user's identity before granting access.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: The process of determining whether an authenticated user is permitted to perform a specific action.

docs.title: Background Job
docs.text: A task executed asynchronously by the Worker application using BullMQ.

docs.title: Branch
docs.text:
A physical pickup location operated by a Vendor.

A Vendor may own multiple branches.

docs.title: Business Profile
docs.text: Information describing a Vendor's business, such as business name, description, and contact information.

docs.title: Cart
docs.text: A temporary collection of products selected by a Customer before placing an order.

docs.title: Category
docs.text: A logical grouping of products in the global product catalog.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text: A registered user who places pickup orders.

docs.title: FCM
docs.text:
Firebase Cloud Messaging.

Used to deliver push notifications to mobile applications.

docs.title: Functional Requirement
docs.text: A capability that the system must provide.

docs.title: Global Product
docs.text:
A master product definition maintained by administrators.

Vendors create their own product listings from the global product catalog.

docs.title: JWT
docs.text: JSON Web Token used to authenticate API requests.

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirement
docs.text:
A quality attribute describing how well the system performs.

Examples include security, performance, scalability, and reliability.

docs.title: Notification
docs.text:
A message delivered to a user informing them of a business event.

Examples include:

  • Order confirmation
  • Order status changes
  • Pickup ready
  • OTP verification

docs.title: Operating Hours
docs.text: The days and times during which a Branch accepts pickup orders.

docs.title: Order
docs.text: A customer's request to purchase one or more products for pickup.

docs.title: Order Item
docs.text: An individual product included in an Order.

docs.title: Order Modification
docs.text:
A change proposed by a Vendor after an order has been placed.

Examples include:

  • Product unavailable
  • Reduced quantity

docs.title: OTP
docs.text:
One-Time Password.

Used to verify ownership of a mobile phone number.

docs.title: Password
docs.text: A secret credential created by a user after successful phone number verification.

docs.title: Pickup
docs.text: The process by which a Customer collects an order from a Branch.

docs.title: Pickup Code
docs.text:
A unique code generated for an accepted order.

The Vendor verifies this code before completing the pickup.

docs.title: Product
docs.text: An item available for purchase from the global product catalog.

docs.title: Product Availability
docs.text:
The current availability status of a Vendor's product listing.

Products may be temporarily unavailable and automatically restored during the daily reset process.

docs.title: Product Listing
docs.text: A Vendor-specific offering of a Global Product, including price and availability.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text: The personal information associated with a registered Account.

docs.title: RBAC
docs.text:
Role-Based Access Control.

An authorization model that grants permissions based on assigned roles.

docs.title: Refresh Token
docs.text: A long-lived token used to obtain a new JWT access token after the current one expires.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: The HTTP-based interface exposed by the backend for client applications.

docs.title: Scheduled Job
docs.text:
A background task executed automatically at a predefined time.

Example:

Daily product availability reset.

docs.title: SMS Provider
docs.text: An external service responsible for delivering OTP messages.

docs.title: System Administrator
docs.text: See Administrator.

docs.title: User
docs.text:
A generic term referring to any authenticated person using the platform.

User roles include:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Administrator

docs.title: Vendor
docs.text: A business that offers products for customer pickup through the platform.

docs.title: Vendor Owner
docs.text: The primary account responsible for managing a Vendor.

docs.title: Vendor Product Listing
docs.text: A Vendor's configured offering of a Global Product, including pricing and availability.

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text: A persistent communication channel used for real-time updates between the backend and connected applications.

docs.title: Worker
docs.text: A background application responsible for processing asynchronous jobs, scheduled tasks, and notifications.

Preferred Term Avoid Vendor Shop, Store, Merchant Branch Outlet, Location Customer Consumer, Buyer Product Listing Vendor Product Global Product Master Product Pickup Collection Pickup Code Collection Code Order Modification Order Change Worker Background Service

docs.title: Purpose

This directory contains the authoritative business rules governing the Halal-Queue platform.

Every functional requirement, API endpoint, database constraint, workflow, UI behavior, and automated test should trace back to one or more business rules defined here.

Business rules describe what the business requires, not how the software is implemented.
