docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the rules governing Platform Administrators. Administrators hold elevated privileges to manage the global catalog, onboard/suspend vendors, and oversee platform health.

docs.title: BR-ADM-001 — Global Catalog Management
docs.text: Statement: Only Platform Administrators have the authority to create, modify, or archive Global Products and Categories.

docs.title: BR-ADM-002 — Vendor Suspension
docs.text: Statement: Platform Administrators may suspend a vendor at any time for policy violations. Consequence: A suspended vendor is immediately hidden from the customer app, and all incoming orders are blocked. Existing Preparing orders must still be fulfilled or manually cancelled by the administrator.

docs.title: BR-ADM-003 — Custom Variation Approval
docs.text: Statement: When a vendor creates a custom variation on their product listing, it is placed in a Pending Approval state. A Platform Administrator must review and approve the variation before the listing becomes active and visible to customers.

docs.title: BR-ADM-004 — Transaction Overrides
docs.text: Statement: Administrators have the authority to initiate manual refunds on behalf of a vendor in the event of a dispute.

docs.title: BR-ADM-005 — System Notifications
docs.text: Statement: Administrators may broadcast push notifications or banner messages to all Customers or all Vendors (e.g., for system maintenance or promotional events).

docs.title: BR-ADM-006 — Admin Audit Trail
docs.text: Statement: Every action taken by a Platform Administrator (e.g., approving a vendor, editing a global product, refunding an order) must be securely logged with a timestamp and the Administrator's identity. This audit log cannot be modified or deleted.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document governs the behavior of the customer's shopping cart before it is converted into a finalized Order.

docs.title: BR-CRT-001 — Single Vendor Constraint
docs.text: Statement: A single shopping cart may only contain items from a single Vendor Branch. Rationale: Since fulfillment is based on physical pickup at a specific location, a single order/cart cannot span multiple physical vendors.

docs.title: BR-CRT-002 — Cart Clearing on Vendor Change
docs.text: Statement: If a customer has items in their cart from Vendor A and attempts to add an item from Vendor B, the system must prompt the customer to either clear their cart to proceed with Vendor B or cancel the action.

docs.title: BR-CRT-003 — Cart Persistence
docs.text: Statement: Cart contents should persist across application restarts for the logged-in user. Carts for guest users (if supported) persist only locally on the device.

docs.title: BR-CRT-004 — Price Synchronization
docs.text: Statement: Prices in the cart are not locked. If a vendor changes the price of a product while it is sitting in a customer's cart, the cart total must update dynamically to reflect the current selling price upon checkout.

docs.title: BR-CRT-005 — Minimum Order Value
docs.text: Statement: If the vendor enforces a minimum order value, the checkout button must remain disabled until the cart subtotal meets or exceeds the specified minimum value.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the business rules governing the lifecycle, visibility, publication, searchability, synchronization, and operational management of Vendor Product Listings.

docs.title: Publication Lifecycle
docs.text:
A Vendor Product Listing progresses through the following lifecycle:

Draft
   │
   ├────────► Active (Standard)
   │
   └────────► Pending Approval (Custom Variations)
                   │
                   ▼
                 Active
   │
   ├────────► Unavailable
   │              │
   │              ▼
   └──────────── Active

Active
   │
   ▼
Archived

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A newly created Vendor Product Listing shall initially be in the Draft state unless explicitly published by the vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Draft listings shall only be visible to the owning vendor.

Customers, administrators (except for management purposes), and other vendors shall not see draft listings in customer-facing views.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may publish a Draft listing only when all mandatory product information has been completed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Before a listing becomes Active, the platform shall validate that all required information is present, including:

  • Selling price
  • Availability configuration
  • Required variation configuration
  • At least one display image (vendor-specific or inherited)
  • Active Global Product reference

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If a Vendor Product Listing includes custom, vendor-specific Variation Groups, publishing the listing shall transition it to a Pending Approval state instead of Active.

The listing shall remain inactive and invisible to customers until a Platform Administrator approves the custom variations. Upon approval, the listing becomes Active.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only Active listings may receive customer orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Unavailable listings shall remain visible to customers but shall not be purchasable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Archived listings shall be removed from all customer-facing catalog views and shall not accept new orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
An Archived listing shall not be reactivated directly.

A vendor shall restore it to Draft, review its configuration, and publish it again.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customer search results shall include only Active and Unavailable listings.

Draft and Archived listings shall never appear in customer searches.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers may filter products using supported catalog attributes such as:

  • Category
  • Vendor
  • Product name
  • Availability

Additional filters may be introduced in future versions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall support configurable sorting of customer search results.

Supported sorting methods include:

  • Relevance
  • Alphabetical
  • Newest
  • Price (ascending)
  • Price (descending)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendors shall be able to:

  • Create listings
  • Edit listings
  • Archive listings
  • Publish listings
  • Mark listings unavailable
  • Restore availability

Only for listings they own.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Administrators may manage Global Products, Categories, and perform administrative actions on Vendor Product Listings when required.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Updates to shared Global Product attributes shall automatically synchronize to all related Vendor Product Listings unless explicitly designated as vendor-managed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Synchronization of Global Product updates shall not overwrite vendor-managed attributes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Changes to catalog information shall not modify historical order data.

Orders shall preserve the product snapshot captured at the time of purchase.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If a Global Product is archived, all related Vendor Product Listings shall automatically become unavailable for new orders.

Historical orders shall remain unchanged.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Moving a Global Product to a different category shall immediately affect all associated Vendor Product Listings.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Catalog search indexes shall be refreshed whenever searchable product information changes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall prevent duplicate Vendor Product Listings for the same vendor and Global Product combination.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Customers shall never see incomplete, inconsistent, or partially configured product listings.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record audit events for significant catalog operations, including:

  • Publication
  • Archiving
  • Price updates
  • Availability changes
  • Category changes
  • Global Product updates
  • Synchronization events

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Vendor Product Listing shall always reference a valid Active or Archived Global Product.

Orphaned Vendor Product Listings shall not exist.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Platform Administrators may temporarily disable Vendor Product Listings that violate platform policies.

Disabled listings shall not be visible to customers until restored.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The catalog architecture shall support future enhancements, including:

  • Product tags
  • Brand management
  • Product bundles
  • Related products
  • Nutritional information
  • Certifications
  • Product recommendations These capabilities are outside the scope of Version 1.

docs.text: State Vendor Customer Purchasable Draft Visible Hidden No Pending Approval Visible Hidden No Active Visible Visible Yes Unavailable Visible Visible No Archived Visible Hidden No Disabled (Admin) Visible Hidden No

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the structure of the Halal-Queue product catalog.

It covers:

  • Categories
  • Global Products
  • Vendor Product Listings
  • Quantity Types
  • Product Variations
  • Product Images
  • Product Identity

Business rules related to pricing, availability, visibility, and vendor management are documented separately.

docs.title: Catalog Overview
docs.text:
The Halal-Queue catalog follows a two-level model.

Global Product

↓

Vendor Product Listing

A Global Product defines the product itself.

Each vendor creates its own Vendor Product Listing from the Global Product.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every product in the platform shall originate from a single Global Product.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Provides a standardized catalog shared across all vendors.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Customers purchase Vendor Product Listings rather than Global Products directly.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A single Global Product may have multiple Vendor Product Listings.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Vendor Product Listing shall belong to exactly one vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Global Product shall have a permanent unique identifier.

The identifier shall never change.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Vendor Product Listing shall have its own permanent unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Global Product shall have one primary display name.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Global Product may include an optional description.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Global Product may contain one or more images.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: One image shall be designated as the primary image.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Global Product shall belong to exactly one primary category.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Categories may contain child categories.

The hierarchy shall form a tree.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Categories are managed by Platform Administrators.

Vendors cannot create categories.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Archived categories shall not accept new Global Products.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Global Product shall define exactly one quantity type.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: To support products that are sold by both Weight and Piece (e.g., Meat), Platform Administrators should create separate Global Products based on the underlying quantity type (e.g., "Chicken (Whole)" vs "Chicken (Per Kg)").

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Piece
  • Weight
  • Custom Unit

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every quantity type shall define its display unit.

Examples:

  • Piece
  • kg
  • g
  • Pack
  • Dozen
  • Bottle

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Products using weight-based quantity types may support fractional quantities.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Products using piece-based quantity types shall only allow whole-number quantities.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Global Product may define one or more Variation Groups.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Variation Group represents one configurable aspect of a product.

Examples:

  • Size
  • Cut
  • Packaging
  • Freshness

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Variation Group shall contain one or more Variation Options.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Variation Group shall define whether customers may select:

  • Exactly one option
  • Multiple options

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Variation Groups may be mandatory or optional.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Variation Groups shall have a configurable display order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Variation Options shall also have an independent display order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Global Product shall exist in one of the following states:

  • Draft
  • Active
  • Archived

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Draft Global Products shall not be visible to vendors or customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Archived Global Products shall not accept new Vendor Product Listings.

Existing Vendor Product Listings shall become unavailable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The identity of a Global Product shall never change during its lifecycle.

Business attributes may change, but identity shall remain constant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing Vendor Product Listings.

A Vendor Product Listing represents the products that a vendor actually sells to customers.

The listing references a Global Product while allowing the vendor to manage its own commercial and operational information.

docs.title: Vendor Listing Overview
docs.text:
Global Product
      │
      ├──────────────┐
      │              │
Vendor A         Vendor B
Listing          Listing

The Global Product is shared.

Each Vendor Product Listing is independent.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Vendor Product Listing shall belong to exactly one vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Vendor Product Listing shall reference exactly one Global Product.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each vendor manages its own listing independently of other vendors.

Changes made by one vendor shall never affect another vendor's listing.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Vendor Product Listing shall define its own selling price.

Prices are vendor-specific.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Vendor Product Listing shall maintain its own availability status.

Availability shall not affect other vendors.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: When a vendor manually marks a product as unavailable, the system shall automatically restore the product to Available at the beginning of the vendor's next business day unless the vendor archives the listing or manually changes its status beforehand.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may archive a Vendor Product Listing.

Archived listings shall not be visible to customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor Product Listing shall exist in one of the following states:

  • Active
  • Unavailable
  • Archived

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may provide an optional description specific to its own listing.

The Global Product description shall remain unchanged.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may optionally provide vendor-specific product images.

If no vendor images are provided, the Global Product primary image shall be displayed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may configure the display priority of its own listings for internal management purposes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may define internal preparation notes for staff.

Internal notes shall never be visible to customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor Product Listing shall support the Variation Groups defined by its associated Global Product.

Additionally, a vendor may create custom, vendor-specific Variation Groups for options not covered by the Global Product. However, adding custom Variation Groups requires administrative approval before the listing can become Active.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may disable specific Variation Options that are not currently offered.

Disabled options shall not be presented to customers for that vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may define price adjustments for individual Variation Options.

Example:

  • Large Cut: +$2.00
  • Premium Packaging: +$1.50

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only Active Vendor Product Listings shall be visible to customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Unavailable listings may appear in search results but shall be clearly identified as unavailable and shall not be purchasable.

Archived listings shall not appear in customer search results.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor shall only be able to create, modify, archive, or delete its own Vendor Product Listings.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Changes to shared Global Product attributes shall automatically be reflected in all Vendor Product Listings unless the attribute is vendor-managed.

Examples of shared attributes include:

  • Product name
  • Category
  • Quantity type
  • Variation structure

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The following attributes are managed independently by each vendor:

  • Selling price
  • Availability
  • Vendor description
  • Vendor images
  • Internal preparation notes
  • Archived status
  • Variation option availability
  • Variation price adjustments
  • Custom variation groups

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may only create a Vendor Product Listing from an Active Global Product.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor shall not create more than one active Vendor Product Listing for the same Global Product.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendor Product Listings shall not be permanently deleted.

Listings shall be archived to preserve historical order integrity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Changes made to a Vendor Product Listing shall not modify historical orders.

Historical orders shall retain a snapshot of product information at the time the order was placed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record all significant Vendor Product Listing changes, including:

  • Listing creation
  • Price changes
  • Availability changes
  • Archive actions
  • Image updates
  • Variation configuration changes

docs.text: Attribute Managed By Selling Price Vendor Availability Vendor Description Vendor Images Vendor Preparation Notes Vendor Variation Option Availability Vendor Variation Price Adjustments Vendor Custom Variation Groups Vendor Archived Status Vendor

docs.title: Platform-Managed Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Managed By Product Name Platform Category Platform Quantity Type Platform Variation Groups Platform Variation Definitions Platform Global Images Platform

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the business rules governing how customers pick up their orders from vendors. Halal-Queue is a pick-up-centric platform, so managing expectations, timing, and verification during pickup is critical.

docs.title: BR-PKP-001 — Fulfillment Method
docs.text: Statement: Halal-Queue exclusively supports Customer Pickup (Takeaway). Delivery is not supported in Version 1.

docs.title: BR-PKP-002 — Ready for Pickup State
docs.text: Statement: A customer may only pick up an order once the vendor has explicitly transitioned the order state to Ready for Pickup.

docs.title: BR-PKP-003 — Pickup Verification
docs.text: Statement: Vendors must verify the identity of the customer before handing over the order. This is done by verifying the unique Order Number or scanning the customer's Order QR code generated by the Customer App.

docs.title: BR-PKP-004 — Order Handover
docs.text: Statement: Once the order has been handed to the customer, the vendor must mark the order as Completed. This serves as the official timestamp of fulfillment.

docs.title: BR-PKP-005 — Abandoned Orders
docs.text: Statement: If a customer fails to pick up an order within a vendor-defined grace period (e.g., 2 hours after closing time), the vendor may mark the order as Abandoned. Abandoned orders are not eligible for a customer-initiated refund.

docs.title: BR-PKP-006 — Pickup Time Estimates
docs.text: Statement: When an order is placed, the system must provide the customer with an estimated pickup time based on the vendor's current queue size and the specific prep time of the items ordered.

docs.title: BR-PKP-007 — Early Arrival
docs.text: Statement: Customers arriving before the Ready for Pickup notification must wait. Vendors are not obligated to expedite orders for early arrivals.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines how a vendor operates on a day-to-day basis, including store toggling, order queue management, and staff interactions.

docs.title: BR-VOP-001 — Store Online/Offline Status
docs.text: Statement: A vendor may manually toggle their store status between Online and Offline at any time during their configured operating hours. Rationale: Allows vendors to pause incoming orders if they become overwhelmed.

docs.title: BR-VOP-002 — Auto-Offline Outside Operating Hours
docs.text: Statement: The system shall automatically reject new orders and display the vendor as Closed if the current time falls outside the vendor's defined operating hours, regardless of the manual Online/Offline toggle.

docs.title: BR-VOP-003 — Active Order Queue
docs.text: Statement: Vendors must process orders in a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) manner, unless a specific order requires significantly longer preparation time.

docs.title: BR-VOP-004 — Order Rejection
docs.text: Statement: A vendor may reject a newly placed order before accepting it. If an order is rejected, the customer must be notified immediately, and the payment authorization must be voided or refunded. Restriction: Vendors cannot reject an order once it has transitioned to the Preparing state.

docs.title: BR-VOP-005 — Staff Roles
docs.text: Statement: A vendor may have multiple staff accounts. - Vendor Admin: Can edit business profile, banking details, and manage products. - Vendor Staff: Can only view the order queue, update order statuses, and verify pickups.

docs.title: BR-VOP-006 — End of Day Reconciliation
docs.text: Statement: Vendors have access to a daily summary of Completed and Abandoned orders for financial reconciliation at the end of their business day.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This directory defines the business rules governing identity, authentication, authorization, account lifecycle, and session management within the Halal-Queue platform.

Authentication ensures that every platform user can securely establish their identity, access authorized resources, and perform business operations according to their assigned permissions.

Identity, Authentication, Session Management, and Authorization are modeled as independent subsystems to maintain clear separation of responsibilities and support future expansion.

docs.title: Authentication Domains
docs.text: Document Description identity.md User identity model and account types registration.md User registration rules account-verification.md Email and phone verification authentication.md Login and authentication process session-management.md Sessions, tokens, logout, expiration authorization.md Roles, permissions, and access control account-lifecycle.md Account states and lifecycle password-management.md Password creation, reset, and update

docs.title: Rule Prefix
docs.text:
All Authentication Business Rules use:

BR-AUTH-###

Example:

BR-AUTH-001
BR-AUTH-002
BR-AUTH-003

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Authentication

↓

docs.title: Authentication Principles
docs.text:
The authentication subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every user has a unique identity.
  • Authentication verifies identity.
  • Authorization determines access.
  • Sessions are managed independently of authentication.
  • Security-sensitive actions are auditable.
  • Authentication failures do not expose sensitive information.
  • Business modules shall never implement authentication logic directly.

docs.title: Supported User Types
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Vendor Staff
  • Administrator

Additional user types may be introduced in future platform versions.

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
Authentication records shall be traceable to:

  • User Identity
  • Authentication Events
  • Session Records
  • Authorization Decisions
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the lifecycle of user accounts within the Halal-Queue platform.

Every Identity exists in exactly one Account Status at any point in time. Account Status determines whether the Identity may authenticate, access platform resources, or perform business operations.

docs.title: Lifecycle Principles
docs.text:
The account lifecycle follows these principles:

  • Every Identity has exactly one Account Status.
  • Account Status changes only through approved business processes.
  • Every status transition is auditable.
  • Authentication and authorization depend on Account Status.
  • Historical account information is preserved according to retention policies.

docs.title: Account Lifecycle
docs.text:
Pending Verification

↓

Active

├────────► Locked

├────────► Suspended

├────────► Deactivated

└────────► Deleted (Soft Delete)

docs.title: Account Status Definitions
docs.text: Status Description Pending Verification Registration incomplete; phone number not yet verified Active Normal operating state Locked Temporarily blocked due to security policy Suspended Disabled by an administrator or business policy Deactivated Voluntarily closed by the account owner Deleted Soft-deleted and excluded from normal platform operations

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every newly created Identity shall begin in the Pending Verification status until registration is successfully completed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An Identity shall transition to Active immediately after successful completion of registration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only Identities in the Active status may successfully authenticate.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may transition an Identity to the Locked status in response to security events.

Examples include:

  • Excessive failed authentication attempts
  • Security investigation
  • Detected suspicious activity

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Locked Identities shall not authenticate until the lock is removed.

Existing active Sessions may be revoked according to platform security policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may suspend an Identity for operational, legal, or policy reasons.

Examples include:

  • Fraud investigation
  • Vendor policy violation
  • Abuse of platform services

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Suspended Identities shall not authenticate or perform protected business operations until reactivated.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Users may voluntarily deactivate their own account where permitted by platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Deactivated Identities shall not authenticate.

Business records associated with the Identity shall remain preserved.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Deleted accounts shall be implemented using soft deletion.

Identity records shall remain available for:

  • Audit
  • Historical reporting
  • Order history
  • Legal compliance

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Permanent deletion of Identity records shall occur only through approved administrative or legal data-retention procedures.

Version 1 does not expose permanent deletion through user-facing interfaces.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: When an Identity transitions to Locked, Suspended, Deactivated, or Deleted, the platform may revoke all active Sessions according to security policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Significant lifecycle changes may generate Notification Events.

Examples include:

  • Account suspended
  • Account reactivated
  • Account deactivated

Routine status changes are governed by platform notification policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Account Status transition shall be permanently recorded with:

  • Previous Status
  • New Status
  • Timestamp
  • Initiating Actor
  • Reason (where applicable)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only authorized administrators may transition Identities into or out of administrative statuses such as Locked and Suspended.

Users may not modify these statuses themselves.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every lifecycle transition shall be traceable to:

  • Identity
  • Initiating Actor
  • Session (if applicable)
  • Audit History

docs.title: Example Lifecycle
docs.text:
Registration Started

↓

Pending Verification

↓

Phone Verified

↓

Active

↓

Multiple Failed Login Attempts

↓

Locked

↓

Administrator Unlocks Account

↓

Active

↓

User Requests Account Closure

↓

Deactivated

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing account verification within the Halal-Queue platform.

Version 1 uses phone number verification through One-Time Password (OTP). Verification is implemented as an independent Verification Challenge service that can be reused by other platform features.

docs.title: Verification Principles
docs.text:
The verification subsystem follows these principles:

  • Verification is independent of registration.
  • Every verification request creates a Verification Challenge.
  • Verification Challenges are temporary.
  • OTP values are single-use.
  • Verification is fully auditable.
  • Expired challenges cannot be reused.

docs.title: Verification Architecture
docs.text:
Business Process

↓

Verification Challenge

├── Challenge ID
├── Verification Type
├── Phone Number
├── OTP
├── Attempt Counter
├── Expiration Time
├── Status
└── Audit History

↓

Verification Result

docs.title: Supported Verification Types
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Registration

Future versions may support:

  • Password Reset
  • Phone Number Change
  • Sensitive Account Operations
  • Multi-Factor Authentication

docs.title: Verification Challenge States
docs.text: State Description Created Challenge generated OTP Sent OTP successfully sent Verified Verification completed Failed Maximum attempts exceeded Expired Challenge expired Cancelled Challenge cancelled

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every verification request shall create a new Verification Challenge.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Verification Challenge shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Verification Challenge shall record its verification purpose.

Version 1 supports Registration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Verification Challenge shall be permanently associated with exactly one phone number.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall generate a cryptographically secure One-Time Password for every Verification Challenge.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The generated OTP shall be delivered using the configured SMS provider.

Delivery shall follow the Notification Business Rules where applicable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every OTP shall expire after the configured validity period (currently 10 minutes).

Expired OTP values shall never be accepted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A successfully verified OTP shall become permanently invalid.

The same OTP shall never be accepted again.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall maintain a configurable maximum number of verification attempts for each Verification Challenge.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each failed verification attempt shall increment the challenge attempt counter.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
When the maximum number of verification attempts is exceeded, the Verification Challenge shall transition to the Failed state.

Further verification attempts shall be rejected.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Expired Verification Challenges shall not be reactivated.

A new Verification Challenge shall be created if verification is required again.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A successful OTP verification shall transition the Verification Challenge to the Verified state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only one active Verification Challenge may exist for the same verification purpose and phone number.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall never expose OTP values through logs, APIs, audit records, or administrative interfaces.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may view Verification Challenge metadata for operational support.

OTP values shall never be visible.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record:

  • Challenge created
  • OTP generated
  • OTP sent
  • Verification succeeded
  • Verification failed
  • Challenge expired
  • Challenge cancelled

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: OTP delivery shall generate Notification Events when required by platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Completed, expired, failed, and cancelled Verification Challenges shall remain available for auditing according to the platform's data retention policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Verification Challenge shall be traceable to:

  • Registration Session (if applicable)
  • Phone Number
  • Verification Type
  • Notification Events
  • Audit History

docs.title: Verification Workflow
docs.text:
Verification Requested

↓

Challenge Created

↓

OTP Generated

↓

OTP Sent

↓

User Enters OTP

↓

Verified

OR

Failed

OR

Expired

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing user authentication within the Halal-Queue platform.

Authentication verifies that a user is the legitimate owner of an Identity before granting access to platform resources.

Every login attempt is represented by an immutable Authentication Attempt.

Authentication and Session Management are separate business processes.

docs.title: Authentication Principles
docs.text:
The authentication subsystem follows these principles:

  • Authentication verifies identity.
  • Every login creates an Authentication Attempt.
  • Authentication Attempts are immutable.
  • Successful authentication creates a Session.
  • Failed authentication never creates a Session.
  • Authentication is fully auditable.

docs.title: Authentication Architecture
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Authentication Attempt

↓

Credential Validation

↓

Authenticated

↓

Session Created

↓

Business Access

docs.title: Authentication Attempt States
docs.text: State Description Started Login request received Validating Credentials being verified Succeeded Authentication successful Failed Authentication rejected Blocked Login denied due to security policy

docs.title: Supported Authentication Method
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Phone Number
  • Password

Future versions may additionally support:

  • Passkeys
  • Google Sign-In
  • Apple Sign-In
  • Magic Links
  • OTP Login
  • Multi-Factor Authentication

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every login request shall create an Authentication Attempt.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Authentication Attempt shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users shall authenticate using:

  • Phone Number
  • Password

No alternative authentication methods are supported in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only Identities in the Active state may authenticate successfully.

Pending Verification, Suspended, and Deactivated identities shall be denied authentication.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authentication shall validate the submitted password against the securely stored password hash.

Plain-text passwords shall never be stored or compared.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A successful Authentication Attempt shall transition to the Succeeded state and trigger Session creation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Invalid credentials shall transition the Authentication Attempt to the Failed state.

No Session shall be created.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authentication failures shall return a generic response.

The platform shall not reveal whether the phone number or password was incorrect.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall maintain a configurable count of consecutive failed Authentication Attempts for each Identity and phone number.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
When the configured threshold of failed Authentication Attempts is reached, further authentication attempts may be temporarily blocked.

The block duration shall be configurable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A successful authentication shall reset the consecutive failed Authentication Attempt counter.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Authentication Attempt may record device information, including:

  • Device Type
  • Operating System
  • Application Version
  • Device Identifier (if available)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Authentication Attempt may record:

  • IP Address
  • User Agent
  • Geographic Region (if available)

This information is used for security monitoring and auditing.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Authentication Attempt shall record:

  • Request Time
  • Completion Time

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may evaluate Authentication Attempts for suspicious activity, including:

  • Excessive failures
  • Rapid repeated attempts
  • Repeated attempts from different IP addresses
  • Unusual device patterns

Version 1 records these events for monitoring but does not automatically classify risk.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record:

  • Authentication Started
  • Authentication Succeeded
  • Authentication Failed
  • Authentication Blocked

according to the platform's data retention policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may generate a Notification Event for significant authentication-related events, including:

  • Password changed
  • Login from a new device (future)
  • Account locked
  • Suspicious authentication activity (future)

Routine successful logins shall not generate notifications in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authentication Attempts shall never be modified or deleted except in accordance with approved data retention policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Authentication Attempt shall be traceable to:

  • Identity
  • Session (if created)
  • Device Information
  • Network Information
  • Audit History

docs.title: Authentication Workflow
docs.text:
Login Requested

↓

Authentication Attempt Created

↓

Phone Number Lookup

↓

Password Validation

↓

Succeeded
      │
      ▼
Session Created

OR

Failed

OR

Blocked

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing authorization within the Halal-Queue platform.

Authorization determines which business operations an authenticated Identity is permitted to perform.

Authorization is based on Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

docs.title: Authorization Principles
docs.text:
The authorization subsystem follows these principles:

  • Authentication verifies identity.
  • Authorization grants permissions.
  • Permissions are assigned to Roles.
  • Identities receive permissions only through assigned Roles.
  • Business modules never implement authorization logic independently.
  • Every authorization decision is auditable.

docs.title: Authorization Architecture
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Role Assignment

↓

Role

↓

Permission Catalog

↓

Authorization Decision

↓

Business Operation

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Represents a platform user.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Represents a business responsibility.

Examples:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Vendor Staff
  • Administrator

docs.title: Permission
docs.text:
Represents a single business capability.

Examples:

  • Create Order
  • Cancel Order
  • Manage Products
  • View Reports
  • Manage Users

docs.title: Role Assignment
docs.text: Connects an Identity to one or more Roles.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every protected business operation shall require authorization before execution.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only authenticated Active Sessions may request authorization.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Identity shall have at least one assigned Role.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
An Identity may be assigned multiple Roles when permitted by platform policy.

Example:

  • Vendor
  • Customer

The effective permissions are the union of all assigned Roles.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Permissions shall only be assigned to Roles.

Permissions shall never be assigned directly to Identities.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: All platform permissions shall be centrally maintained within the Permission Catalog.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Permission shall have a unique identifier and descriptive name.

Examples:

  • order.create
  • order.cancel
  • catalog.product.create
  • catalog.product.update
  • vendor.staff.manage

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Roles shall grant only the minimum permissions required to perform their business responsibilities.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Customer Role may perform only customer-facing operations.

Examples include:

  • Browse vendors
  • Browse products
  • Place orders
  • View own orders
  • Manage own profile

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Vendor Role may perform operations related to the vendor's own business.

Examples include:

  • Manage products
  • Manage categories
  • Accept orders
  • Reject orders
  • Update order status
  • Manage vendor staff

Vendor permissions apply only to resources owned by that vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendor Staff permissions are limited to responsibilities assigned by the Vendor.

Examples include:

  • View assigned orders
  • Update preparation status
  • Verify pickup
  • Manage inventory (if authorized)

Vendor Staff shall never receive platform-wide administrative permissions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Administrators may perform platform administration according to assigned administrative permissions.

Administrative permissions shall be managed separately from vendor permissions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorization shall validate resource ownership where applicable.

Example:

A Vendor may update only products belonging to that Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Unauthorized requests shall be rejected.

The response shall not disclose internal permission structures.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Changes to Role definitions or Permission assignments affect future authorization decisions immediately.

Existing Sessions are not required to be recreated.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only authorized Administrators may create, modify, or deactivate Roles and Permissions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall audit:

  • Role assignments
  • Permission changes
  • Administrative authorization changes
  • Critical authorization failures

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Permissions may be evaluated together with resource ownership and business context.

Possessing a permission alone does not guarantee access to every resource.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The authorization architecture shall support future capabilities including:

  • Custom Roles
  • Permission Groups
  • Temporary Permissions
  • Time-based Access
  • Delegated Administration
  • Organization-level Roles

These capabilities are outside the scope of Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every authorization decision shall be traceable to:

  • Identity
  • Session
  • Assigned Roles
  • Required Permission
  • Business Resource
  • Audit History

docs.title: Example Role Model
docs.text:
Customer
    │
    ├── order.create
    ├── order.view.own
    └── profile.update

Vendor
    │
    ├── catalog.manage
    ├── order.manage
    ├── staff.manage
    └── reports.view

Vendor Staff
    │
    ├── order.prepare
    ├── pickup.verify
    └── inventory.view

Administrator
    │
    ├── users.manage
    ├── vendors.manage
    ├── roles.manage
    ├── permissions.manage
    └── system.manage

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing user identity within the Halal-Queue platform.

Identity represents a person within the platform. It exists independently of authentication credentials, sessions, and authorization while serving as the foundation for all user-related operations.

Version 1 authenticates users using Phone Number + Password after successful phone number verification.

docs.title: Identity Principles
docs.text:
The identity subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every user has exactly one Identity.
  • Every Identity has one unique phone number.
  • Identity is independent of authentication credentials.
  • Identity owns profile information.
  • Identity owns roles and permissions through authorization.
  • Identity is immutable except through approved profile updates.

docs.title: Identity Model
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Phone Number (Unique)

↓

Profile

├── Name
├── Email

↓

Credentials

└── Password Hash

↓

Verification

└── Phone OTP

↓

Roles

↓

Sessions

↓

Audit History

docs.title: Supported Identity Types
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Vendor Staff
  • Administrator

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every registered user shall have exactly one Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall have a permanent globally unique identifier.

The internal Identity ID shall never be exposed publicly.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall have exactly one unique phone number.

Duplicate phone numbers are not permitted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A phone number may belong to only one active Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An Identity shall not become active until the associated phone number has been successfully verified using OTP.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall include the user's full name.

Name is required.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall include the user's email address.

Email is required but does not require verification in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users shall authenticate using:

  • Phone Number
  • Password

No other authentication methods are supported in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall exist in one of the following states:

  • Pending Verification
  • Active
  • Suspended
  • Deactivated

Only Active identities may authenticate successfully.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Identity shall be traceable to:

  • Profile
  • Credentials
  • Phone Verification
  • Sessions
  • Roles
  • Notification Preference Profile
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing password creation, storage, validation, updates, and password recovery.

Password management is independent from Authentication and Verification while integrating with both.

Version 1 authenticates users using:

  • Phone Number
  • Password

Password reset uses the existing Verification Challenge service.

docs.title: Password Principles
docs.text:
The password subsystem follows these principles:

  • Passwords are never stored in plain text.
  • Password creation occurs only after successful phone verification.
  • Password reset requires successful identity verification.
  • Password changes are auditable.
  • Password operations may revoke active sessions.
  • Password policies are centrally managed.

docs.title: Password Architecture
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Password

↓

Authentication

↓

Verification Challenge

↓

Password Reset

↓

Session Revocation

↓

Audit History

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Identity shall define a password during registration after successful phone verification.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Passwords shall never be stored in plain text.

The platform shall store only a secure password hash using an approved password hashing algorithm.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Passwords shall satisfy the platform's configured password policy.

Version 1 policy shall include:

  • Minimum length
  • Maximum length
  • Configurable complexity requirements

The exact values are configuration settings, not business rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
During password creation and password change, users shall confirm the new password.

Passwords must match before submission is accepted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Submitted passwords shall be validated only by comparing the supplied password with the stored password hash.

Plain-text comparison is prohibited.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authenticated users may change their password after providing their current password.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users who cannot authenticate may reset their password after successful completion of a Verification Challenge.

Version 1 uses phone number verification.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Password reset shall require a successfully completed Verification Challenge.

Expired, failed, or cancelled Verification Challenges shall not permit password reset.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A completed Verification Challenge authorizes exactly one password reset operation.

Once the password has been successfully changed, the reset authorization becomes invalid.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
After a successful password reset, all active Sessions associated with the Identity shall be revoked.

Users shall authenticate again using the new password.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
After a password change initiated from an authenticated session, the platform may revoke all other active Sessions while allowing the current Session to continue.

The exact behavior shall be defined by platform security policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 does not restrict reuse of previous passwords.

Future versions may enforce password history policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The architecture shall support password history enforcement in future versions without changing the Identity model.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 does not require periodic password expiration.

Future versions may introduce configurable password lifetime policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may initiate a password reset process.

Administrators shall never know or set a user's password directly.

Administrative resets shall require the user to complete a Verification Challenge before choosing a new password.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Passwords, password hashes, and verification secrets shall never appear in:

  • API responses
  • Logs
  • Audit records
  • Administrative interfaces
  • Notification messages

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record password-related security events including:

  • Password created
  • Password changed
  • Password reset requested
  • Password reset completed
  • Password reset failed

The password itself shall never be recorded.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Successful password changes and password resets shall generate Notification Events.

Version 1 may notify users using SMS and In-App notifications according to platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every password operation shall be traceable to:

  • Identity
  • Verification Challenge (if applicable)
  • Authentication Attempt (if applicable)
  • Session
  • Notification Event
  • Audit History

docs.title: Password Reset Workflow
docs.text:
Forgot Password

↓

Phone Number Entered

↓

Verification Challenge Created

↓

OTP Verified

↓

Choose New Password

↓

Password Updated

↓

All Active Sessions Revoked

↓

User Logs In Again

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing user registration.

Registration is modeled as a temporary Registration Session. An Identity is created only after all required registration steps have been successfully completed.

docs.title: Registration Principles
docs.text:
The registration subsystem follows these principles:

  • Registration begins with a Registration Session.
  • Registration Sessions are temporary.
  • Identity is created only after successful completion.
  • Phone verification is mandatory.
  • Password is created only after phone verification.
  • Registration is fully auditable.

docs.title: Registration Architecture
docs.text:
User

↓

Registration Session

├── Phone Number
├── OTP Verification
├── Name
├── Email
├── Password
└── Expiration

↓

Identity Creation

↓

Active Identity

docs.title: Registration Session States
docs.text: State Description Started Registration initiated OTP Pending Waiting for phone verification Phone Verified OTP verification successful Profile Pending Waiting for profile information Password Pending Waiting for password creation Completed Identity created Expired Registration session expired Cancelled Registration abandoned

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every registration shall begin by creating a Registration Session.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Registration Session is temporary and shall not represent a platform Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall create an Identity only after the Registration Session reaches the Completed state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A valid mobile phone number is required to begin registration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Registration shall fail if the submitted phone number already belongs to an active Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The submitted phone number shall be verified using a One-Time Password (OTP) before registration may continue.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Profile information and password creation shall not be finalized until phone verification succeeds.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The following information is required before Identity creation:

  • Full Name
  • Phone Number
  • Email
  • Password

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users must provide an email address during registration.

Email is required for account creation but does not require verification in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A password shall be created only after successful phone verification.

The platform shall store only a secure password hash.

Plain-text passwords shall never be stored.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Registration Sessions shall automatically expire after the configured timeout period.

Expired sessions shall not create an Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall enforce configurable limits on OTP verification attempts.

Exceeded limits shall temporarily block further verification attempts for that Registration Session.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users may abandon registration at any time before Identity creation.

Cancelled Registration Sessions shall never create an Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only one active Registration Session may exist for the same phone number at any given time.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record significant registration events, including:

  • Registration started
  • OTP sent
  • OTP verified
  • OTP failed
  • Profile completed
  • Password created
  • Registration completed
  • Registration expired
  • Registration cancelled

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A newly created Identity shall enter the Active state immediately after successful registration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Successful registration shall generate a Notification Event according to the Notification Business Rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Registration Sessions shall never expose OTP values, password hashes, internal identifiers, or security-sensitive information.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Completed, expired, and cancelled Registration Sessions shall remain available for auditing according to the platform's data retention policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Registration Session shall be traceable to:

  • Phone Number
  • Verification Events
  • Identity (if created)
  • Notification Events
  • Audit History

docs.title: Registration Workflow
docs.text:
Registration Started

↓

Phone Number Entered

↓

OTP Sent

↓

OTP Verified

↓

Profile Completed

↓

Password Created

↓

Identity Created

↓

Registration Completed

If verification fails or the session expires, the workflow terminates without creating an Identity.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing authenticated user sessions within the Halal-Queue platform.

A Session represents an active authenticated connection between an Identity and the platform.

Sessions are independent security objects and are managed separately from Authentication Attempts.

docs.title: Session Principles
docs.text:
The session subsystem follows these principles:

  • Successful authentication creates a Session.
  • Sessions belong to exactly one Identity.
  • One Identity may have multiple active Sessions.
  • Sessions may be revoked independently.
  • Session activity is auditable.
  • Expired or revoked Sessions cannot access protected resources.

docs.title: Session Architecture
docs.text:
Identity

↓

Session Registry

├── Mobile Session

├── Web Session

├── Tablet Session

└── Other Device Sessions

↓

Authorization Check

↓

Application Access

docs.title: Session Lifecycle
docs.text:
Created

↓

Active

↓

Expired

OR

Revoked

OR

Logged Out

Terminal states:

  • Expired
  • Revoked
  • Logged Out

docs.title: Session States
docs.text: State Description Active Valid authenticated session Expired Session exceeded lifetime Revoked Session manually invalidated Logged Out User ended session

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A successful Authentication Attempt shall create a new Session.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Session shall belong to exactly one Identity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Session shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
An Identity may have multiple active Sessions simultaneously.

Examples:

  • Mobile application
  • Web browser
  • Tablet device

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Session shall record:

  • Session ID
  • Identity ID
  • Device Information
  • Created Timestamp
  • Last Activity Timestamp
  • Expiration Timestamp
  • Status

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Sessions may record:

  • Device Type
  • Operating System
  • Application Version
  • Browser Information
  • Device Identifier (where available)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Sessions shall automatically expire after the configured session lifetime.

Expired Sessions shall not access protected resources.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform may extend Session validity based on authenticated activity according to session policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Users may terminate an active Session through logout.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Users may revoke an individual Session without affecting other active Sessions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized security actions may revoke all active Sessions belonging to an Identity.

Examples:

  • Password reset
  • Account compromise
  • Administrative security action

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Revoked Sessions shall immediately lose access to protected resources.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Session Management shall remain independent of the underlying authentication token mechanism.

The platform may use:

  • JWT Tokens
  • Opaque Tokens
  • Other secure session technologies

without changing business rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Long-lived authentication credentials used to maintain sessions shall be securely managed.

Sensitive credentials shall never be stored in plain text.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Version 1 allows multiple concurrent Sessions unless restricted by security policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may monitor Sessions for:

  • Unusual activity
  • Excessive concurrent sessions
  • Suspicious device changes

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Sessions shall protect against:

  • Unauthorized reuse
  • Token theft
  • Session hijacking
  • Invalid access attempts

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record:

  • Session Created
  • Session Used
  • Session Expired
  • Session Revoked
  • Session Logged Out

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may view active Sessions for support and security purposes.

Administrators shall not access user authentication credentials.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users may view and manage their active Sessions where supported.

Future versions may provide:

  • Device list
  • Remote logout
  • Recent activity history

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Session shall be traceable to:

  • Identity
  • Authentication Attempt
  • Device Information
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This directory defines the business rules governing notifications throughout the Halal-Queue platform.

Notifications inform customers, vendors, administrators, and platform operators about significant business events. They are event-driven, auditable, and independent of the business workflows that generate them.

Notification generation, delivery, retry handling, and tracking are separated to improve reliability, maintainability, and future extensibility.

docs.title: Notification Domains
docs.text: Document Description notification-events.md Business events that generate notifications delivery-channels.md Delivery mechanisms and channel rules notification-preferences.md User notification settings templates.md Notification template management delivery-tracking.md Delivery status, retries, failures, and auditing

docs.title: Rule Prefix
docs.text:
All notification business rules use:

BR-NOT-###

Example:

BR-NOT-001
BR-NOT-002
BR-NOT-003

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
Business Event

        │

        ▼

Notification Event

        │

        ▼

Notification Service

        │

        ├──────── Push

        ├──────── Email

        ├──────── SMS

        ├──────── In-App

        └──────── Future Channels

        │

        ▼

Delivery Tracking

        │

        ▼

Audit History

docs.title: Notification Principles
docs.text:
The notification subsystem follows these principles:

  • Notifications are generated by business events.
  • Notification delivery is asynchronous.
  • Business transactions must not depend on notification delivery.
  • Every notification is auditable.
  • Failed deliveries may be retried.
  • Users control their notification preferences where applicable.
  • Critical operational notifications may override user preferences according to platform policy.
  • Notification content is template-driven.

docs.title: Notification Actors
docs.text:
Notifications may involve:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Vendor Staff
  • Administrator
  • Platform Operator
  • System

docs.title: Notification Lifecycle
docs.text:
Business Event

↓

Notification Created

↓

Queued

↓

Delivering

↓

Delivered

OR

Failed

↓

Retry

↓

Delivered

OR

Expired

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
Every notification shall be traceable to:

  • Business Event
  • Related Entity (Order, Vendor, Product, etc.)
  • Recipient
  • Delivery Channel
  • Delivery Status
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing notification delivery channels and channel routing.

Notification delivery is managed through a configurable Channel Routing Policy, allowing the platform to determine the appropriate delivery channels without embedding routing logic inside business modules or notification providers.

docs.title: Delivery Principles
docs.text:
The delivery subsystem follows these principles:

  • Notification generation is independent of delivery.
  • Channel selection is policy-driven.
  • Multiple delivery channels may be used.
  • Delivery channels operate independently.
  • Delivery failures do not affect business transactions.
  • Channel providers are replaceable.

docs.title: Delivery Architecture
docs.text:
Business Event

↓

Notification Event

↓

Channel Routing Policy

↓

Notification Delivery

├── Push

└── Future Channels

↓

Delivery Tracking

docs.title: Supported Channels
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Push Notification

Future versions may support:

  • In-App Notification
  • Email
  • SMS
  • WhatsApp
  • Telegram
  • Webhooks

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Event shall be evaluated by the Channel Routing Policy before delivery begins.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Channel Routing Policy shall determine the eligible delivery channels for each Notification Event.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Recipient notification preferences shall be considered during channel selection unless platform policy requires mandatory delivery.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Critical operational notifications may bypass recipient notification preferences.

Examples include:

  • Security alerts
  • Account recovery
  • Critical order updates
  • Platform policy notifications

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Notification Event may be delivered through one or more delivery channels.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each delivery channel shall operate independently.

Failure of one delivery shall not prevent attempts through other eligible channels.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Channel Routing Policy may define channel priority.

Example:

  1. Push Notification
  2. In-App Notification
  3. Email
  4. SMS

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If a higher-priority channel cannot deliver a notification, the platform may attempt delivery through lower-priority channels according to routing policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Delivery shall occur only through channels that are operational and properly configured.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Business rules shall not depend on any specific third-party notification provider.

Notification providers may be replaced without changing business behavior.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Push Notifications shall be used for timely mobile application alerts.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Email notifications shall be used for messages requiring permanent or detailed records.

Examples include:

  • Order confirmation
  • Account verification
  • Administrative communications

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: SMS notifications shall be reserved for high-value or time-sensitive communications when appropriate.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: In-App Notifications shall be available whenever the recipient is authenticated within the platform.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Channel Routing Policy may suppress non-critical notifications during recipient quiet hours.

Critical notifications may bypass quiet hour restrictions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notifications may be scheduled for future delivery when required by business rules or routing policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notifications shall not be delivered after their expiration time.

Expired notifications shall be recorded as expired.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification channels shall transmit only information appropriate for the selected delivery medium.

Sensitive information shall never be included in unsecured channels.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Channel Routing Policy shall prevent duplicate deliveries through the same delivery channel unless explicitly configured.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may temporarily disable one or more delivery channels for operational reasons.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may calculate channel metrics including:

  • Delivery success rate
  • Delivery latency
  • Failure rate
  • Channel usage
  • Average delivery time

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The notification architecture shall support additional delivery channels without requiring changes to business modules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every delivery attempt shall be traceable to:

  • Notification Event
  • Recipient
  • Delivery Channel
  • Routing Policy
  • Delivery Tracking Record

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing notification delivery, delivery status, retries, provider interaction, auditing, and operational monitoring.

Every delivery attempt is represented by an independent Notification Delivery entity.

A single Notification Event may generate multiple Notification Deliveries, each with its own lifecycle.

docs.title: Delivery Principles
docs.text:
The delivery tracking subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every delivery is independently tracked.
  • Delivery status is immutable once completed.
  • Each channel has its own delivery lifecycle.
  • Retry policies are channel-specific.
  • Provider failures do not affect business transactions.
  • Every delivery is fully auditable.

docs.title: Delivery Model
docs.text:
Notification Event

↓

Notification Deliveries

├── Push Delivery

├── Email Delivery

├── SMS Delivery

└── In-App Delivery

↓

Delivery History

↓

Operational Analytics

docs.title: Delivery Lifecycle
docs.text:
Queued

↓

Sending

├────────► Delivered

├────────► Failed

├────────► Expired

└────────► Retrying

Delivered, Failed, and Expired are terminal states.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every channel selected by the Channel Routing Policy shall create a separate Notification Delivery.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Delivery shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Delivery shall belong to exactly one Notification Event.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Notification Delivery shall reference exactly one delivery channel.

Examples include:

  • Push
  • Email
  • SMS
  • In-App

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Delivery shall begin in the Queued state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A queued delivery shall transition to Sending before communication with the delivery provider begins.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A successfully completed delivery shall transition to the Delivered state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Failed deliveries shall transition to the Failed state and record the failure reason.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Retry behavior shall follow the configured retry policy for the associated delivery channel.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each retry attempt shall create a new delivery attempt record while preserving previous attempts.

Retry attempts shall never overwrite historical data.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Deliveries exceeding their expiration time shall transition to the Expired state.

Expired deliveries shall not be retried.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Business rules shall remain independent of third-party notification providers.

Providers may be replaced without changing notification behavior.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record provider responses when available.

Examples include:

  • Provider Message ID
  • Delivery Timestamp
  • Error Code
  • Error Description

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every delivery shall record:

  • Queued time
  • Sending time
  • Completion time

where applicable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every state transition within the delivery lifecycle shall be permanently recorded.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall prevent duplicate deliveries through the same channel unless explicitly required by retry policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators shall be able to monitor active deliveries in real time.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized users may search Notification Deliveries using supported criteria, including:

  • Notification Event
  • Recipient
  • Channel
  • Delivery State
  • Date Range
  • Provider Message ID

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may calculate delivery metrics including:

  • Delivery Success Rate
  • Average Delivery Time
  • Retry Rate
  • Failure Rate
  • Expiration Rate
  • Channel Performance
  • Provider Performance

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may present operational dashboards showing:

  • Queue Depth
  • Active Deliveries
  • Failed Deliveries
  • Retry Activity
  • Provider Availability
  • Delivery Throughput

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Completed Notification Deliveries shall never be modified or deleted except in accordance with platform data retention policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Notification Delivery shall reference:

  • Notification Event
  • Business Event
  • Correlation ID

to support end-to-end tracing.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Delivery records shall never expose authentication secrets, provider credentials, encryption keys, or confidential internal configuration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The architecture shall support multiple providers for the same delivery channel.

Routing between providers shall be configurable without changes to business modules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Notification Delivery shall be traceable to:

  • Business Event
  • Notification Event
  • Recipient
  • Delivery Channel
  • Template Version
  • Provider Response
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing Notification Events.

A Notification Event is an immutable business object created whenever a significant platform event requires one or more recipients to be notified.

Notification Events are independent of delivery channels and business workflows.

docs.title: Notification Principles
docs.text:
The notification event system follows these principles:

  • Business modules never deliver notifications directly.
  • Business modules publish Notification Events.
  • Notification Events are immutable.
  • One Notification Event may generate multiple deliveries.
  • Notification Events are processed asynchronously.
  • Notification failures shall not affect business transactions.

docs.title: Notification Event Model
docs.text:
Business Event

↓

Notification Event

↓

Notification Service

↓

Delivery Channel

↓

Recipient

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every significant business event requiring user communication shall generate a Notification Event.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification Events shall never be modified after creation.

Corrections shall be represented by additional Notification Events.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Event shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Event shall reference exactly one originating business event.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Events shall include a Correlation ID linking all related business operations and notification deliveries.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Notification Event shall record its creation timestamp.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Notification Event shall have one priority level:

  • Critical
  • High
  • Normal
  • Low

Priority influences delivery order but not business logic.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Notification Event shall specify one or more recipients.

Supported recipients include:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Vendor Staff
  • Administrator
  • Platform Operator

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification Events shall contain the minimum information required to render notification content.

Payload data shall reference business entities rather than duplicate them whenever practical.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 Notification Events may originate from:

  • Order lifecycle
  • Order modifications
  • Preparation
  • Pickup
  • Cancellation
  • Catalog changes
  • Vendor onboarding
  • Account events
  • Administrative actions

Future modules may introduce additional event sources.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification Events shall be processed asynchronously by the Notification Service.

Business transactions shall not wait for notification delivery.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Events shall be placed into a processing queue before delivery begins.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A single Notification Event may produce multiple Notification Deliveries using different delivery channels.

  • Push Notification
  • Email

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Failure of one delivery channel shall not prevent delivery through other eligible channels.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall prevent duplicate Notification Events for the same business event unless explicitly permitted by platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Events may define an expiration time after which pending deliveries shall no longer be attempted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall permanently retain Notification Event records for auditing and operational analysis.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Customers shall only receive Notification Events relevant to their own account and activities.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Vendors shall receive Notification Events only for business entities they own or manage.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may access all Notification Events for support, auditing, and operational purposes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Events shall contribute to the historical timeline of related business entities where applicable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Events shall never contain sensitive credentials, authentication secrets, payment information, or confidential internal data.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may calculate metrics including:

  • Notifications generated
  • Notifications delivered
  • Notifications failed
  • Average processing time
  • Delivery latency
  • Channel usage

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Notification Event shall be traceable to:

  • Business Event
  • Business Entity
  • Recipient
  • Delivery Records
  • Audit History

↓

↓

↓

↓

↓
