docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing notification preferences for all platform users.

Each user owns a dedicated Notification Preference Profile that controls how and when notifications may be delivered. Preferences influence notification routing but do not override mandatory platform communications.

docs.title: Preference Principles
docs.text:
The notification preference subsystem follows these principles:

  • Preferences belong to a dedicated profile.
  • Every user owns one Notification Preference Profile.
  • Preferences are configurable by the user where permitted.
  • Mandatory notifications may bypass user preferences.
  • Preference changes are auditable.
  • Preference updates take effect immediately unless otherwise specified.

docs.title: Preference Model
docs.text:
User

↓

Notification Preference Profile

├── Push Preferences
├── Email Preferences
├── SMS Preferences
├── In-App Preferences
├── Quiet Hours
├── Language
├── Time Zone
├── Category Preferences
└── Audit History

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every platform user shall own exactly one Notification Preference Profile.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Notification Preference Profile shall belong to exactly one user.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall automatically create a default Notification Preference Profile when a new user account is created.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Approved preference changes shall become effective immediately for newly generated Notification Events.

Notifications already in delivery processing are not required to adopt updated preferences.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users may independently enable or disable supported notification channels, including:

  • Push Notifications
  • Email
  • SMS
  • In-App Notifications

Availability depends on supported platform features and verified contact information.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users may configure preferences independently for supported notification categories.

Version 1 categories include:

  • Orders
  • Pickup
  • Promotions
  • Account
  • Security
  • Platform Announcements

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The following categories cannot be disabled by users:

  • Security
  • Account Recovery
  • Legal Notices
  • Critical Order Status Changes
  • Platform Policy Notifications

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Users may configure quiet hours during which eligible non-critical notifications may be delayed.

Critical notifications may bypass quiet hours.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Quiet hour evaluation shall use the time zone configured in the Notification Preference Profile.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Notification Preference Profile shall define the user's preferred notification language.

Notification templates shall use the preferred language whenever available.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification delivery shall occur only through verified communication channels where verification is required.

Examples include:

  • Verified email address
  • Verified mobile number
  • Registered mobile device

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If a preferred delivery channel is unavailable, the Channel Routing Policy shall evaluate eligible fallback channels.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A user may register multiple devices for Push Notifications.

The platform may deliver notifications to one or more eligible devices according to routing policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification delivery behavior for multiple registered devices shall be configurable by platform policy.

Version 1 may deliver Push Notifications to all active registered devices.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall validate all preference changes before they become active.

Invalid combinations shall be rejected.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may temporarily override notification preferences only for operational, legal, security, or support purposes.

Administrative overrides shall be audited.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every preference modification shall record:

  • Previous value
  • New value
  • Timestamp
  • Actor
  • Reason (if applicable)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Users shall be able to view and manage their own Notification Preference Profile.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may view Notification Preference Profiles for support purposes.

Administrative modifications shall follow platform authorization policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Preference Profiles may be included in user data exports where permitted by applicable privacy policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Historical preference changes shall be retained according to the platform's data retention policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Notification Preference Profile shall remain associated with the originating user throughout the account lifecycle.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Notification Preference architecture shall support future capabilities including:

  • Per-vendor preferences
  • Per-device preferences
  • Digest notifications
  • Smart notification scheduling
  • AI-assisted delivery optimization
  • Temporary notification muting
  • Vacation mode

These capabilities are outside the scope of Version 1.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing Notification Templates.

Notification Templates are reusable, version-controlled content definitions used to render notifications for different business events and delivery channels.

Business logic shall never contain notification text directly.

docs.title: Template Principles
docs.text:
The Notification Template subsystem follows these principles:

  • Templates are independent of business logic.
  • Templates are reusable.
  • Templates support multiple delivery channels.
  • Templates are versioned.
  • Template rendering is deterministic.
  • Historical notifications preserve the rendered content that was delivered.

docs.title: Template Architecture
docs.text:
Business Event

↓

Notification Event

↓

Template Registry

↓

Template Rendering

↓

Rendered Notification

↓

Delivery Channel

docs.title: Template Components
docs.text:
Each Notification Template consists of:

  • Template Identifier
  • Business Event Type
  • Delivery Channel
  • Version
  • Subject (where applicable)
  • Title
  • Body
  • Placeholder Definitions
  • Status

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: All notification content shall originate from the Notification Template Registry.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Notification Template shall have a globally unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Notification Template shall be associated with one supported Notification Event type.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Different delivery channels may use different templates for the same Notification Event.

Example:

  • Push

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each template revision shall receive a new version.

Older versions shall remain available for historical reference.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Exactly one template version shall be active for a given combination of:

  • Business Event
  • Delivery Channel

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Templates may define placeholders to insert runtime business data.

Examples include:

  • {{order_number}}
  • {{vendor_name}}
  • {{customer_name}}
  • {{pickup_code}}
  • {{pickup_time}}
  • {{store_name}}

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall validate all required placeholders before rendering a notification.

Rendering shall fail if required placeholder values are unavailable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Notification rendering shall produce immutable output ready for delivery.

Subsequent template changes shall not modify previously rendered notifications.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Previously delivered notifications shall retain the rendered content that was actually delivered.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Templates may be activated or deactivated by authorized administrators.

Inactive templates shall not be selected for new Notification Events.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only authorized administrators may create, modify, activate, deactivate, or version Notification Templates.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Templates shall be validated before activation.

Validation shall include:

  • Placeholder integrity
  • Channel compatibility
  • Required fields

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Templates may support channel-specific capabilities, including:

  • Rich text
  • Images
  • Action buttons
  • Deep links

Support depends on the delivery channel.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification Templates shall not expose sensitive credentials, authentication secrets, payment information, or confidential internal data.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may preview rendered templates using sample data before activation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may collect template usage metrics including:

  • Delivery volume
  • Channel usage
  • Rendering failures

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Template Registry architecture shall support future capabilities including:

  • A/B testing
  • Dynamic personalization
  • Brand themes
  • Tenant-specific templates
  • Seasonal campaigns
  • AI-assisted content generation

These capabilities are outside the scope of Version 1.

This directory defines all business rules governing the complete order lifecycle within Halal-Queue.

It includes:

  • Order creation
  • Order lifecycle

  • Preparation workflow
  • Pickup verification
  • Cancellation

These rules define what the business requires. Implementation details are specified later in the Functional Requirements, APIs, and Technical Design documents.

docs.title: Ordering Principles
docs.text:
The ordering workflow follows these principles:

  • Every order belongs to exactly one vendor.
  • Every order has one current state.
  • State transitions must be valid.
  • Historical data is immutable.
  • Every significant action is auditable.
  • Customers are informed of important status changes.
  • Vendors control fulfillment.
  • Pickup verification is mandatory before completion.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing order cancellation within the Halal-Queue platform.

Rather than treating cancellation as a simple state transition, the platform models cancellation as a dedicated Cancellation Request. This preserves auditability, supports future approval workflows, and enables future payment and refund capabilities.

docs.title: Cancellation Principles
docs.text:
The cancellation workflow follows these principles:

  • Every cancellation is recorded.
  • Orders are never silently cancelled.
  • Every cancellation has an initiator.
  • Every cancellation has a business reason.
  • Cancellation history is immutable.
  • Completed orders cannot be cancelled.

docs.title: Cancellation Model
docs.text:
Order

↓

Cancellation Request

├── Customer Request

├── Vendor Request

├── Administrator Request

└── System Request

↓

Decision

↓

Cancelled

docs.title: Cancellation Request States
docs.text: State Description Pending Waiting for evaluation Approved Cancellation approved Rejected Cancellation denied Withdrawn Request withdrawn by requester

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every cancellation shall be represented by a dedicated Cancellation Request.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only one active Cancellation Request may exist for an order at any time.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Cancellation Request shall identify its initiator.

Supported initiators include:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Administrator
  • System

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Cancellation Request shall include a business reason.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Customers may request cancellation only while the order has not entered the Preparing state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may request cancellation when the order cannot be fulfilled due to operational or business reasons.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may cancel orders for policy enforcement, fraud prevention, legal compliance, or operational support.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The system may automatically create a Cancellation Request for predefined business conditions, including:

  • Modification request timeout
  • Vendor inactivity beyond configured limits
  • Platform maintenance (if applicable)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 automatically approves valid cancellation requests according to platform policy.

Future versions may introduce configurable approval workflows.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An approved Cancellation Request shall transition the associated order to the Cancelled state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Cancelled orders are terminal and shall not re-enter the order lifecycle.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Orders in the Completed state cannot be cancelled.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Orders with an approved Cancellation Request shall never enter the Pickup workflow.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If preparation has not yet started, all pending Preparation Tasks shall be cancelled automatically.

Completed Preparation Tasks remain part of the historical record.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record:

  • Initiator
  • Reason
  • Timestamp
  • Decision
  • Decision timestamp
  • Related order state

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers shall be notified whenever:

  • A cancellation request is submitted
  • A cancellation request is approved
  • A cancellation request is rejected

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Vendors shall receive notifications regarding cancellation events affecting their orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators shall be able to review all Cancellation Requests.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Cancellation Requests shall never be modified or deleted after completion.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Cancellation Request shall preserve sufficient information to support future refund processing, even though refunds are outside the scope of Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may generate operational metrics including:

  • Cancellation rate
  • Customer-initiated cancellations
  • Vendor-initiated cancellations
  • Automatic cancellations
  • Average cancellation time

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Cancellation Request shall be traceable to:

  • Parent Order
  • Active Revision
  • Vendor
  • Customer
  • Preparation Tasks
  • Audit History

docs.title: Cancellation Workflow
docs.text:
Cancellation Requested

↓

Validation

↓

Approved ─────────► Order Cancelled

OR

Rejected ─────────► Order Continues

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing historical order records and business events.

Halal-Queue maintains a permanent historical record of every order through immutable Order Events. These events provide a complete chronological timeline without changing the current order state.

docs.title: History Principles
docs.text:
The order history follows these principles:

  • Every significant business action generates an Order Event.
  • Order Events are immutable.
  • Events are chronological.
  • Events never replace the current order state.
  • Events support auditing, analytics, customer support, and reporting.

docs.title: Order History Model
docs.text:
Order

↓

Current State

↓

Order Events

├── Order Created
├── Submitted
├── Vendor Review Started
├── Accepted
├── Preparation Started
├── Preparation Completed
├── Ready for Pickup
├── Pickup Verified
├── Completed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every significant business action shall generate an Order Event.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Order Events shall never be modified or deleted after creation.

Corrections shall be represented by additional events.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Order Events shall be stored in chronological order based on their creation timestamp.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Order Event shall have a permanent unique identifier.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Order Event shall belong to exactly one order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall support the following event categories:

  • Order
  • Revision
  • Preparation
  • Pickup
  • Cancellation
  • Notification
  • Administrative

Additional categories may be introduced in future versions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Supported Version 1 event types include:

  • Order Created
  • Order Submitted
  • Vendor Review Started
  • Vendor Accepted
  • Vendor Rejected
  • Revision Created
  • Revision Accepted
  • Revision Rejected
  • Preparation Started
  • Preparation Completed
  • Ready for Pickup
  • Pickup Session Created
  • Verification Succeeded
  • Verification Failed
  • Pickup Completed
  • Cancellation Requested
  • Order Cancelled
  • Administrative Override

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Order Event shall record:

  • Event ID
  • Event Type
  • Timestamp
  • Related Order
  • Related Revision (if applicable)
  • Actor
  • Event Details

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every event shall identify the initiating actor.

Supported actors include:

  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Administrator
  • System

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Order Events shall accurately represent the chronological business history of the order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Historical events shall never alter the current business state of the order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers may view business-relevant events related to their own orders.

Internal operational events shall not be displayed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Vendors may view all events associated with their own orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may access the complete event history for any order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized users may search historical events using supported criteria, including:

  • Order Number
  • Date Range
  • Event Type
  • Vendor
  • Customer

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall support filtering Order Events by event category and event type.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Operational metrics may be generated from Order Events, including:

  • Order processing time
  • Vendor response time
  • Preparation duration
  • Pickup delay
  • Cancellation rate
  • Modification frequency

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Historical Order Events shall remain permanently associated with the originating order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized administrators may export Order History for reporting, auditing, and operational analysis, subject to applicable permissions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Notification events shall reference the business event that triggered them.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Order Event shall be traceable to:

  • Parent Order
  • Active Revision (if applicable)
  • Related Preparation Task (if applicable)
  • Pickup Session (if applicable)
  • Cancellation Request (if applicable)

docs.text:

09:22  Preparation Completed

09:23  Ready for Pickup

09:42  Pickup Completed

09:42  Order Completed

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing individual items within a customer order.

An Order Item represents a single product requested by the customer, including the requested quantity, agreed quantity, pricing, and fulfillment status.

Order Items are managed independently while remaining part of a single Order.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The Order Item subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every Order contains one or more Order Items.
  • Every Order Item references exactly one Product.
  • Each Order Item maintains its own lifecycle.
  • Changes to one Order Item do not automatically affect other Order Items.
  • Order Item history is preserved for auditing.

docs.title: Order Item Architecture
docs.text:
Order

├── Order Item
│     ├── Product
│     ├── Requested Quantity
│     ├── Approved Quantity
│     ├── Unit Price
│     ├── Line Total
│     ├── Status
│     └── Customer Note (Optional)
│
├── Pickup Details
└── Order Status

docs.title: Order Item Status
docs.text:
Each Order Item may have one of the following statuses.

Status Description Pending Awaiting vendor review Confirmed Vendor can fulfill the requested quantity Change Requested Vendor proposed a modification Cancelled Item cancelled Ready Item prepared for pickup Completed Item successfully picked up

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Order shall contain at least one Order Item.

Orders without Order Items are invalid.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Order Item shall reference exactly one Product.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Order Item shall record the quantity originally requested by the customer.

The requested quantity shall never be modified.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Order Item shall record the quantity approved for fulfillment.

Initially, the approved quantity equals the requested quantity.

If a customer accepts a Vendor Change Request, the approved quantity shall be updated.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Order Item shall store the unit price at the time the order is placed.

Later catalog price changes shall not affect existing orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Line Total shall equal:

Approved Quantity × Unit Price

The Line Total shall be recalculated whenever the approved quantity changes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Order Item maintains its own status independently of other Order Items.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A customer may cancel an affected Order Item through the Order Modification process.

Remaining Order Items continue normally.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may request changes to an individual Order Item.

Supported changes include:

  • Reduce quantity
  • Mark unavailable

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers may include an optional note for each Order Item.

Example:

Choose ripe bananas if available.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may provide a note when requesting changes to an Order Item.

Example:

Only two units are available today.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An Order Item reaches the Completed status only after the customer successfully collects the order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An Order shall be considered Completed only when all remaining Order Items are completed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record significant Order Item events, including:

  • Created
  • Quantity changed
  • Change requested
  • Customer accepted
  • Customer cancelled
  • Ready
  • Completed

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
Customer Order

Order #1001

Milk × 2
Bread × 1
Eggs × 12

Internally

Order

├── Item 1
│     Milk
│     Requested: 2
│     Approved: 2
│
├── Item 2
│     Bread
│     Requested: 1
│     Approved: 1
│
└── Item 3
      Eggs
      Requested: 12
      Approved: 12

docs.text:
Vendor cannot fulfill all milk.

Milk

Requested:
5

Approved:
2

Status:
Change Requested

Customer accepts.

Milk

Requested:
5

Approved:
2

Status:
Confirmed

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the complete lifecycle of an order within Halal-Queue.

Every order shall follow a controlled finite state machine (FSM). State transitions are strictly validated to ensure data integrity, predictable workflows, and consistent user experience.

docs.title: State Machine Principles
docs.text:
The order lifecycle shall comply with the following principles:

  • Every order has exactly one current state.
  • Every state transition shall be validated.
  • Invalid transitions shall be rejected.
  • Every transition shall be recorded in the audit log.
  • Historical transitions shall never be modified.
  • Every transition shall record the actor, timestamp, and reason (when applicable).

docs.title: Order State Machine
docs.text:
Cart

↓

Submitted

↓

Pending Vendor Review

├──────────────► Rejected

├──────────────► Awaiting Customer Decision

│                       │

│                       ├────► Rejected

│                       │

│                       └────► Accepted

│

└──────────────► Accepted

↓

Preparing

↓

Ready for Pickup

↓

Picked Up

↓

Completed

docs.title: Order States
docs.text: State Terminal Customer Visible Submitted No Yes Pending Vendor Review No Yes Awaiting Customer Decision No Yes Accepted No Yes Preparing No Yes Ready for Pickup No Yes Picked Up No Yes Completed Yes Yes Rejected Yes Yes Cancelled Yes Yes

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every order shall have a permanent unique identifier assigned at creation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every order shall receive a human-readable order number.

The order number shall remain unchanged throughout the order lifecycle.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every order shall belong to exactly one vendor.

Orders containing products from multiple vendors are not permitted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Immediately after successful checkout, an order shall enter the Submitted state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The system shall automatically transition a Submitted order to Pending Vendor Review after successful creation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
While an order is pending review, the vendor may:

  • Accept the order
  • Reject the order
  • Request modifications

No preparation activities shall begin in this state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may accept an order only if all requested products can be fulfilled.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A vendor may reject an order only for valid business reasons.

Examples include:

  • Store closed
  • Products unavailable
  • Operational issue

The rejection reason shall be recorded.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may request modifications instead of rejecting the order when only part of the order requires changes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
An order enters Awaiting Customer Decision when a modification request is submitted.

No preparation shall begin until the customer responds.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If the customer accepts the proposed modifications, the order shall transition to Accepted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If the customer rejects the proposed modifications, the order shall transition to Rejected unless another business rule applies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Accepted orders are ready to begin preparation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor shall explicitly transition an Accepted order into Preparing when preparation begins.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may transition an order to Ready for Pickup only after all products have been prepared.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An order shall not transition to Picked Up until successful pickup verification has occurred.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
After successful pickup confirmation, the order shall transition to Completed.

Completed orders are immutable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The following states are terminal:

  • Completed
  • Rejected
  • Cancelled

Terminal orders cannot re-enter the workflow.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The system shall reject all state transitions that are not explicitly permitted by the finite state machine.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only authorized actors may perform state transitions.

State Transition Actor Submitted → Pending Vendor Review System Pending Vendor Review → Accepted Vendor Pending Vendor Review → Rejected Vendor Pending Vendor Review → Awaiting Customer Decision Vendor Awaiting Customer Decision → Accepted Customer Awaiting Customer Decision → Rejected Customer Accepted → Preparing Vendor Preparing → Ready for Pickup Vendor Ready for Pickup → Picked Up Vendor (after verification) Picked Up → Completed System

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every successful state transition shall record:

  • Previous state
  • New state
  • Timestamp
  • Actor
  • Reason (if applicable)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every customer-visible state transition shall trigger the appropriate notification according to the Notification Business Rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The timestamp of each state transition shall be preserved permanently for audit and reporting purposes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Order state history shall never be edited or deleted.

Corrections shall be represented as new events rather than modifying historical records.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
At any point in time, an order shall exist in exactly one valid state.

Concurrent or conflicting states are not permitted.

docs.title: State Transition Matrix
docs.text: Current State Allowed Next States Submitted Pending Vendor Review Pending Vendor Review Accepted, Rejected, Awaiting Customer Decision Awaiting Customer Decision Accepted, Rejected Accepted Preparing Preparing Ready for Pickup Ready for Pickup Picked Up Picked Up Completed Completed — Rejected — Cancelled —

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules for modifying customer orders after they have been placed.

Order modifications occur when a Vendor cannot completely fulfill an order as originally requested.

The original customer order is never overwritten. Instead, the Vendor submits an Order Change Request for customer approval.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The Order Modification subsystem follows these principles:

  • The original order remains unchanged.
  • Vendors cannot modify confirmed customer orders without customer approval.
  • Customers always decide whether to accept proposed changes.
  • Every modification is recorded for audit purposes.
  • Order history remains complete and traceable.

docs.title: Order Modification Architecture
docs.text:
Customer Order

↓

Vendor Review

↓

Order Change Request

↓

Customer Decision

├── Accept Changes
├── Reject Changes
└── Cancel Order

docs.title: Supported Vendor Modifications
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Mark ordered item as unavailable
  • Reduce ordered quantity
  • Add an explanation for the customer

Version 1 does not support:

  • Increasing quantity
  • Replacing products
  • Adding new products
  • Changing product prices

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Vendor shall submit an Order Change Request instead of directly modifying a customer order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Order modifications shall require customer approval before becoming effective.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The original customer order shall remain unchanged until the customer accepts the proposed changes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If an ordered product is unavailable, the Vendor may mark that item as unavailable in the Order Change Request.

The Vendor shall provide a reason for the change.

Examples:

  • Product unavailable
  • Supplier delay
  • Product damaged
  • Product recalled

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may reduce the quantity of an ordered product when the full requested quantity cannot be fulfilled.

Example:

Original:

Milk × 5

Requested Change:

Milk × 2

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Order Change Request shall include a customer-visible explanation.

Example:

"Only 2 units are available today."

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
When an Order Change Request is received, the customer may:

  • Accept all proposed changes
  • Cancel the affected item(s)
  • Cancel the entire order

Partial acceptance of individual proposed changes is not supported in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: When the customer accepts the Order Change Request, the platform shall update the order using the approved changes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If the customer removes the affected item(s), the remaining order shall continue if at least one order item remains.

If no order items remain, the order shall be cancelled.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The customer may cancel the complete order after receiving an Order Change Request.

The order shall transition to the Cancelled state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Vendor shall be notified of the customer's decision.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The customer shall receive a notification whenever an Order Change Request is submitted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may include multiple item changes within a single Order Change Request.

Example:

  • Milk reduced from 5 to 2
  • Eggs marked unavailable

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Order modifications are permitted only before the Vendor marks the order as Ready for Pickup.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record:

  • Original order values
  • Proposed changes
  • Vendor explanation
  • Customer decision
  • Timestamp
  • Initiating Identity

docs.title: Example 1 — Quantity Reduction
docs.text:
Customer Order

Milk × 5
Bread × 1

Vendor Request

Milk × 2

Reason:
Only 2 units are available today.

Customer Decision

Accept

Final Order

Milk × 2
Bread × 1

docs.title: Example 2 — Product Unavailable
docs.text:
Customer Order

Eggs × 1
Milk × 2

Vendor Request

Eggs

Unavailable

Reason:
Supplier delivery delayed.

Customer Decision

Remove Eggs

Final Order

Milk × 2

docs.title: Example 3 — Order Cancelled
docs.text:
Customer Order

Milk × 2
Eggs × 1

Vendor Request

Milk unavailable
Eggs unavailable

Customer Decision

Cancel Order

Final Order Status

Cancelled

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the generation, uniqueness, format, lifecycle, and usage of Business Order Numbers.

A Business Order Number is the public identifier used by customers, vendors, administrators, customer support, receipts, notifications, and reports.

The Business Order Number is independent of the internal database identifier.

docs.title: Numbering Principles
docs.text:
The Business Order Number follows these principles:

  • Human-readable
  • Globally unique
  • Permanent
  • Searchable
  • Immutable
  • Independent of database IDs

docs.title: Business Identifier Model
docs.text:
Database ID

↓

Business Order Number

↓

Customer
Vendor
Support
Reports
Receipts
Notifications

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every order shall receive a Business Order Number when the order is successfully created.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The internal database identifier shall never be exposed to customers or vendors.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Business Order Number shall be globally unique across the platform.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Once assigned, a Business Order Number shall never change.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Business Order Number shall be used in all customer-facing and vendor-facing communications.

Examples include:

  • Order confirmation
  • Pickup screen
  • QR code metadata
  • Notifications
  • Email
  • SMS
  • Printed receipt
  • Customer support

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized users shall be able to locate an order using its Business Order Number.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Business Order Number shall be generated immediately after successful order creation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If Business Order Number generation fails, the order creation process shall fail and no partial order shall be created.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 uses the following format:

HQ-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN

Example:

HQ-20260728-000123

Future versions may introduce configurable numbering formats without affecting existing order numbers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The numeric sequence shall increase monotonically according to the platform's numbering strategy.

Gaps in numbering are acceptable if they result from failed or rolled-back transactions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Business Order Numbers shall avoid ambiguous characters and formatting that may confuse users.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each QR code generated for pickup shall reference the Business Order Number.

The QR code may include additional secure metadata as required by the platform.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Receipts, invoices, order summaries, and pickup confirmations shall display the Business Order Number.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Business Order Numbers shall remain permanently associated with their originating orders, including archived, rejected, cancelled, and completed orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Business Order Numbers may be used as report references but shall not be interpreted as indicators of business volume or transaction sequencing beyond their intended purpose.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
External systems integrating with Halal-Queue may reference orders using the Business Order Number.

Internal database identifiers shall not be required.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Business Order Number shall be traceable to:

  • Internal Order ID
  • Order Events
  • Active Revision
  • Pickup Session
  • Cancellation Request
  • Audit History

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Internal ID

845932

↓

Business Order Number

HQ-20260728-000123

The internal identifier is used only by the platform.

The Business Order Number is used by all users and external integrations.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing order preparation after an order has been accepted.

Preparation is modeled as a separate operational process. Every accepted order generates one or more Preparation Tasks, allowing the platform to support both simple and advanced fulfillment workflows.

docs.title: Preparation Principles
docs.text:
The preparation workflow follows these principles:

  • Preparation begins only after the order is accepted.
  • Every preparation task belongs to one order.
  • Preparation tasks are immutable once completed.
  • Every task has its own lifecycle.
  • Orders become ready for pickup only after all preparation tasks are completed.
  • Preparation activities shall be fully auditable.

docs.title: Preparation Model
docs.text:
Order

↓

Active Revision

↓

Preparation Tasks

├── Task 1

├── Task 2

└── Task N

↓

Ready for Pickup

Version 1 normally creates a single preparation task, but the architecture supports multiple tasks in future releases.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only an order in the Accepted state may begin preparation.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: When preparation begins, the platform shall create one or more Preparation Tasks associated with the Active Revision.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Preparation Task shall belong to exactly one order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Preparation Tasks shall always reference the currently Active Revision.

Historical revisions shall never generate preparation tasks.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Preparation Task shall exist in one of the following states:

  • Pending
  • In Progress
  • Completed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may transition a Preparation Task from Pending to In Progress.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A vendor may mark a Preparation Task as Completed only after all assigned work has finished.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Completed Preparation Tasks shall not be modified.

Corrections shall be recorded as separate operational events.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An order shall become eligible for the Ready for Pickup state only when every associated Preparation Task has been completed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Before transitioning an order to Ready for Pickup, the platform shall verify that no Preparation Task remains Pending or In Progress.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only the owning vendor may manage Preparation Tasks for its orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may view Preparation Tasks for operational monitoring and support.

Administrative modification of tasks shall be restricted according to platform permissions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers shall not see individual Preparation Tasks.

Customers shall only see the overall order status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record:

  • Preparation start time
  • Preparation completion time
  • Responsible actor

for every Preparation Task.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall permanently retain the complete history of Preparation Task events.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: If preparation cannot be completed due to an operational issue, the vendor shall follow the order cancellation or support workflow rather than altering completed preparation records.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendors may record internal preparation notes.

Internal notes shall never be visible to customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Preparation Tasks may optionally be assigned to one or more staff members.

This capability is reserved for future platform versions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Multiple Preparation Tasks may execute concurrently if supported by future operational workflows.

Version 1 typically uses a single task.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Preparation Tasks may define execution dependencies.

A dependent task shall not begin until all prerequisite tasks have been completed.

Version 1 does not require task dependencies but the architecture shall support them.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall reject any attempt to mark an order as Ready for Pickup if at least one Preparation Task remains incomplete.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: When all Preparation Tasks are completed and the order transitions to Ready for Pickup, the customer shall be notified according to the Notification Business Rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Historical Preparation Tasks shall remain permanently associated with the order and shall never be reassigned to another order or revision.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Preparation metrics may be calculated using Preparation Task timestamps, including:

  • Preparation start delay
  • Preparation duration
  • Average preparation time
  • Vendor fulfillment performance

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Preparation Task shall be traceable to:

  • Parent Order
  • Active Revision
  • Vendor
  • Responsible actor(s)
  • Audit history

docs.title: Preparation State Machine
docs.text:
Pending

↓

In Progress

↓

Completed

Completed is a terminal state.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the valid lifecycle states and transitions for customer orders.

The Order State Machine ensures every order follows a predictable and valid workflow from placement through completion or cancellation.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The Order State Machine follows these principles:

  • Every order has exactly one current status.
  • Orders may transition only through approved state changes.
  • Invalid transitions are prohibited.
  • All state transitions are recorded.
  • Terminal states cannot transition to another state.

docs.title: Order States
docs.text: State Description Pending Customer submitted the order; awaiting vendor review Confirmed Vendor accepted the order Change Requested Vendor requested customer approval for changes Preparing Vendor is preparing the order Ready for Pickup Order is ready for collection Completed Customer collected the order Cancelled Order cancelled

docs.title: Valid State Transitions
docs.text: Current State Allowed Next States Pending Confirmed, Cancelled Confirmed Preparing, Change Requested, Cancelled Change Requested Confirmed, Cancelled Preparing Ready for Pickup, Cancelled Ready for Pickup Completed Completed None Cancelled None

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every newly created order shall begin in the Pending state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only the Vendor may transition an order from Pending to Confirmed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If order changes are required, the Vendor shall transition the order to Change Requested.

The order shall remain in this state until the customer responds.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
After receiving a customer response:

  • Accept changes → Confirmed
  • Cancel order → Cancelled

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only confirmed orders may transition to Preparing.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only preparing orders may transition to Ready for Pickup.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only ready-for-pickup orders may transition to Completed after successful pickup verification.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Orders may be cancelled before pickup completion.

Completed orders cannot be cancelled.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Completed and Cancelled are terminal states.

No further transitions are permitted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall reject any state transition not explicitly defined in this document.

Examples:

Invalid:

Pending
    ↓
Completed

Invalid:

Preparing
    ↓
Pending

Invalid:

Completed
    ↓
Preparing

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every state transition shall record:

  • Previous state
  • New state
  • Timestamp
  • Initiating user
  • Optional reason

docs.title: Example Order Lifecycle
docs.text:
Pending

↓

Confirmed

↓

Preparing

↓

Ready for Pickup

↓

Completed

docs.title: Example With Change Request
docs.text:
Pending

↓

Confirmed

↓

Change Requested

↓

Confirmed

↓

Preparing

↓

Ready for Pickup

↓

Completed

docs.text:
Pending

↓

Confirmed

↓

Cancelled

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the pickup process for customer orders.

A Pickup represents the fulfillment stage where a customer collects a prepared order from the selected Vendor Branch.

Every confirmed order has exactly one Pickup and one Pickup Code used for verification.

docs.title: Pickup Principles
docs.text:
The Pickup subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every confirmed order has exactly one Pickup.
  • Every Pickup has exactly one Pickup Code.
  • Pickup begins only after the order is marked Ready for Pickup.
  • Pickup verification is required before completing an order.
  • Pickup Codes are unique and single-use.
  • Completed pickups cannot be reversed.
  • Pickup events are auditable.

docs.title: Pickup Architecture
docs.text:
Order
    │
    ▼
Pickup

├── Pickup Code
├── Pickup Status
├── Ready At
├── Collected At
├── Verified By
└── Audit History

docs.title: Pickup Status
docs.text: Status Description Pending Order is being processed and is not ready for pickup Ready Order is prepared and waiting for customer pickup In Progress Vendor is verifying the Pickup Code Completed Customer successfully collected the order Cancelled Order was cancelled before pickup

docs.title: Pickup Code
docs.text:
Version 1 uses a six-digit numeric Pickup Code.

Example:

483921

The Pickup Code is generated automatically when an order is confirmed.

The Pickup Code:

  • Is unique
  • Is visible to the customer
  • Is required for pickup verification
  • Can only be used once
  • Expires after successful pickup or order cancellation

Future versions may additionally support:

  • QR Code
  • Barcode

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Pickup record shall be created automatically when an order is confirmed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall automatically generate a unique six-digit Pickup Code for every Pickup.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The customer shall be able to view the Pickup Code from the Order Details screen.

The Pickup Code shall not be displayed to other customers.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may mark an order as Ready for Pickup only after all remaining Order Items have been prepared.

When an order becomes Ready:

  • Pickup Status becomes Ready
  • Customer is notified
  • Pickup Code becomes active

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Before releasing an order, the Vendor shall verify the customer's Pickup Code.

Only a valid Pickup Code allows the order to be collected.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
If an invalid Pickup Code is entered:

  • The order shall not be released.
  • Pickup Status remains Ready.
  • The customer may retry with the correct code.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
After successful Pickup Code verification:

  • Pickup Status becomes Completed.
  • Order Status becomes Completed.
  • Pickup Code becomes invalid.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Pickup Code remains valid until:

  • The order is successfully collected, or
  • The order is cancelled.

Expired Pickup Codes cannot be reused.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Pickup Code may be successfully verified only once.

After successful verification, the code shall become permanently invalid.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The platform shall record the date and time when the customer collects the order.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Cancelled orders shall have a Pickup Status of Cancelled.

Cancelled orders cannot be collected.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The customer shall receive notifications when:

  • The order is Ready for Pickup.
  • The order has been collected.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only authorized Vendor users may:

  • Mark an order Ready for Pickup.
  • Verify the Pickup Code.
  • Complete the Pickup.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall record:

  • Pickup created
  • Pickup Code generated
  • Order marked Ready
  • Successful pickup
  • Pickup cancelled
  • Verification timestamp

Failed verification attempts may be recorded for operational monitoring.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Pickup shall be traceable to:

  • Order
  • Customer
  • Vendor
  • Branch
  • Pickup Code
  • Audit History

docs.title: Example Pickup Flow
docs.text:
Customer Places Order

↓

Order Confirmed

↓

Pickup Created

↓

Pickup Code Generated

↓

Vendor Prepares Order

↓

Ready for Pickup

↓

Customer Arrives

↓

Customer Shows Pickup Code

↓

Vendor Verifies Pickup Code

↓

Order Collected

↓

Pickup Completed

↓

Pickup Code Expired

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines how product availability impacts the ordering process.

docs.title: BR-ORD-AVL-001 — Checkout Validation
docs.text: Statement: Before an order is finalized and payment is captured, the system must perform a real-time availability check on all items in the customer's cart.

docs.title: BR-ORD-AVL-002 — Out of Stock Resolution
docs.text: Statement: If an item in the cart becomes Unavailable between the time it was added to the cart and the time of checkout, the checkout process must be blocked, and the customer must be prompted to remove or modify the unavailable item.

docs.title: BR-ORD-AVL-003 — Variation Option Availability
docs.text: Statement: An item is considered unavailable if the vendor marks the entire product as Unavailable, OR if the specific variation option (e.g., "Large Cut") chosen by the customer has been disabled by the vendor.

docs.title: BR-ORD-AVL-004 — Daily Auto-Restock
docs.text: Statement: If an item was manually marked as Unavailable by a vendor today, the system assumes this is a temporary daily shortage. The item will be automatically reset to Active/Available at the start of the vendor's next business day unless explicitly archived.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This directory defines the business rules governing vendors within the Halal-Queue platform.

A Vendor represents a business that offers halal food products or services through the platform. Vendor Management covers the complete lifecycle of a vendor, including onboarding, business profile management, branch operations, staff administration, service availability, halal verification, operational status, and auditing.

Vendor Management is independent of Authentication, Ordering, and Catalog Management, but integrates with each through well-defined business interfaces.

docs.title: Vendor Principles
docs.text:
The Vendor Management subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every Vendor represents one business entity.
  • Every Vendor has one Business Profile.
  • A Vendor may operate one or more Branches.
  • Vendor Staff operate only within their assigned Vendor.
  • Vendor ownership and business resources are isolated from other Vendors.
  • Vendor actions are fully auditable.
  • Vendor lifecycle is managed independently from user identities.

docs.title: Vendor Domains
docs.text: Document Description vendor-lifecycle.md Vendor onboarding, activation, suspension, closure business-profile.md Business identity and profile information branch-management.md Physical branches and locations operating-hours.md Business and branch opening hours staff-management.md Vendor staff assignment and management service-areas.md Delivery or pickup service coverage halal-verification.md Halal certification and verification vendor-documents.md Business documents and supporting records vendor-status.md Operational status and availability vendor-audit.md Vendor audit and operational history

docs.title: Rule Prefix
docs.text:
All Vendor Management rules use:

BR-VENDOR-###

Example:

BR-VENDOR-001
BR-VENDOR-002
BR-VENDOR-003

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
Platform

↓

Vendor

├── Business Profile
├── Branches
├── Operating Hours
├── Staff
├── Catalog
├── Orders
├── Service Areas
├── Halal Verification
├── Documents
├── Status
└── Audit History

docs.title: Vendor Scope
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Single business ownership
  • One or more physical branches
  • Vendor-managed staff
  • Pickup orders
  • Halal verification records
  • Business profile management
  • Operational status management

Future versions may support:

  • Franchise organizations
  • Corporate groups
  • Shared management teams
  • Cross-branch inventory
  • Multi-brand businesses

docs.title: Ownership Model
docs.text:
A Vendor owns:

  • Business Profile
  • Branches
  • Products
  • Categories
  • Orders (business context)
  • Vendor Staff
  • Operating Hours
  • Service Areas
  • Business Documents

Platform Administrators manage platform governance but do not become owners of vendor resources.

docs.title: Integration Points
docs.text:
Vendor Management integrates with:

  • Authentication (Vendor Identity)
  • Authorization (Vendor Roles & Permissions)
  • Catalog Management (Products & Categories)
  • Ordering (Order Fulfillment)
  • Notifications (Operational Alerts)
  • Audit & Compliance

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
Vendor records shall be traceable to:

  • Vendor Identity
  • Business Profile
  • Branches
  • Staff
  • Orders
  • Documents
  • Halal Verification
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing Vendor Branches within the Halal-Queue platform.

A Branch represents a physical operating location where customer orders are prepared, fulfilled, and collected.

Branches are first-class business entities with their own operational configuration, staff, operating hours, and lifecycle.

docs.title: Branch Principles
docs.text:
The Branch subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every Branch belongs to exactly one Vendor.
  • Every Vendor may own one or more Branches.
  • Every customer order belongs to exactly one Branch.
  • Branches operate independently.
  • Branch lifecycle is independent from Vendor lifecycle.
  • Branch operations are fully auditable.

docs.title: Branch Architecture
docs.text:
Vendor

↓

Branch

├── Branch ID
├── Branch Name
├── Address
├── Geographic Location
├── Operating Hours
├── Staff
├── Orders
├── Status
└── Audit History

docs.title: Branch Lifecycle
docs.text:
Created

↓

Configured

↓

Operational

↓

Temporarily Closed

↓

Operational

↓

Permanently Closed

docs.title: Branch Status
docs.text: Status Description Created Branch record created Configured Initial setup completed Operational Accepting customer orders Temporarily Closed Closed for a limited period Permanently Closed No longer operates

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Branch shall belong to exactly one Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall have a globally unique Branch ID.

The Branch ID is immutable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may own one or more Branches.

Version 1 supports both:

  • Single-branch Vendors
  • Multi-branch Vendors

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall define a human-readable Branch Name.

Examples:

  • Dhanmondi Branch
  • Banani Branch
  • Main Kitchen

Branch Names are unique only within the same Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall maintain a complete physical address.

Address information shall support customer navigation, pickup, and administrative operations.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall maintain geographic coordinates.

Coordinates are used for:

  • Map display
  • Distance calculation
  • Nearby vendor discovery
  • Future delivery features

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Branch shall maintain its own operational configuration.

Examples include:

  • Operating Hours
  • Staff
  • Order Queue
  • Operational Status

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every customer order shall be assigned to exactly one Branch.

Orders shall never belong directly to a Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch may determine the availability of products offered by its Vendor.

Version 1 uses a shared Vendor catalog.

Future versions may support branch-specific availability.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendor Staff shall be assigned to one or more Branches.

Staff permissions apply only within assigned Branches.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall maintain its own Operating Hours.

Operating Hours are defined in the Operating Hours Business Rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Each Branch shall maintain its own operational status independently of other Branches.

Closing one Branch shall not affect the operation of other Branches belonging to the same Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch may be temporarily closed for operational reasons.

Examples include:

  • Maintenance
  • Public holidays
  • Equipment failure
  • Staff shortage

Temporarily closed Branches shall not accept new orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch may be permanently closed.

Historical business data associated with the Branch shall remain available for auditing and reporting.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only Operational Branches shall be displayed as available for new customer orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Before becoming Operational, a Branch shall have:

  • Address configured
  • Geographic coordinates configured
  • Operating Hours configured
  • Operational Status configured

Additional requirements may be introduced by platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record significant Branch events including:

  • Branch created
  • Branch updated
  • Branch opened
  • Branch temporarily closed
  • Branch reopened
  • Branch permanently closed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Authorized Vendor Owners and Administrators may create, update, suspend, or close Branches according to platform authorization rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Operational events affecting one Branch shall not automatically affect other Branches belonging to the same Vendor unless explicitly configured by platform policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Branch shall be traceable to:

  • Vendor
  • Business Profile
  • Operating Hours
  • Assigned Staff
  • Orders
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the Business Profile of a Vendor.

A Business Profile contains the public information displayed to customers about a Vendor. It represents how the business appears within the Halal-Queue platform while remaining independent from the Vendor's internal identity.

The Business Profile is intended for customer discovery, trust, and communication.

docs.title: Business Profile Principles
docs.text:
The Business Profile subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every Vendor owns exactly one Business Profile.
  • The Business Profile is customer-facing.
  • Legal business information is separated from branding information.
  • Branding updates shall not affect Vendor identity.
  • Business Profile changes are auditable.

docs.title: Business Profile Architecture
docs.text:
Vendor

↓

Business Profile

├── Business Identity
├── Contact Information
├── Branding
├── Store Attributes
├── Store Categories
├── Supported Services
└── Audit History

docs.title: Business Identity
docs.text:
Business Identity contains official business information.

Fields include:

  • Legal Business Name
  • Display Name
  • Business Registration Number (optional)
  • Business Type

docs.title: Contact Information
docs.text:
Business contact information includes:

  • Primary Phone Number
  • Email Address (optional)
  • Website (optional)

This information is used for customer communication and platform administration.

docs.title: Branding
docs.text:
Branding defines how the Vendor appears to customers.

Fields include:

  • Logo
  • Cover Image
  • Short Description
  • Full Description

Branding content shall comply with platform content policies.

docs.title: Store Attributes
docs.text:
Store Attributes help customers understand the business.

Examples include:

  • Open 24 Hours
  • Air Conditioned
  • Wheelchair Accessible
  • Parking Available
  • Family Friendly

Platform administrators manage the available attribute list.

docs.title: Store Categories
docs.text:
Store Categories classify Vendors for browsing and search.

Examples include:

  • Supermarket
  • Grocery Store
  • Convenience Store
  • Organic Grocery
  • Wholesale Store
  • Specialty Foods
  • Bakery
  • Pharmacy (Future)

A Vendor may belong to multiple categories.

docs.title: Supported Services
docs.text:
Supported Services indicate which fulfillment methods are offered.

Version 1 supports:

  • Pickup

Future versions may include:

  • Delivery
  • Scheduled Pickup
  • Curbside Pickup

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Business Profile shall belong to exactly one Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Each Vendor shall maintain exactly one Business Profile.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Business Profile shall define a customer-visible Display Name.

Display Names are not required to match the Legal Business Name.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Legal Business Name shall represent the officially registered business where applicable.

This information is used for administrative and legal purposes.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Updating branding information shall not modify Vendor identity, ownership, or operational status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Business Profile shall define at least one primary contact phone number.

Email address and website are optional in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may publish an official website.

Website URLs shall be validated before publication.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Operational Vendor shall publish a logo.

Uploaded media shall comply with platform media policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may publish one or more cover images.

Version 1 displays a single primary cover image.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may publish:

  • Short Description
  • Full Description

Descriptions shall comply with platform content policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Store Attributes shall be selected from platform-managed values.

Free-text attribute creation is not permitted in Version 1.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may belong to one or more Store Categories.

Categories are managed by platform administrators.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Business Profile shall accurately reflect the services offered by the Vendor.

Version 1 supports Pickup only.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only approved Business Profile information shall be visible to customers.

Internal administrative information shall never be publicly displayed.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Vendor shall complete all mandatory Business Profile fields before becoming Operational.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Platform administrators may review Business Profile content to ensure compliance with platform policies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record significant Business Profile changes, including:

  • Display Name updated
  • Logo changed
  • Contact information updated
  • Branding updated
  • Store Categories changed
  • Store Attributes changed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform may retain historical Business Profile versions for auditing purposes.

Version 1 records audit events but does not expose profile version history through the user interface.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Published Business Profile information may be indexed for customer search and discovery.

Only publicly visible information shall be searchable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Business Profile shall be traceable to:

  • Vendor
  • Owner Identity
  • Administrative Actions
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the operating schedule of Vendor Branches.

Operating Hours determine when a Branch is available to receive, prepare, and fulfill customer orders.

The platform separates the regular weekly schedule from temporary and exceptional schedules to provide operational flexibility.

docs.title: Operating Schedule Principles
docs.text:
The Operating Schedule subsystem follows these principles:

  • Every Branch has exactly one Operating Schedule.
  • The Operating Schedule belongs to exactly one Branch.
  • Weekly schedules and exceptions are managed independently.
  • Temporary schedule changes do not permanently modify the weekly schedule.
  • Operating decisions are based on the effective schedule at the current date and time.
  • All schedule changes are auditable.

docs.title: Operating Schedule Architecture
docs.text:
Branch

↓

Operating Schedule

├── Weekly Schedule
├── Holiday Exceptions
├── Temporary Closures
├── Special Opening Hours
├── Time Zone
└── Audit History

docs.title: Weekly Schedule
docs.text:
The Weekly Schedule defines the normal operating hours for each day of the week.

Each day may be configured as:

  • Closed
  • Open for one continuous period
  • Open for multiple operating periods

Examples:

Monday

  • 10:00–15:00
  • 17:00–22:00

Tuesday

  • Closed

Wednesday

  • 09:00–22:00

docs.title: Holiday Exceptions
docs.text:
Holiday Exceptions temporarily override the Weekly Schedule for specific dates.

Examples:

  • Eid-ul-Fitr
  • Eid-ul-Adha
  • National holidays
  • Vendor-declared holidays

Holiday Exceptions apply only to the specified date.

docs.title: Temporary Closures
docs.text:
Temporary Closures suspend branch operations for a defined period.

Examples:

  • Equipment maintenance
  • Staff shortage
  • Power outage
  • Emergency situations

During a Temporary Closure, the Branch shall not accept new customer orders.

docs.title: Special Opening Hours
docs.text:
Special Opening Hours temporarily replace the Weekly Schedule.

Examples:

  • Ramadan schedule
  • Promotional campaigns
  • Festival events
  • Extended business hours

Special Opening Hours override the Weekly Schedule only for their configured period.

docs.title: Time Zone
docs.text:
Every Operating Schedule shall define the time zone used for schedule calculations.

Version 1 supports multiple time zones to accommodate branches across different regions.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Operating Schedule shall belong to exactly one Branch.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Operational Branch shall maintain an Operating Schedule.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: The Weekly Schedule shall define operating hours for each day of the week.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Branches may designate any day as Closed.

Closed days shall not accept new customer orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch may define multiple operating periods within the same day.

Example:

  • Lunch service
  • Dinner service

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Holiday Exceptions shall override the Weekly Schedule for the affected dates.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Temporary Closures shall override all other schedules for their effective duration.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Special Opening Hours shall temporarily replace the Weekly Schedule during their configured validity period.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall determine Branch availability using the following priority:

  1. Temporary Closure
  2. Holiday Exception
  3. Special Opening Hours
  4. Weekly Schedule

The first applicable rule determines the effective operating state.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Branches shall accept new customer orders only while operational according to the effective schedule.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Schedule changes shall not automatically cancel customer orders already accepted.

Order handling after closure follows operational policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Operating periods shall not overlap within the same schedule type.

The platform shall validate schedule consistency before publication.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Changes to Operating Schedules become effective according to their configured activation date and time.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only authorized Vendor Owners, permitted Vendor Staff, or Platform Administrators may modify Operating Schedules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record significant schedule events including:

  • Weekly Schedule updated
  • Holiday Exception added
  • Temporary Closure created
  • Temporary Closure removed
  • Special Opening Hours configured

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Operating Schedule shall be traceable to:

  • Branch
  • Vendor
  • Initiating Identity
  • Audit History

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the lifecycle of a Vendor within the Halal-Queue platform.

A Vendor represents a business entity operating on the platform. Every Vendor progresses through a defined lifecycle from onboarding to retirement while maintaining complete business traceability and audit history.

docs.title: Vendor Principles
docs.text:
The Vendor lifecycle follows these principles:

  • Every Vendor represents exactly one business entity.
  • Every Vendor has exactly one Owner Identity.
  • Every Vendor owns exactly one Business Profile.
  • Vendors may own one or more Branches.
  • Vendor lifecycle is independent of user account lifecycle.
  • Every lifecycle transition is auditable.

docs.title: Vendor Architecture
docs.text:
Vendor

├── Vendor ID
├── Owner Identity
├── Business Profile
├── Branches
├── Vendor Staff
├── Status
└── Audit History

docs.title: Vendor Lifecycle
docs.text:
Application Submitted

↓

Under Review

↓

Approved

↓

Profile Setup

↓

Operational

↓

Suspended

↓

Reactivated

↓

Closed

docs.title: Vendor Status Definitions
docs.text: Status Description Application Submitted Vendor application received Under Review Platform reviewing application Approved Vendor approved but not yet operational Profile Setup Business information being completed Operational Vendor may receive customer orders Suspended Vendor temporarily disabled Closed Vendor closed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Vendor shall be created only after a successful vendor application has been accepted.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Vendor shall have a globally unique Vendor ID.

Vendor IDs are immutable.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Vendor shall have exactly one Owner Identity.

The Owner Identity is responsible for administration of the Vendor.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The Vendor Owner may:

  • Update the Business Profile
  • Create Branches
  • Invite Vendor Staff
  • Manage Products
  • Configure Operating Hours
  • Manage Service Areas
  • View Reports

Subject to authorization rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Vendor operates independently.

Vendor resources shall never be shared with another Vendor unless explicitly supported by future platform features.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: New Vendor applications shall begin in the Application Submitted status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Vendor application shall enter the Under Review status before approval or rejection.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Only authorized administrators may approve Vendor applications.

Approval transitions the Vendor to the Approved status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: An Approved Vendor shall complete the required Business Profile before becoming Operational.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor shall become Operational only after satisfying all mandatory onboarding requirements.

These include:

  • Business Profile completed
  • At least one Branch created
  • Operating Hours configured
  • At least one published product

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Only Operational Vendors may receive customer orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may suspend a Vendor.

Suspended Vendors shall not receive new orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Suspending a Vendor shall not remove historical orders.

Orders already accepted shall be handled according to operational policy.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Authorized administrators may reactivate a suspended Vendor.

Reactivation restores Operational status after all suspension conditions have been resolved.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Vendor may be closed by:

  • Platform Administration
  • Vendor Owner (subject to platform policy)

Closed vendors may be reactivated by a Platform Administrator at any time.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Closed Vendors shall not:

  • Accept new orders
  • Modify catalog
  • Create new branches
  • Add staff

Historical business records shall remain preserved.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Version 1 does not support transferring Vendor ownership.

Future versions may introduce controlled ownership transfer workflows.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record:

  • Vendor Created
  • Application Reviewed
  • Vendor Approved
  • Business Profile Completed
  • Vendor Activated
  • Vendor Suspended
  • Vendor Reactivated
  • Vendor Closed

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Significant Vendor lifecycle events may generate Notification Events.

Examples include:

  • Application approved
  • Suspension
  • Reactivation
  • Closure

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every Vendor lifecycle transition shall be traceable to:

  • Vendor
  • Owner Identity
  • Administrator (where applicable)
  • Audit History

docs.title: Vendor Lifecycle Example
docs.text:
Vendor Application

↓

Application Submitted

↓

Under Review

↓

Approved

↓

Business Profile Completed

↓

Operational

↓

Suspended

↓

Operational

↓

Closed

↓

Operational (by Admin)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the business rules governing the operational status of Vendors and their Branches.

Vendor Status determines whether a Vendor or Branch is currently available to receive and fulfill customer orders.

Vendor Status is separate from the Vendor Lifecycle. A Vendor may be approved and operational while a Branch is temporarily unavailable.

docs.title: Status Principles
docs.text:
The Vendor Status subsystem follows these principles:

  • Vendor Lifecycle and Vendor Status are independent.
  • Each Branch maintains its own operational status.
  • Branch Status determines whether new orders may be accepted.
  • Status changes are auditable.
  • Customers shall only see Branches that are available for ordering.

docs.title: Status Architecture
docs.text:
Vendor
    │
    ├── Branch A
    │      └── Status
    │
    ├── Branch B
    │      └── Status
    │
    └── Branch C
           └── Status

docs.title: Branch Status Values
docs.text: Status Description Open Branch is accepting new orders Busy Branch is operational but may temporarily pause new orders Closed Branch is closed according to its operating hours Maintenance Branch is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance or operational issues Suspended Branch has been suspended by platform administration

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: Every Branch shall maintain exactly one operational status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text: A Branch in the Open status may accept new customer orders if it is also within its configured Operating Hours.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch in the Busy status may temporarily limit or pause new customer orders.

Version 1 may treat Busy the same as Open for simplicity.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch in the Closed status shall not accept new customer orders.

Existing accepted orders shall continue through the normal fulfillment process.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch may enter Maintenance status for planned or unplanned operational activities.

Examples include:

  • Equipment maintenance
  • Power outage
  • Inventory count
  • Emergency closure

Branches in Maintenance shall not accept new customer orders.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Platform Administrators may suspend a Branch.

Suspended Branches shall not:

  • Accept new orders
  • Appear in customer search results
  • Be shown as available for ordering

Historical business data shall remain available.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Vendor Owners may change operational statuses that are under their control.

Examples:

  • Open
  • Busy
  • Maintenance

Only Platform Administrators may apply or remove the Suspended status.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A Branch shall be considered available only when:

  • Status is Open, and
  • Current time falls within the configured Operating Hours.

Both conditions must be satisfied.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Customers shall only be able to place orders from Branches that are currently available.

Unavailable Branches may still appear in search results with an appropriate status indicator.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Changing a Branch to Closed, Busy, Maintenance, or Suspended shall not automatically cancel accepted customer orders.

Order handling shall follow the Ordering Business Rules.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
The platform shall permanently record:

  • Previous Status
  • New Status
  • Timestamp
  • Initiating Identity
  • Reason (optional)

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Every status change shall be traceable to:

  • Vendor
  • Branch
  • Initiating Identity
  • Audit History

docs.title: Example Status Flow
docs.text:
Branch Created

↓

Open

↓

Busy

↓

Open

↓

Maintenance

↓

Open

↓

Closed (End of Business Day)

↓

Open (Next Business Day)

docker compose up -d

Never commit .env files.

  • Use const constructors

docs.title: General
docs.text:
• Small functions
  • Single responsibility
  • Clear naming
  • No dead code
  • No commented code

The project follows a feature branch workflow.

main
 ↑
develop
 ↑
feature/*

• feature/*
  • bugfix/*
  • hotfix/*
  • release/*

docs.title: Pull Requests
docs.text:
Every change requires:

  • Passing CI
