docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the Git branching strategy for the Halal-Queue platform.

The objective is to provide a predictable workflow that supports parallel development while protecting the stability of production code.

docs.title: Branch Structure
docs.text:
main
 │
 ├── develop
 │      │
 │      ├── feature/*
 │      ├── bugfix/*
 │      └── release/*
 │
 └── hotfix/*

docs.title: Main Branch
docs.text:
The main branch represents the production-ready codebase.

Rules:

  • Protected branch
  • No direct commits
  • Pull Requests required
  • CI must pass
  • At least one approval required

docs.title: Develop Branch
docs.text:
The develop branch contains the latest integrated development work.

Rules:

  • Feature branches merge into develop
  • CI validation required

docs.title: Feature Branches
docs.text:
Naming

feature/customer-registration

feature/order-history

feature/vendor-dashboard

Rules

  • One feature per branch
  • Rebase frequently
  • Delete after merge

docs.title: Bug Fix Branches
docs.text:
Naming

bugfix/login-validation

bugfix/order-status

docs.title: Release Branches
docs.text:
Naming

release/v1.0.0

release/v1.1.0

Purpose

  • Final testing
  • Documentation updates
  • Version number updates
  • Bug fixes only

docs.title: Hotfix Branches
docs.text:
Naming

hotfix/security-patch

hotfix/payment-timeout

Hotfixes branch from main and merge back into both main and develop.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep branches short-lived.
  • Rebase before opening a Pull Request.
  • Avoid large feature branches.
  • Delete merged branches.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines commit message standards for the Halal-Queue repository.

The project follows the Conventional Commits specification.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
<type>(scope): <summary>

Example

feat(order): add order cancellation endpoint

fix(auth): validate expired refresh token

docs(api): update pagination guide

refactor(product): simplify price calculation

docs.title: Commit Types
docs.text: Type Purpose feat New feature fix Bug fix docs Documentation refactor Code restructuring style Formatting only test Tests chore Maintenance ci CI/CD build Build configuration perf Performance improvements revert Revert previous commit

docs.title: Summary Rules
docs.text:
The summary should:

  • Be concise
  • Use present tense
  • Start with a lowercase verb
  • Be under 72 characters

docs.title: Good Examples
docs.text:
feat(order): support scheduled pickup

fix(product): prevent duplicate categories

docs(openapi): update authentication examples

docs.title: Avoid
docs.text:
Fixed bug

Updated code

Misc changes

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the code review process for all changes submitted to the Halal-Queue repository.

docs.title: Review Objectives
docs.text:
Every review should verify:

  • Correctness
  • Readability
  • Maintainability
  • Security
  • Performance
  • Test coverage
  • Documentation updates

docs.title: Pull Request Requirements
docs.text:
Every Pull Request shall:

  • Pass CI
  • Be reviewed
  • Resolve review comments
  • Have no merge conflicts

docs.title: Review Checklist
docs.text:
Reviewers should verify:

  • Business requirements are met.
  • Coding standards are followed.
  • No duplicated code.
  • Proper error handling.
  • Logging is appropriate.
  • Sensitive data is not exposed.
  • Tests are included.
  • Documentation is updated.

docs.title: Author Responsibilities
docs.text:
Before requesting review:

  • Run tests
  • Run linting
  • Resolve warnings
  • Update documentation
  • Keep PR focused

docs.title: Reviewer Responsibilities
docs.text:
Reviewers should:

  • Provide constructive feedback.
  • Suggest improvements.
  • Identify defects.
  • Approve only when ready.

docs.title: Approval Policy
docs.text:
Minimum approvals

1 reviewer

Critical security changes

2 reviewers

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep Pull Requests small.
  • Review promptly.
  • Discuss design decisions respectfully.
  • Prefer suggestions over rewrites.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the testing strategy for the Halal-Queue platform.

Testing ensures that software changes are reliable, maintainable, and meet business requirements before deployment.

docs.title: Testing Pyramid
docs.text:
E2E Tests
      Integration Tests
         Unit Tests

The majority of tests should be unit tests.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Purpose

  • Verify individual classes and functions.
  • Mock external dependencies.

Examples

  • Service methods
  • Utility functions
  • Business rules
  • Validators

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
Purpose

Verify interaction between multiple components.

Examples

  • Database repositories
  • Service integration
  • Queue processing
  • Authentication flow

docs.title: End-to-End Tests
docs.text:
Purpose

Validate complete business workflows.

Examples

  • Customer registration
  • Vendor approval
  • Order placement
  • Pickup verification

docs.title: Coverage Targets
docs.text:
Component Minimum Coverage Domain 90% Application 85% Infrastructure 70% Overall 80%

Coverage is measured using automated tools during CI.

docs.title: Test Naming
docs.text:
Names should describe expected behavior.

Good

shouldCreateOrder()

shouldRejectExpiredToken()

shouldCalculateTotalPrice()

Avoid

test1()

orderTest()

example()

docs.title: Test Data
docs.text:
Tests should:

  • Be isolated
  • Use deterministic data
  • Clean up after execution
  • Never depend on production data

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
Every Pull Request shall execute:

  • Linting
  • Unit Tests
  • Integration Tests
  • Build Validation

Main branch additionally executes:

  • End-to-End Tests
  • Coverage Reporting

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Test business rules first.
  • Keep tests independent.
  • Mock external services.
  • Avoid flaky tests.
  • Fix broken tests immediately.

docs.title: Revision History
docs.text: Version Date Changes 1.0.0 2026-07-28 Initial version

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines debugging practices for the Halal-Queue platform.

Effective debugging reduces issue resolution time while maintaining system stability.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Use structured logging.

Each log entry should include:

  • Timestamp
  • Log Level
  • Request ID
  • Correlation ID
  • Module
  • Message

docs.title: Log Levels
docs.text: Level Purpose TRACE Detailed execution DEBUG Development diagnostics INFO Business events WARN Recoverable issues ERROR Application errors FATAL Critical failures

docs.title: Debugging Checklist
docs.text:
Before debugging:

  • Reproduce the issue
  • Collect logs
  • Identify affected module
  • Verify environment
  • Review recent changes

docs.title: Common Techniques
docs.text:
• Inspect logs
  • Set breakpoints
  • Debug API requests
  • Review SQL queries
  • Monitor Redis queues
  • Verify environment variables

docs.title: Production Debugging
docs.text:
Production debugging should:

  • Avoid modifying live data
  • Use read-only queries where possible
  • Preserve audit logs
  • Minimize operational impact

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Prefer logs over print statements.
  • Remove temporary debugging code.
  • Document root causes.
  • Create regression tests after fixes.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines how third-party dependencies are introduced, maintained, and updated.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
Dependencies should be:

  • Necessary
  • Well-maintained
  • Actively supported
  • Secure
  • Compatible with the project license

docs.title: Adding Dependencies
docs.text:
Before adding a dependency, evaluate:

  • Community adoption
  • Maintenance activity
  • Documentation quality
  • Security history
  • License compatibility
  • Bundle size
  • Performance impact

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Use semantic versioning.

Prefer:

  • Stable releases
  • Exact or controlled version ranges
  • Regular updates

Avoid unnecessary major-version upgrades without testing.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Dependencies shall be scanned regularly.

Examples

  • npm audit
  • Dependabot
  • GitHub Security Advisories

Critical vulnerabilities should be addressed promptly.

docs.title: Updating Dependencies
docs.text:
Updates should include:

  • Changelog review
  • Compatibility testing
  • Automated test execution
  • Documentation updates if required

docs.title: Removing Dependencies
docs.text:
Unused dependencies should be removed to reduce:

  • Build time
  • Attack surface
  • Maintenance overhead

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep dependencies current.
  • Avoid duplicate libraries.
  • Prefer official packages.
  • Minimize transitive dependencies.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the release management process for the Halal-Queue platform.

The goal is to ensure releases are predictable, traceable, and repeatable while minimizing production risk.

docs.title: Release Types
docs.text:
Type Description Major Breaking changes Minor New backward-compatible features Patch Bug fixes and documentation updates Hotfix Critical production fixes

Example versions

1.0.0
1.1.0
1.1.2
2.0.0

docs.title: Release Workflow
docs.text:
Feature Development
        │
        ▼
Develop Branch
        │
        ▼
Release Branch
        │
        ▼
QA Testing
        │
        ▼
Production Deployment
        │
        ▼
Version Tag

docs.title: Release Checklist
docs.text:
Before creating a release:

  • All tests pass
  • CI pipeline succeeds
  • Documentation updated
  • OpenAPI specification updated
  • Database migrations reviewed
  • Security review completed
  • Performance validation completed

docs.title: Version Tagging
docs.text:
Git tags follow Semantic Versioning.

Example

v1.0.0

v1.1.0

v1.1.1

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text:
Each release shall include:

  • Version
  • Release date
  • New features
  • Bug fixes
  • Breaking changes
  • Database changes
  • Migration notes

docs.title: Database Migration
docs.text:
Database migrations shall:

  • Be version controlled
  • Execute automatically
  • Be reversible where practical
  • Be tested before release

docs.title: Rollback Strategy
docs.text:
Each production release shall define:

  • Rollback procedure
  • Database rollback plan
  • Configuration rollback
  • Recovery validation

docs.title: Post-Release Verification
docs.text:
After deployment verify:

  • Application starts successfully
  • Database migrations completed
  • Authentication works
  • Notifications function
  • Monitoring reports healthy status
  • Error rates remain normal

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep releases small.
  • Release frequently.
  • Automate deployments.
  • Tag every production release.
  • Maintain release notes.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document provides a secure development checklist for engineers working on the Halal-Queue platform.

Every feature should be reviewed against this checklist before merging.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• JWT authentication implemented
  • Refresh tokens handled securely
  • Passwords hashed using Argon2id
  • HTTPS enforced
  • Token expiration validated

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
• RBAC implemented
  • Authorization checked on every protected endpoint
  • Administrative endpoints restricted
  • Ownership validation enforced

docs.title: Input Validation
docs.text:
• Request validation enabled
  • Input sanitized
  • SQL injection prevented
  • XSS prevention applied
  • File uploads validated

docs.title: Sensitive Data
docs.text:
• No passwords logged
  • No secrets committed
  • API keys stored securely
  • Environment variables used
  • Personal data minimized

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• Parameterized queries used
  • Foreign key constraints enabled
  • Transactions used where required
  • Audit fields maintained

docs.title: File Upload
docs.text:
• MIME type validated
  • File size validated
  • Unique object names generated
  • Executable files rejected

docs.title: API Security
docs.text:
• Rate limiting enabled
  • CORS configured
  • Security headers enabled
  • Consistent error responses
  • Request size limits enforced

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Vulnerability scan completed
  • Outdated packages reviewed
  • Unused dependencies removed

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
• Sensitive information excluded
  • Authentication events logged
  • Administrative actions audited
  • Errors logged with correlation IDs

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
• Secrets stored securely
  • Debug mode disabled
  • TLS configured
  • Monitoring enabled
  • Backups verified

docs.title: Final Review
docs.text:
Before merging:

  • Security checklist completed
  • Code review approved
  • Tests passed
  • Documentation updated

docs.text: Version Date Changes 1.0.0 2026-07-28 Initial version

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines performance review guidelines for new features and services.

The objective is to maintain a responsive, scalable, and efficient platform.

docs.title: API Performance
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Response times are acceptable
  • Pagination implemented
  • Filtering supported where appropriate
  • Sorting optimized
  • Large payloads avoided

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Indexes reviewed
  • Queries optimized
  • N+1 queries eliminated
  • Transactions minimized
  • Query plans reviewed when necessary

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Consider caching for:

  • Product catalog
  • Categories
  • Vendor information
  • Frequently accessed configuration

Use Redis where appropriate.

docs.title: Background Processing
docs.text:
Move long-running tasks to queues.

Examples

  • Notifications
  • Report generation
  • Image processing
  • Scheduled jobs

docs.title: File Handling
docs.text:
• Compress images where appropriate
  • Avoid unnecessary downloads
  • Use object storage
  • Stream large files

docs.title: Mobile Applications
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Lazy loading used
  • Images optimized
  • Network requests minimized
  • Offline caching considered
  • UI rendering remains responsive

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
Monitor:

  • API response time
  • Database latency
  • Queue depth
  • Cache hit ratio
  • Memory usage
  • CPU utilization
  • Error rate

docs.title: Performance Testing
docs.text:
Before major releases:

  • Load testing
  • Stress testing
  • Endurance testing
  • Scalability testing

Document results and address critical bottlenecks.

docs.title: Performance Review Checklist
docs.text:
Before merging:

  • Database impact reviewed
  • API response evaluated
  • Memory usage acceptable
  • Background jobs assessed
  • Monitoring updated if required

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Measure before optimizing.
  • Optimize bottlenecks first.
  • Prefer simple solutions.
  • Continuously monitor production performance.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This directory defines the project's software development process.

It describes how features are planned, implemented, validated, documented, and prepared for release.

Unlike the architecture documentation, which explains how the system is designed, this directory explains how contributors should build and deliver software.

This documentation applies to:

  • Backend
  • Customer Mobile
  • Vendor Mobile
  • Worker
  • Admin Web
  • Infrastructure
  • Documentation
  • AI Coding Agents

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
This documentation aims to ensure that every implementation is:

  • Consistent
  • Predictable
  • Maintainable
  • Testable
  • Well documented
  • Production ready

docs.title: Development Documents
docs.text: Document Purpose implementation-roadmap.md Defines the official implementation order of application features. implementation-playbook.md Practical implementation guide for common development tasks. feature-lifecycle.md Defines the lifecycle of every feature from planning to completion. development-workflow.md Standard development workflow followed by all contributors and AI agents. definition-of-done.md Defines the minimum quality requirements before work is considered complete. release-checklist.md Checklist required before releasing a new version.

docs.title: When To Read These Documents
docs.text: Situation Read Starting a new project implementation-roadmap.md Implementing a new feature implementation-playbook.md Planning feature work feature-lifecycle.md Unsure about development process development-workflow.md Before marking work complete definition-of-done.md Preparing a release release-checklist.md

docs.title: Recommended Reading Order
docs.text:
New contributors should read these documents in the following order:

  1. implementation-roadmap.md
  2. implementation-playbook.md
  3. feature-lifecycle.md
  4. development-workflow.md
  5. definition-of-done.md
  6. release-checklist.md

docs.title: Development Principles
docs.text:
Development within this repository follows these principles:

  • Read before writing.
  • Search before creating.
  • Reuse before duplicating.
  • Follow documented architecture.
  • Follow documented business rules.
  • Follow applicable AI skills.
  • Keep changes small and reviewable.
  • Test every change.
  • Keep documentation synchronized.

docs.title: Relationship With Other Documentation
docs.text:
Development documentation complements, but does not replace, the other documentation domains.

Documentation Purpose ../business/ Business rules and domain behavior ../architecture/ System architecture and technical design ../engineering-governance/ Engineering standards and coding conventions ../security/ Security requirements and practices ../testing/ Testing strategy and standards ../deployment/ Deployment procedures ../operations/ Operational procedures and monitoring ../diagrams/ Architecture and workflow diagrams ../repository/ Repository organization and structure ../../openapi/ API contracts and specifications

docs.title: AI Coding Agents
docs.text:
AI coding agents must use this directory together with:

  • AGENTS.md
  • Applicable repository skills
  • Relevant project documentation

Development documentation defines the expected implementation workflow.

It does not override:

  1. Explicit user instructions
  2. AGENTS.md
  3. Project documentation
  4. Repository skills

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
This directory should evolve with the development process.

When introducing new development practices, workflows, or quality requirements:

  • Update the relevant document.
  • Avoid duplicating information.
  • Keep cross-references current.
  • Preserve consistency across the repository.

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text:
• ../architecture/
  • ../business/
  • ../engineering-governance/
  • ../testing/
  • ../deployment/
  • ../operations/
  • ../../AGENTS.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the minimum quality requirements that every completed task, feature, bug fix, refactoring, documentation update, and infrastructure change must satisfy before it is considered complete.

No work is considered complete until the applicable requirements in this document have been satisfied.

This document applies to:

  • Backend
  • Customer Mobile
  • Vendor Mobile
  • Worker
  • Admin Web
  • Documentation
  • Infrastructure
  • OpenAPI
  • Database

docs.title: Core Principle
docs.text:
"Code Complete" does NOT mean "Feature Complete."

A task is complete only when:

  • implementation is finished
  • validation is finished
  • documentation is synchronized
  • review is complete

docs.title: Universal Checklist
docs.text: The following checklist applies to every task.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Requirements understood
  • Scope respected
  • No undocumented assumptions made

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Repository architecture respected
  • Module boundaries respected
  • Existing implementation patterns reused
  • No unnecessary abstractions introduced

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
• Production-ready implementation
  • Readable code
  • Consistent naming
  • No dead code
  • No commented-out code
  • No debug code
  • No temporary implementation
  • No unexplained TODOs

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Authentication respected
  • Authorization respected
  • Input validation completed
  • Sensitive information protected
  • No secrets committed
  • Error handling reviewed

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation must remain synchronized with implementation.

If applicable:

  • Business documentation updated
  • Architecture updated
  • OpenAPI updated
  • Diagrams updated
  • ADR updated
  • README updated
  • Changelog updated

Only update affected documentation.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Applicable tests completed.

  • Unit tests
  • Integration tests
  • API tests
  • UI tests
  • End-to-end tests

If tests could not be executed:

Document why.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run the applicable validation.

  • Formatter
  • Linter
  • Type checking
  • Build
  • Static analysis

Never claim validation succeeded unless it actually ran.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Before completion:

  • Self review completed
  • Final diff reviewed
  • No unrelated changes
  • No accidental files
  • No generated artifacts committed accidentally

docs.title: Backend Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for backend changes.

  • DTO completed
  • Validation completed
  • Service completed
  • Repository completed
  • Controller completed
  • Policies implemented
  • OpenAPI updated
  • Tests completed

docs.title: Customer Mobile Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for Customer Mobile.

  • Models completed
  • API client updated
  • Repository updated
  • State management completed
  • UI completed
  • Validation completed
  • Localization updated
  • Tests completed

docs.title: Vendor Mobile Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for Vendor Mobile.

  • Models completed
  • API integration completed
  • Repository updated
  • State management completed
  • UI completed
  • Validation completed
  • Localization updated
  • Tests completed

docs.title: Worker Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for Worker.

  • Events handled
  • Jobs completed
  • Retry policy reviewed
  • Idempotency verified
  • Logging completed
  • Tests completed

docs.title: Admin Web Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for Admin Web.

  • API integration completed
  • UI completed
  • State management updated
  • Validation completed
  • Permissions implemented
  • Tests completed

docs.title: Database Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for database changes.

  • Schema reviewed
  • Migration created
  • Migration tested
  • Existing data considered
  • Constraints reviewed
  • Indexes reviewed
  • Rollback considered

Never modify existing applied migrations.

docs.title: API Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for API changes.

  • Endpoint implemented
  • Validation completed
  • Authorization completed
  • Error responses reviewed
  • Status codes reviewed
  • OpenAPI updated
  • API tests completed

docs.title: Documentation Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for documentation updates.

  • Correct document updated
  • No duplicated information
  • Cross-references verified
  • Navigation updated if necessary
  • README updated if required

docs.title: Infrastructure Definition of Done
docs.text:
Applicable for infrastructure changes.

  • Configuration reviewed
  • Documentation updated
  • Deployment impact reviewed
  • Rollback considered
  • Security reviewed

docs.title: Bug Fix Definition of Done
docs.text:
A bug fix is complete when:

  • Root cause identified
  • Root cause fixed
  • Regression test added (where practical)
  • Documentation updated (if behavior changed)

Do not fix symptoms only.

docs.title: Refactoring Definition of Done
docs.text:
A refactoring is complete when:

  • Behavior unchanged
  • Tests still pass
  • Readability improved
  • Complexity reduced
  • Documentation still accurate

docs.title: Feature Definition of Done
docs.text:
A feature is complete when:

  • Business rules implemented
  • APIs completed
  • UI completed
  • Worker completed (if applicable)
  • Notifications completed (if applicable)
  • Documentation completed
  • Tests completed
  • Manual verification completed

docs.title: Manual Verification
docs.text:
Where applicable, manually verify:

  • happy path
  • validation
  • authorization
  • permissions
  • error handling
  • edge cases

docs.title: Final Questions
docs.text:
Before marking work complete, answer:

  1. Does the implementation satisfy the requirements?
  2. Does it follow the documented architecture?
  3. Does it follow repository standards?
  4. Is the documentation synchronized?
  5. Have applicable tests passed?
  6. Is the change understandable by another developer?
  7. Would I confidently approve this pull request?

If any answer is "No",

the task is not complete.

docs.title: Completion Statement
docs.text:
A task may be reported as complete only when:

  • all applicable Definition of Done items have been satisfied, or
  • any remaining items are explicitly documented with a clear explanation and approved by the user.

Never claim a task is complete when required work remains outstanding.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the standard development workflow for all contributors and AI coding agents.

Following this workflow ensures:

  • consistent implementation
  • predictable reviews
  • minimal regressions
  • synchronized documentation
  • maintainable code

This workflow applies to:

  • Backend
  • Customer Mobile
  • Vendor Mobile
  • Worker
  • Admin Web
  • Infrastructure
  • Documentation

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
Receive Task
        ↓
Understand Requirements
        ↓
Read Documentation
        ↓
Read Applicable Skills
        ↓
Inspect Existing Implementation
        ↓
Plan
        ↓
Approval (if required)
        ↓
Implement
        ↓
Validate
        ↓
Update Documentation
        ↓
Self Review
        ↓
Ready For Merge

docs.title: Step 1 — Receive Task
docs.text:
Determine:

  • objective
  • scope
  • affected applications
  • affected modules
  • expected deliverables

Do not begin implementation immediately.

docs.title: Step 2 — Understand Requirements
docs.text:
Identify:

  • business requirement
  • technical requirement
  • acceptance criteria
  • dependencies

If requirements are incomplete:

Stop.

Ask questions.

Never guess.

docs.title: Step 3 — Read Documentation
docs.text:
Read only the documentation relevant to the task.

Possible locations include:

  • docs/business/
  • docs/architecture/
  • docs/security/
  • docs/testing/
  • docs/deployment/
  • docs/engineering-governance/
  • docs/diagrams/

Documentation is the primary source of truth.

docs.title: Step 4 — Read Applicable Skills
docs.text:
Inspect:

.agents/skills/

Read only the skills relevant to the task.

Examples:

Backend

↓

NestJS skill (nestjs-best-practices)

React Native / Expo

↓

Expo skill (expo-best-practices)

Admin Web (React + Vite)

↓

Vite & React skill (vite-best-practices, vercel-react-best-practices)

API

↓

OpenAPI guidelines / skill

Testing

↓

Testing skill

Documentation

↓

Documentation skill

Skills complement documentation.

docs.title: Step 5 — Inspect Existing Implementation
docs.text:
Before writing code:

Locate:

  • existing module
  • existing service
  • existing repository
  • existing DTO
  • existing tests
  • existing documentation

Search before creating.

Reuse before rewriting.

docs.title: Step 6 — Planning
docs.text:
Create a concise implementation plan.

The plan should identify:

  • affected applications
  • affected modules
  • affected APIs
  • database changes
  • events
  • documentation updates
  • tests

Do not begin coding until the approach is understood.

docs.title: Step 7 — Approval
docs.text:
Approval is required before:

  • breaking changes
  • architecture changes
  • database schema changes
  • dependency changes
  • infrastructure changes
  • repository restructuring
  • deleting public APIs

Present:

  • proposed change
  • impact
  • affected files
  • risks

Wait for approval.

docs.title: Step 8 — Implementation
docs.text:
Implement using the documented architecture.

Implementation order:

Backend

↓

Worker

↓

Customer Mobile

↓

Vendor Mobile

↓

Admin Web

Do not implement unrelated improvements.

docs.title: Step 9 — Validation
docs.text:
Run all applicable validation.

Examples:

  • formatter
  • lint
  • type check
  • tests
  • build

Never claim validation succeeded unless it actually ran.

docs.title: Step 10 — Documentation
docs.text:
Update affected documentation.

Possible updates:

  • OpenAPI
  • Business
  • Architecture
  • Diagrams
  • README
  • ADR
  • Changelog

Update only the authoritative document.

docs.title: Step 11 — Self Review
docs.text:
Review the implementation before considering it complete.

Verify:

  • architecture
  • security
  • correctness
  • readability
  • documentation
  • tests

Review the final diff.

docs.title: Step 12 — Ready For Merge
docs.text:
A task is ready when:

  • implementation complete
  • tests complete
  • documentation complete
  • validation complete
  • review complete

docs.title: Branch Strategy
docs.text:
Each feature should be implemented in an isolated branch.

Do not combine unrelated work.

One branch should represent one logical change.

docs.title: Commit Guidelines
docs.text:
Commits should be:

  • small
  • logical
  • reviewable

Avoid mixing:

  • refactoring
  • features
  • dependency updates
  • documentation
  • formatting

in one commit whenever possible.

docs.title: Pull Request Checklist
docs.text:
Before opening a pull request:

  • Scope completed
  • Tests passing
  • Documentation updated
  • OpenAPI updated
  • Build successful
  • Final diff reviewed

docs.title: Merge Criteria
docs.text:
A change may be merged only when:

  • implementation is complete
  • validation completed
  • documentation synchronized
  • review completed
  • no known blocking issues remain

docs.title: Development Principles
docs.text:
Always:

  • Read before writing.
  • Search before creating.
  • Reuse before duplicating.
  • Follow documentation.
  • Follow applicable skills.
  • Respect architecture.
  • Keep changes small.
  • Keep changes reviewable.

Never:

  • Guess business rules.
  • Skip documentation.
  • Skip tests.
  • Skip validation.
  • Introduce undocumented behavior.
  • Mix unrelated work.
  • Leave incomplete implementations.

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text:
Stop and request guidance when:

  • documentation conflicts
  • architecture conflicts
  • business rules are unclear
  • destructive changes are required
  • breaking changes are proposed
  • required documentation is missing

Never resolve ambiguity by assumption.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the standard lifecycle for implementing a feature in this repository.

Every feature, regardless of size, follows the same lifecycle.

The objective is to:

  • reduce regressions
  • maintain consistency
  • keep documentation synchronized
  • ensure every feature is production-ready
  • prevent incomplete implementations

docs.title: Guiding Principles
docs.text:
Every feature should be:

  • independently testable
  • independently reviewable
  • independently deployable (where applicable)

Features should be implemented as complete vertical slices.

Never leave a partially implemented feature merged into the main branch.

docs.title: Feature Lifecycle
docs.text:
Planning
    ↓
Analysis
    ↓
Design
    ↓
Implementation
    ↓
Validation
    ↓
Documentation
    ↓
Review
    ↓
Ready for Release

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Understand what needs to be built.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document provides practical implementation guides for common development tasks.

Unlike architecture documentation, this document focuses on how to implement new functionality consistently within this repository.

This playbook complements:

  • AGENTS.md
  • Development Workflow
  • Feature Lifecycle
  • Definition of Done

docs.title: Before Starting Any Task
docs.text:
Always complete the following steps before writing code.

  1. Read the business documentation.
  2. Read the relevant architecture documentation.
  3. Read applicable AI skills.
  4. Search the repository.
  5. Locate similar implementations.
  6. Determine affected modules.
  7. Determine affected APIs.
  8. Determine affected documentation.

Never skip investigation.

docs.title: Adding a New API Endpoint
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Review OpenAPI guidelines.
  2. Update the OpenAPI specification.
  3. Create request DTO.
  4. Create response DTO.
  5. Add validation.
  6. Implement service.
  7. Implement controller.
  8. Add tests.
  9. Update documentation.

Never implement an undocumented endpoint.

docs.title: Adding a New Database Entity
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Review the domain model.
  2. Identify owning module.
  3. Design schema.
  4. Create migration.
  5. Create repository.
  6. Add tests.
  7. Update ERD if required.
  8. Update documentation.

Never modify an existing applied migration.

docs.title: Adding a New Business Rule
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Update business documentation.
  2. Update architecture if required.
  3. Update API if required.
  4. Implement backend.
  5. Update mobile apps.
  6. Add tests.

Business documentation is the source of truth.

docs.title: Adding a New Mobile Screen
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Review existing UI patterns.
  2. Reuse components.
  3. Create screen.
  4. Connect state management.
  5. Connect repository.
  6. Connect API.
  7. Add localization.
  8. Add tests.

docs.text:
Steps

  1. Determine trigger.
  2. Determine recipient.
  3. Determine delivery channel.
  4. Create template.
  5. Implement backend.
  6. Implement worker.
  7. Add tests.

Never duplicate notifications.

docs.title: Adding a Background Job
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Define responsibility.
  2. Define trigger.
  3. Define retry policy.
  4. Ensure idempotency.
  5. Add monitoring.
  6. Add tests.

docs.title: Adding a Scheduled Task
docs.text:
Determine

  • schedule
  • retry
  • timeout
  • logging
  • monitoring

Document all scheduled jobs.

docs.title: Adding an Event
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Identify owner.
  2. Review event architecture.
  3. Define payload.
  4. Implement publisher.
  5. Implement consumers.
  6. Add tests.

Events are contracts.

docs.title: Adding Validation
docs.text:
Validation belongs at the application boundary.

Never rely solely on frontend validation.

Validate:

  • input
  • permissions
  • ownership
  • business rules

docs.title: Adding Authorization
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Authenticate user.
  2. Check permission.
  3. Check ownership.
  4. Check business rule.
  5. Continue.

Never bypass authorization.

docs.title: Updating Existing Features
docs.text:
Before changing existing behavior:

  • inspect implementation
  • inspect tests
  • inspect documentation
  • inspect API

Never change behavior accidentally.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
Before refactoring

Determine:

  • why
  • scope
  • dependencies
  • risks

Goals

  • readability
  • maintainability
  • consistency

Not

  • changing behavior

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
Steps

  1. Reproduce.
  2. Find root cause.
  3. Fix root cause.
  4. Add regression test.
  5. Verify.

Never fix only symptoms.

docs.title: Documentation Updates
docs.text:
Update only the authoritative document.

Never duplicate information.

Always update:

  • OpenAPI
  • diagrams
  • business docs
  • architecture

when applicable.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
For every feature determine:

  • Unit tests
  • Integration tests
  • API tests
  • UI tests
  • Manual verification

Use the smallest effective test.

docs.text:

  • skipped documentation

docs.text:
When unsure:

Read documentation.

Read skills.

Search existing code.

Then implement.

Never guess.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the minimum requirements before releasing any version of the system.

Its purpose is to ensure that every release is:

  • Stable
  • Tested
  • Documented
  • Secure
  • Deployable
  • Recoverable

This checklist applies to:

  • Backend
  • Customer Mobile
  • Vendor Mobile
  • Worker
  • Admin Web
  • Database
  • Infrastructure

docs.title: Release Workflow
docs.text:
Feature Freeze
        ↓
Code Freeze
        ↓
Validation
        ↓
Documentation Review
        ↓
Release Candidate
        ↓
Deployment
        ↓
Smoke Testing
        ↓
Production Release
        ↓
Post Release Monitoring

docs.title: 1. Feature Freeze
docs.text:
Before release:

  • No new features being merged
  • Scope frozen
  • Outstanding issues reviewed

docs.title: 2. Code Freeze
docs.text:
Before deployment:

  • No breaking refactoring
  • No dependency upgrades
  • No architectural changes

Only bug fixes may be merged after code freeze.

docs.title: 3. Source Control
docs.text:
• Main branch is stable
  • Version tagged
  • Changelog updated

docs.title: 4. Documentation
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Business documentation
  • Architecture documentation
  • OpenAPI
  • Diagrams
  • Deployment documentation
  • README updates

docs.title: 5. API
docs.text:
Verify:

  • OpenAPI synchronized
  • No undocumented endpoints
  • No undocumented breaking changes
  • API version reviewed

docs.title: 6. Database
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Migrations reviewed
  • Migrations tested
  • Rollback considered
  • Existing data compatibility verified

Never deploy untested migrations.

docs.title: 7. Backend
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Build successful
  • Unit tests passed
  • Integration tests passed
  • API tests passed
  • Security review completed

docs.title: 8. Customer Mobile
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Build successful
  • API integration verified
  • Manual testing completed
  • Release configuration verified

docs.title: 9. Vendor Mobile
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Build successful
  • API integration verified
  • Manual testing completed

docs.title: 10. Admin Web
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Build successful
  • Permissions verified
  • Manual testing completed

docs.title: 11. Worker
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Background jobs tested
  • Retry behavior verified
  • Idempotency verified
  • Logging verified

docs.title: 12. Infrastructure
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Docker images built
  • Environment variables verified
  • Secrets configured
  • Storage available
  • Database available
  • Queue available
  • Monitoring available

docs.title: 13. Security
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Authentication tested
  • Authorization tested
  • Sensitive data protected
  • Secrets not committed
  • Error handling reviewed

docs.title: 14. Performance
docs.text:
Verify where applicable:

  • Slow endpoints reviewed
  • Database queries reviewed
  • Memory usage acceptable
  • Background jobs acceptable

docs.title: 15. Manual Regression Testing
docs.text: Verify critical user journeys.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text:
• Login
  • Browse vendors
  • Browse products
  • Add to cart
  • Place order
  • Receive notifications
  • View order history

  • Accept order
  • Reject order
  • Send change request
  • Mark ready
  • Complete pickup

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:

  • Vendor management
  • Branch management
  • User management
  • Reports

docs.title: 16. Deployment
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Deployment completed
  • Health checks passed
  • Database migration completed
  • Worker started
  • Monitoring active

docs.title: 17. Smoke Tests
docs.text:
Immediately after deployment:

  • Backend reachable
  • Database reachable
  • Authentication works
  • Customer app works
  • Vendor app works
  • Admin web works
  • Notifications work

docs.title: 18. Post Release
docs.text:
Monitor:

  • Error logs
  • Background jobs
  • API errors
  • Performance
  • User reports

docs.title: Release Approval
docs.text:
A release may proceed only when:

  • Definition of Done satisfied
  • Release Checklist completed
  • Outstanding critical issues resolved
  • Deployment plan verified

docs.title: Release Decision
docs.text:
Choose one:

  • Approved for Release
  • Blocked
  • Postponed

If blocked, document:

  • Blocking issue
  • Impact
  • Resolution plan

docs.title: Final Rule
docs.text:
Never deploy software that has not been:

  • Implemented
  • Tested
  • Reviewed
  • Documented
  • Validated

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines how deprecated functionality is managed.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
Deprecation should:

  • Be communicated clearly
  • Be documented
  • Include migration guidance
  • Provide a reasonable transition period

docs.title: API Deprecation
docs.text:
A deprecated endpoint shall:

  • Be marked in OpenAPI
  • Include documentation
  • Provide a replacement endpoint
  • Specify a removal date

docs.title: Removal Process
docs.text:
1. Mark as deprecated.
  2. Publish migration guide.
  3. Notify stakeholders.
  4. Remove in the next major version.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: Critical security issues may require accelerated removal.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines how engineering documentation is created, reviewed, maintained, and retired.

Documentation is considered part of the product and shall evolve with the software.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
Documentation shall be:

  • Accurate
  • Complete
  • Version controlled
  • Reviewable
  • Discoverable
  • Consistent

docs.text: Category Examples Business BRD, Use Cases Architecture System Design, ADRs API OpenAPI Operations Runbooks, SLOs Developer Coding Standards Database ERD, Schema

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Document Type Owner Business Product Owner Architecture Software Architect API Backend Team Mobile Mobile Team Infrastructure Platform Team Operations DevOps Team

docs.title: Review Frequency
docs.text: Document Review ADRs As Needed API Every Release Operations Quarterly Security Quarterly Business Every Sprint Architecture Quarterly

docs.text:

docs.title: Change Management
docs.text:
Documentation updates shall accompany:

  • New features
  • Breaking changes
  • Database changes
  • API changes
  • Infrastructure changes
  • Security changes

Documentation Pull Requests should be reviewed alongside code changes.

docs.title: Version Control
docs.text:
Documentation shall:

  • Reside in Git
  • Use Markdown
  • Be reviewed through Pull Requests
  • Maintain revision history

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text:
Obsolete documents shall:

  • Be marked as deprecated
  • Reference replacement documents
  • Remain accessible for historical purposes where appropriate

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep documents concise.
  • Prefer diagrams for complex workflows.
  • Link related documents.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines the lifecycle of REST APIs from initial design through retirement.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Proposal

↓

Design

↓

Review

↓

Implementation

↓

Testing

↓

Release

↓

Maintenance

↓

Deprecation

↓

docs.title: Design Phase
docs.text:
Every API shall include:

  • OpenAPI specification
  • Request schema
  • Response schema
  • Error responses
  • Security requirements
  • Examples

Implementation must not begin until the API design has been reviewed and approved.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The platform uses URI-based versioning.

Examples

/api/v1/orders

/api/v2/orders

Breaking changes require a new major API version.

docs.title: Backward Compatibility
docs.text:
Minor releases should remain backward compatible.

Breaking changes should:

  • Introduce a new API version
  • Publish migration guidance
  • Provide an overlap period for supported versions

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text:
Deprecated APIs shall:

  • Be marked in the OpenAPI specification
  • Be documented
  • Include a recommended replacement
  • Specify a planned retirement date

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text:
Before retiring an API:

  • Notify stakeholders
  • Publish migration documentation
  • Confirm consumers have migrated
  • Remove the endpoint in the next supported major release

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
Monitor:

  • Request volume
  • Error rates
  • Consumer adoption
  • Deprecated endpoint usage

These metrics inform deprecation and retirement decisions.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Design APIs before implementation.
  • Maintain consistency across resources.
  • Avoid breaking changes where possible.
  • Document every public endpoint.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document identifies, evaluates, and tracks technical and operational risks affecting the Halal-Queue platform.

The register should be reviewed regularly and updated as new risks emerge or existing risks change.

docs.title: Risk Assessment Matrix
docs.text: Impact Description Low Minimal business impact Medium Noticeable operational impact High Significant service disruption Critical Major business disruption Likelihood Description Rare Unlikely to occur Possible Could occur occasionally Likely Expected to occur periodically Almost Certain Expected to occur frequently

docs.title: Active Risks
docs.text: ID Risk Impact Likelihood Mitigation Owner Status R-001 Database outage Critical Possible Replication, backups, monitoring Platform Team Open R-002 Redis unavailable High Possible High availability, health checks Platform Team Open R-003 Object storage outage High Rare Redundant storage, backups Platform Team Open R-004 API abuse High Possible Authentication, rate limiting, WAF Security Team Open R-005 Dependency vulnerability High Likely Automated scanning, patch management Engineering Open R-006 CI/CD pipeline failure Medium Possible Redundant runners, monitoring DevOps Open R-007 Documentation drift Medium Likely Documentation reviews, PR requirements Engineering Open R-008 Vendor lock-in Medium Possible Open standards, portable infrastructure Architecture Open

docs.title: Risk Response Strategies
docs.text:
Possible responses include:

  • Avoid
  • Reduce
  • Transfer
  • Accept

Each risk should have a defined response strategy and an assigned owner.

docs.title: Review Process
docs.text:
The Engineering Leadership Team shall review the risk register:

  • Monthly
  • Before major releases
  • After significant incidents
  • Following architectural changes

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text: Critical risks shall be escalated immediately to Engineering Leadership and tracked until mitigation is complete.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Review risks proactively.
  • Assign clear ownership.
  • Track mitigation progress.
  • Record residual risk after mitigation.
  • Link risks to ADRs or incident reports where appropriate.

These documents are intended for DevOps engineers, SREs, system administrators, and software engineers responsible for production environments.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the monitoring strategy for the Halal-Queue platform.

Monitoring enables proactive detection of system issues and provides visibility into application health and performance.

docs.title: Monitoring Objectives
docs.text:
The monitoring solution shall:

  • Detect failures quickly
  • Measure system health
  • Track application performance
  • Support troubleshooting
  • Provide operational dashboards

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Monitor:

  • Backend API
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis
  • BullMQ Workers
  • Object Storage
  • Mobile API Gateway
  • Background Jobs

docs.title: Key Metrics
docs.text:
Application

  • Requests per second
  • Average response time
  • Error rate
  • Active users

Infrastructure

  • CPU usage
  • Memory usage
  • Disk usage
  • Network traffic

Database

  • Connections
  • Slow queries
  • Query latency
  • Transaction rate

Queue

  • Queue depth
  • Failed jobs
  • Processing time
  • Retry count

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Recommended dashboards:

  • System Overview
  • API Performance
  • Database
  • Queue Processing
  • Notifications
  • Business Metrics

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Monitor all production services.
  • Use meaningful dashboards.
  • Review trends regularly.
  • Define alert thresholds.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines logging standards for the Halal-Queue platform.

Logs support monitoring, troubleshooting, auditing, and security investigations.

docs.title: Log Format
docs.text:
Logs should be structured JSON.

Each log should include:

  • Timestamp
  • Level
  • Request ID
  • Correlation ID
  • Service
  • Module
  • Message

docs.title: Log Levels
docs.text: Level Purpose TRACE Detailed execution DEBUG Debugging INFO Business events WARN Recoverable issues ERROR Errors FATAL Critical failures

docs.title: Sensitive Data
docs.text:
Never log:

  • Passwords
  • JWT tokens
  • Refresh tokens
  • Credit card data
  • Secrets
  • API keys

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Recommended retention:

Log Type Retention Application 30 Days Audit 1 Year Security 1 Year

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use structured logging.
  • Include correlation IDs.
  • Avoid duplicate logs.
  • Rotate logs automatically.

docs.title: Purpose

Alerts notify engineers when system health or business operations require attention.

docs.title: Alert Severity
docs.text: Severity Description Critical Immediate response required High Significant degradation Medium Investigation required Low Informational

docs.title: Critical Alerts

  • API unavailable
  • Database unavailable
  • Redis unavailable
  • Authentication failure

  • Backup failure

docs.title: High Alerts

Examples

  • High response time
  • Elevated error rate
  • Queue backlog
  • Disk usage above threshold
  • Memory exhaustion

docs.title: Notification Channels
docs.text:
Alerts may be sent using:

  • Email
  • Slack
  • Microsoft Teams
  • PagerDuty

docs.title: Alert Quality
docs.text:
Alerts should:

  • Be actionable
  • Include context
  • Avoid duplicates
  • Reduce alert fatigue

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text: Critical alerts should follow a documented escalation process until resolved.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the backup and recovery strategy for the Halal-Queue platform.

The objective is to ensure business continuity and prevent data loss caused by hardware failures, software defects, or operational mistakes.

docs.title: Backup Scope
docs.text:
The following assets shall be backed up:

  • PostgreSQL databases
  • Application configuration
  • Object storage metadata
  • Uploaded files (where applicable)
  • Infrastructure configuration
  • CI/CD configuration

docs.title: Backup Frequency
docs.text: Asset Frequency PostgreSQL Daily Transaction Logs Continuous (WAL Archiving) Object Storage Daily Configuration On Change Git Repository Hosted Repository

docs.title: Backup Retention
docs.text:
Backup Type Retention Daily 30 Days Weekly 12 Weeks Monthly 12 Months

Retention policies may be adjusted to meet business and regulatory requirements.

docs.title: Recovery Objectives
docs.text: Metric Target Recovery Time Objective (RTO) ≤ 2 Hours Recovery Point Objective (RPO) ≤ 15 Minutes

docs.title: Recovery Procedure
docs.text:
Recovery includes:

  1. Identify affected systems.
  2. Restore infrastructure.
  3. Restore database.
  4. Restore object storage.
  5. Verify application integrity.
  6. Perform smoke testing.
  7. Resume production traffic.

docs.title: Backup Validation
docs.text:
Backups shall be:

  • Verified automatically
  • Tested regularly
  • Protected with encryption
  • Stored in separate locations

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Encrypt backups.
  • Test restoration regularly.
  • Automate backup scheduling.
  • Monitor backup success.
  • Store copies off-site.

docs.title: Revision History
docs.text: Version Date Changes 1.0.0 2026-07-28 Initial version

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the disaster recovery (DR) strategy for the Halal-Queue platform.

A disaster is any event that causes significant disruption to production services.

docs.title: Disaster Scenarios
docs.text:
Examples include:

  • Data center outage
  • Cloud region failure
  • Database corruption
  • Security incident
  • Ransomware attack
  • Infrastructure failure

docs.title: Recovery Priorities
docs.text:
Priority order:

  1. Authentication
  2. Database
  3. Backend API
  4. Redis
  5. Background Workers
  6. Object Storage
  7. Notification Services

docs.title: Recovery Process
docs.text:
Incident

↓

Assessment

↓

Containment

↓

Infrastructure Recovery

↓

Database Recovery

↓

Application Recovery

↓

Verification

↓

Production Restored

docs.title: Recovery Testing
docs.text:
Disaster recovery procedures shall be tested:

  • At least annually
  • After major infrastructure changes
  • Following significant architectural updates

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Recovery documentation shall include:

  • Contact list
  • Recovery steps
  • System dependencies
  • Validation checklist

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Maintain redundant infrastructure.
  • Store backups in multiple locations.
  • Document every recovery exercise.
  • Review DR plans regularly.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document defines routine maintenance activities for the Halal-Queue platform.

docs.title: Scheduled Maintenance
docs.text:
Typical activities include:

  • Operating system updates
  • Database maintenance
  • Security patches
  • Dependency upgrades
  • Infrastructure updates
  • Certificate renewal

docs.title: Maintenance Window
docs.text:
Recommended maintenance window:

  • Low-traffic periods
  • Scheduled in advance
  • Communicated to stakeholders

docs.title: Pre-Maintenance Checklist
docs.text:
Before maintenance:

  • Verify backups
  • Notify stakeholders
  • Review rollback plan
  • Verify monitoring
  • Confirm maintenance scope

docs.title: Post-Maintenance Checklist
docs.text:
After maintenance:

  • Verify application health
  • Review logs
  • Execute smoke tests
  • Confirm monitoring
  • Close maintenance record

docs.title: Emergency Maintenance
docs.text:
Emergency maintenance may bypass standard scheduling when required to:

  • Resolve security vulnerabilities
  • Restore service
  • Prevent data loss

All emergency actions shall be documented.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Automate repetitive tasks.
  • Minimize downtime.
  • Test changes in staging.
  • Document all maintenance activities.

docs.text: Version Date Changes 1.0.0 2026-07-28 Initial version

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines standardized operational procedures (runbooks) for common production activities.

Runbooks provide step-by-step instructions that enable engineers to perform routine operational tasks consistently and safely.

docs.title: Available Runbooks
docs.text: ID Runbook RB-001 Restart Backend Service RB-002 Restart Queue Workers RB-003 Restore PostgreSQL Backup RB-004 Rotate JWT Secrets RB-005 Renew TLS Certificates RB-006 Scale Application Instances RB-007 Clear Redis Cache RB-008 Recover Failed Jobs

docs.title: Runbook Template
docs.text:
Each runbook should include:

  • Purpose
  • Prerequisites
  • Required permissions
  • Step-by-step procedure
  • Validation steps
  • Rollback procedure
  • Related documentation

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
• Maintenance window approved (if required)
  • Monitoring dashboard available
  • Rollback plan prepared

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Verify current application health.
  2. Notify stakeholders if required.
  3. Restart backend service.
  4. Wait for health checks to succeed.
  5. Verify API availability.
  6. Confirm background workers reconnect.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Health endpoint returns HTTP 200
  • Database connectivity
  • Redis connectivity
  • Queue processing
  • Authentication

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Every operational procedure should have a corresponding runbook.

Runbooks should be reviewed after:

  • Major releases
  • Infrastructure changes
  • Incident postmortems

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep runbooks concise.
  • Include screenshots where appropriate.
  • Test procedures regularly.
  • Update immediately after operational changes.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the incident response process for production environments.

The objective is to restore service quickly while minimizing business impact.

docs.title: Incident Lifecycle
docs.text:
Detection

↓

Assessment

↓

Classification

↓

Containment

↓

Investigation

↓

Resolution

↓

Recovery

↓

Postmortem

docs.title: Incident Severity
docs.text: Severity Description Target Response SEV-1 Complete service outage 15 minutes SEV-2 Major functionality degraded 30 minutes SEV-3 Minor functionality affected 4 hours SEV-4 Cosmetic or informational Next business day

docs.title: Incident Roles
docs.text: Role Responsibility Incident Commander Coordinates response Technical Lead Leads technical investigation Communications Lead Provides stakeholder updates Scribe Documents timeline and actions

docs.title: Response Process
docs.text:
1. Detect the incident.
  2. Assess severity.
  3. Assign an Incident Commander.
  4. Contain the issue.
  5. Restore service.
  6. Verify recovery.
  7. Conduct a post-incident review.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
During active incidents:

  • Maintain a timeline of events.
  • Provide regular stakeholder updates.
  • Document decisions and actions.
  • Record recovery time.

docs.title: Postmortem
docs.text:
Every SEV-1 and SEV-2 incident shall include:

  • Root cause analysis
  • Timeline
  • Customer impact
  • Corrective actions
  • Preventive actions
  • Follow-up tasks

Postmortems should focus on improving systems and processes rather than assigning blame.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Respond quickly.
  • Escalate early.
  • Communicate clearly.
  • Document everything.
  • Learn from every incident.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines measurable service reliability objectives for the Halal-Queue platform.

SLOs establish target levels of availability and performance that guide operational priorities and continuous improvement.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: Service Target Availability Backend API 99.9% Authentication 99.9% Product Catalog 99.9% Ordering 99.9% Notifications 99.5%

docs.title: Performance Objectives
docs.text: Metric Target API Response (P95) < 300 ms API Response (P99) < 800 ms Login < 2 seconds Order Creation < 3 seconds Product Search < 500 ms

docs.title: Reliability Objectives
docs.text: Metric Target Failed Deployments < 2% Successful Backups 100% Failed Queue Jobs < 1% Database Availability 99.9%

docs.title: Error Budget
docs.text:
For a 99.9% monthly availability target:

Period Allowed Downtime Day ~1.4 minutes Month ~43 minutes Year ~8.8 hours

When the error budget is exhausted:

  • Pause non-essential feature releases.
  • Prioritize reliability improvements.
  • Review operational practices.

docs.title: Service Indicators (SLIs)
docs.text:
Track:

  • Request success rate
  • Response latency
  • Queue processing success
  • Database latency
  • Authentication success rate
  • Notification delivery rate

docs.title: Review Process
docs.text:
SLOs shall be reviewed:

  • Quarterly
  • After major incidents
  • Following significant architecture changes

Adjustments should be based on operational data and business requirements.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Define realistic objectives.
  • Monitor continuously.
  • Use SLOs to guide engineering decisions.
  • Review trends rather than isolated events.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This directory defines how the Halal-Queue software is implemented.

While the Business documentation explains what the system should do and the System Design documentation explains how the system is designed, this documentation explains how the source code is organized, developed, tested, and maintained.

It establishes development standards to ensure the codebase remains consistent, maintainable, and scalable.

docs.title: Objectives

The software architecture aims to provide:

  • Consistent project organization
  • Clear module boundaries
  • High maintainability
  • High testability
  • Secure implementation
  • Reliable deployments
  • Clean code practices
  • Easy onboarding for new developers

docs.title: Architecture Principles

  • Modular Monolith architecture
  • Clean Architecture
  • Domain-Driven Design (DDD)
  • SOLID principles
  • Dependency Inversion Principle
  • Separation of Concerns
  • Secure by Default
  • Convention over Configuration

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the high-level repository layout for the Halal-Queue project. Since we use a monorepo approach (as defined in ADR-010), all components of the system reside in a single repository.

A standardized directory structure ensures that developers, automated scripts, and CI/CD pipelines can predictably locate source code, documentation, and configuration files.

docs.title: High-Level Repository Layout
docs.text:
The root of the halal-queue repository is organized into distinct top-level directories, separating different architectural concerns.

halal-queue/
│
├── apps/                # Applications (e.g., frontend, backend)
├── packages/            # Reusable packages and shared libraries
├── docs/                # Comprehensive engineering and business documentation (MkDocs)
├── openapi/             # API specifications and guidelines
├── docker/              # Container definitions and docker-compose configurations
├── infrastructure/      # Deployment and infrastructure-as-code
├── scripts/             # Automation, deployment, and utility scripts
├── tests/               # E2E and cross-module integration tests
├── tools/               # Internal development tools and CLI utilities
├── .github/             # GitHub actions, workflows, and issue templates
├── mkdocs.yml           # MkDocs site configuration
└── README.md            # Primary entry point for the repository

docs.title: 1. apps/
docs.text: Contains the source code for the executable applications: NestJS backend, React Native (Expo) mobile applications (Customer App, Vendor App), and React + Vite Admin Web Portal. * Rule: Applications should focus on assembly and wiring. Shared logic should be extracted to packages/.

docs.title: 2. packages/
docs.text: Contains reusable code, libraries, and modules that can be shared across multiple applications. * Rule: Packages must be independent and not rely on specific applications.

docs.title: 3. docs/
docs.text: The single source of truth for project knowledge. It contains business rules, system design, software architecture, and engineering governance. * Rule: This directory is rendered as a static site via MkDocs. All files must be in Markdown.

docs.title: 4. openapi/
docs.text: Contains OpenAPI specifications and API guidelines that define the contract for communication between services and applications.

docs.title: 5. docker/
docs.text: Contains container definitions. Rather than scattering Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml files throughout the repository, centralizing them here allows the DevOps team to easily manage the infrastructure-as-code required to spin up the entire system locally or in production.

docs.title: 6. infrastructure/
docs.text: Contains everything related to deployment, cloud provisioning, and infrastructure configuration.

docs.title: 7. scripts/
docs.text: Contains utility scripts used by developers or CI/CD pipelines. Scripts here should be well-documented and idempotent.

docs.title: 8. tests/
docs.text: Contains repository-level tests, such as cross-module E2E tests.

docs.title: 9. tools/
docs.text: Internal development tools and utilities used for repository maintenance and code generation.

docs.title: 10. .github/
docs.text: Contains all GitHub-specific configurations, including CI/CD workflow definitions, pull request templates, and issue templates. No business logic or application code should reside here.

docs.title: Rules for Adding New Directories
docs.text: To maintain an organized repository: 1. Do not create new top-level directories unless absolutely necessary and approved via an Architecture Decision Record (ADR). 2. Use existing directories for their designated purpose. 3. If introducing a new application (e.g., an Admin Web Portal), it must be placed inside the frontend/ directory (e.g., frontend/admin-web/).

docs.text:
• ADR-010: Monorepo Strategy

  • 03-clean-architecture.md (For layer responsibilities)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document outlines the internal directory and package structure of the NestJS Backend (/backend/). It ensures the modular monolith follows clear, consistent boundaries, separating business domains cleanly so they could be extracted into microservices in the future.

docs.title: High-Level Backend Structure
docs.text:
The backend/ directory is primarily divided into apps/ (if deploying multiple entry points) and libs/ or modules/ for shared domains. We follow a standard NestJS monorepo-style structure.

backend/
│
├── src/
│   ├── config/              # Global application configuration
│   ├── common/              # Shared utilities, decorators, filters
│   ├── modules/             # Business domain modules (The core!)
│   └── main.ts              # Application entry point
│
├── test/                    # e2e tests
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json

docs.title: The Modules Directory
docs.text:
The application is a Modular Monolith. Every business domain (e.g., Catalog, Orders, Users) is an isolated module inside src/modules/.

src/modules/
│
├── catalog/                 # Product and Vendor Listing management
├── orders/                  # Order processing and lifecycle
├── users/                   # Customer and Vendor identities
├── notifications/           # FCM delivery
└── payment/                 # Payment gateways

docs.title: Internal Module Structure (Clean Architecture)
docs.text:
Each domain module strictly adheres to Clean Architecture principles. Inside src/modules/catalog/, you will find:

catalog/
│
├── application/             # Use Cases, CQRS Commands/Queries
│   ├── commands/
│   ├── queries/
│   └── dto/
│
├── domain/                  # Entities, Value Objects, Domain Exceptions
│   ├── entities/
│   ├── events/
│   └── repositories/        # Repository Interfaces (Ports)
│
├── infrastructure/          # Database adapters, External API integrations
│   ├── persistence/         # Prisma implementations of domain repositories
│   └── external/
│
├── presentation/            # REST Controllers, GraphQL Resolvers
│   ├── controllers/
│   └── view-models/
│
└── catalog.module.ts        # NestJS Module definition

docs.title: Dependency Rules
docs.text: To maintain the modular monolith: 1. No Cross-Infrastructure Dependencies: The orders module cannot directly query the catalog module's database tables. It must use the public Application or Domain services exposed by catalog. 2. Strict Clean Architecture Direction: infrastructure and presentation can depend on application. application can depend on domain. domain can depend on nothing.
